children.title: Fixed-Point Displacements
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point displacement forms used as residual certificates.

notation.meaning: fixed-point displacement of T at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-valued displacement certificate for a single-valued fixed-point mapping.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Fixed-point theorems and contraction p. 16

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(x\in H\), the fixed-point displacement vector and its scalar residual are defined by \[d_T(x):=x-Tx,\qquad r_T(x):=\lVert d_T(x)\rVert.\] They satisfy \[r_T(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_T(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Tx=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{Fix}T.\] Thus the displacement is an exact zero certificate for the fixed-point equation, independently of any nonexpansiveness assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement is the difference between a point and its image. Its norm vanishes exactly at fixed points.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Displacements

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1.3 Fixed-point theorems and contraction p. 16

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative displacement certificate for contractions; Picard convergence is excluded as algorithmic content.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T\) is a contraction with modulus \(q<1\), it has a unique fixed point \(x^*\), and for every \(x\in H\), \[\|x-x^*\|\le\frac{1}{1-q}\|x-Tx\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a contraction, displacement controls distance to the unique fixed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Contraction Displacement Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Exactness Does Not Imply a Linear Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of metric certification for an unrestricted fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x)=x-x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\) and \(d_T(x)=x^2\). Consequently, \[\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}T)}{|d_T(x)|}=\frac1{|x|}\to\infty\quad(x\to0,\ x\ne0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact displacement can decay too rapidly to bound distance to the fixed-point set linearly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local constant \(C\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}T)\le C\|d_T(x)\|\) near zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Exactness Does Not Imply a Linear Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Displacement Regularity for Nonexpansive and Averaged Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity of the displacement under standard fixed-point mapping classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T\) is nonexpansive, then \(d_T=I-T\) is \(2\)-Lipschitz and \(1/2\)-cocoercive. More generally, if \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), then \[\langle d_Tx-d_Ty,x-y\rangle\ge\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|d_Tx-d_Ty\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Displacements of nonexpansive maps are cocoercive, with an improved constant for averaged maps.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive, or more specifically \(\alpha\)-averaged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I-T\) is \(1/2\)-cocoercive in the nonexpansive case and \(1/(2\alpha)\)-cocoercive in the \(\alpha\)-averaged case.
knowledge_statements.title: Displacement Regularity for Nonexpansive and Averaged Maps

children.title: Resolvent Displacements
children.top_down_role: Resolvent displacement forms for proximal or monotone-operator settings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance certification induced by strong monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(A\) is maximally \(m\)-strongly monotone with \(m>0\), and let \(x^*\) be its unique zero. For \(y=J_{\lambda A}x\) and \(a=A_\lambda x=(x-y)/\lambda\in A(y)\), \[\|y-x^*\|\le\frac1m\|a\|,\qquad \|x-x^*\|\le\left(\lambda+\frac1m\right)\|a\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity converts the scaled resolvent displacement into distance bounds at both the resolvent point and input point.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Monotone Residual Error Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-operator analogue of Moreau decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximal monotone \(A\) and \(\lambda>0\), \[J_{\lambda A}(x)+\lambda J_{A^{-1}/\lambda}(x/\lambda)=x.\] Hence \[I-J_{\lambda A}=\lambda J_{A^{-1}/\lambda}\circ(\lambda^{-1}I).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolvent displacement is the scaled resolvent of the inverse relation at the scaled input.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core regularity of maximal-monotone resolvent displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_{\lambda A}=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}\), \(d=I-J_{\lambda A}\), and \(A_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}d\). Then both \(J_{\lambda A}\) and \(d\) are firmly nonexpansive. Consequently, \(A_\lambda\) is monotone, \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz, and \(\lambda\)-cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolvent displacement is firmly nonexpansive, and its scaled form is the Lipschitz, cocoercive Yosida approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I-J_{\lambda A}\) is firmly nonexpansive and \(A_\lambda\) is \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz and \(\lambda\)-cocoercive.
knowledge_statements.title: Firm Nonexpansiveness and Yosida Regularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximality Is Needed for an Everywhere-Defined Displacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global resolvent displacement for a nonmaximal monotone relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{gph}A=\{(0,0)\}\subset\mathbb R^2\). Then \(A\) is monotone but not maximal monotone, and for every \(\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname{dom}(I+\lambda A)^{-1}=\{0\}.\] Thus neither \(J_{\lambda A}\) nor \(I-J_{\lambda A}\) is an everywhere-defined residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity without maximality does not ensure that the resolvent displacement is defined on the whole space.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximality Is Needed for an Everywhere-Defined Displacement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise comparison of Yosida residuals at different resolvent parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\lambda\le\mu\), define \(A_\tau=\tau^{-1}(I-J_{\tau A})\) and \(d_{\tau A}=I-J_{\tau A}\). Then for every \(x\in H\), \[\|A_\mu x\|\le \|A_\lambda x\|\le\frac{\mu}{\lambda}\|A_\mu x\|,\qquad \frac{\lambda}{\mu}\|d_{\mu A}(x)\|\le\|d_{\lambda A}(x)\|\le\|d_{\mu A}(x)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the resolvent parameter decreases the scaled Yosida residual and increases the unscaled displacement, up to the parameter-ratio bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|A_\mu x\|\le\|A_\lambda x\|\le(\mu/\lambda)\|A_\mu x\|\) and \((\lambda/\mu)\|d_{\mu A}(x)\|\le\|d_{\lambda A}(x)\|\le\|d_{\mu A}(x)\|\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize Ordering of Resolvent Displacements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative resolvent regularity under strong monotonicity; iteration convergence is excluded as algorithm-level material.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally \(m\)-strongly monotone with \(m>0\), then for every \(\lambda>0\), \[\|J_{\lambda A}x-J_{\lambda A}z\|\le \frac{1}{1+\lambda m}\|x-z\|\qquad(x,z\in H).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity makes the resolvent a strict contraction with factor one divided by one plus the parameter times the modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Monotonicity Contraction of the Resolvent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between graph vectors of the operator and its scaled resolvent displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, \(\lambda>0\), and \(A_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}(I-J_{\lambda A})\). For every \(x,a\in H\), \[a=A_\lambda x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\in A(x-\lambda a).\] Equivalently, \[\operatorname{gph}A_\lambda=\{(y+\lambda a,a):(y,a)\in\operatorname{gph}A\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Yosida residual at an input is exactly an operator graph vector at the corresponding resolvent point.
knowledge_statements.title: Yosida Graph Parametrization

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda a_x\) for some \(a_x\in A(J_{\lambda A}x)\), and \(d_{\lambda A}(x)=0\iff 0\in A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal-monotone resolvent displacement and its induced inclusion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The resolvent \(J_{\lambda A}\) is everywhere defined and single-valued. For every \(x\in H\), let \(y=J_{\lambda A}x\). The resolvent identity gives \[x-y\in\lambda A(y),\qquad R_{\lambda A}(x)=\frac{x-y}{\lambda}\in A(y).\] Consequently, \[d_{\lambda A}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=J_{\lambda A}x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in A(x).\] Hence either \(d_{\lambda A}(x)\) or \(R_{\lambda A}(x)\) is an exact residual for the monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resolvent displacement is a scaled operator value at the resolvent point and vanishes exactly at zeros of the operator.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Displacements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resolvent identities and exact zero certificate are mathematically standard and the representation kind fits, but no inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Displacement Representation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing conversion or comparison between the two displacement families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence for relaxed fixed-point maps generated by a resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=J_{\lambda A}\) and \(T_\theta=(1-\theta)I+\theta J\). Then \[I-T_\theta=\theta(I-J).\] Hence, if \(\theta\ne0\), \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\theta=\operatorname{Fix}J=\operatorname{zer}A\) and \(\|x-T_\theta x\|=|\theta|\|x-Jx\|\). For \(\theta=0\), the displacement vanishes identically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero relaxation scales resolvent displacement without changing its zeros; zero relaxation destroys the certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{T_\theta}=\theta d_{J_{\lambda A}}\), with identical zeros when \(\theta\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Resolvent Displacement Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrelaxed correspondence among fixed-point displacement, resolvent displacement, and the Yosida residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space, \(\lambda>0\), \(J_{\lambda A}=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}\), and \(T=J_{\lambda A}\). Then \[d_T(x):=x-Tx=x-J_{\lambda A}x=:d_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda A_\lambda(x),\] where \(A_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}(I-J_{\lambda A})\). If \(y=J_{\lambda A}x\), then \(A_\lambda(x)=(x-y)/\lambda\in A(y)\), and \[d_T(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow A_\lambda(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow x\in\operatorname{zer}A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a resolvent mapping, fixed-point displacement, resolvent displacement, and the scaled Yosida residual coincide up to the factor lambda and have the same zero set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_T=d_{\lambda A}=\lambda A_\lambda\), \(A_\lambda(x)\in A(J_{\lambda A}x)\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}J_{\lambda A}=\operatorname{zer}A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point–Resolvent Displacement Identity

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_T(x)=d_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda R_{\lambda A}(x)\) for every \(x\in H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence when the fixed-point map is a maximal-monotone resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in H\), the fixed-point and resolvent representations coincide according to \[d_T(x)=x-Tx=x-J_{\lambda A}x=d_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda R_{\lambda A}(x).\] Moreover, if \(y=Tx\), then \[R_{\lambda A}(x)=\frac{x-y}{\lambda}\in A(y).\] Therefore \[d_T(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_{\lambda A}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in A(x),\] so the two displacement conventions encode the same certificate, differing only by the scale \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a resolvent fixed-point map, fixed-point displacement, resolvent displacement, and scaled inclusion residual are identical up to the stepsize.
knowledge_statements.title: Displacement Representation Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated correspondence is internally consistent and appropriate as a representation, but the maximal-monotone resolvent identities have no cited evidence or locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Firm Nonexpansiveness and Cocoercivity of Resolvent Displacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A property of resolvent displacement rather than the correspondence between displacement conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be maximal monotone, \(J=J_{\lambda A}\), \(d=I-J\), and \(A_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}d\). Then \[\|d(x)-d(y)\|^2\le\langle d(x)-d(y),x-y\rangle,\] and equivalently \[\langle A_\lambda x-A_\lambda y,x-y\rangle\ge\lambda\|A_\lambda x-A_\lambda y\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolvent displacement is firmly nonexpansive, and the scaled Yosida residual is cocoercive.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I-J_{\lambda A}\text{ is firmly nonexpansive and }A_\lambda\text{ is }\lambda\text{-cocoercive}.

notation.meaning: Yosida approximation or scaled resolvent displacement

knowledge_statements.title: Firm Nonexpansiveness and Cocoercivity of Resolvent Displacement

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns exact and relaxed scaling correspondences between fixed-point and resolvent displacement conventions. Generic fixed-point displacement and resolvent-only properties remain in their respective siblings; accordingly, the proposed firm-nonexpansiveness record was deferred as misplaced. The foundational identity and common zero-set certificate remain missing.

children.title: Inclusion Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual representations tied to approximate satisfaction of operator inclusions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex operator values in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A(x)\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, then there is a unique vector \[v_x=P_{A(x)}(0)\in A(x)\] satisfying \(\|v_x\|=\operatorname{dist}(0,A(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex operator value has a unique minimum-norm residual vector.
assumptions_latex: \(A(x)\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a real Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the operator value A(x)

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm Inclusion Vector

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Values Are Necessary for the Zero Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise failure for a nonclosed operator value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(0)=(0,1]\subset\mathbb R\). Then \[\operatorname{dist}(0,A(0))=0\quad\text{but}\quad0\notin A(0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonclosed operator value can approach zero without containing zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Values Are Necessary for the Zero Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Graph Does Not Ensure Residual Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity boundary for pointwise inclusion residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(A(0)=\{0,1\}\) and \(A(x)=\{1\}\) for \(x\ne0\). Its graph is closed, but \[r_{\mathrm{inc}}(0)=0,\qquad r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)=1\quad(x\ne0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a closed graph can produce a discontinuous same-point inclusion residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}A\) is closed while \(r_{\mathrm{inc}}\) is discontinuous at zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Graph Does Not Ensure Residual Continuity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Closure Invariance of Inclusion Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance depends only on the closure of the operator value at the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}A\), \[\operatorname{dist}(0,A(x))=\operatorname{dist}(0,\overline{A(x)}).\] Consequently, a norm residual alone cannot distinguish membership in \(A(x)\) from membership in its closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing the operator value at a point does not change the inclusion residual there.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Closure Invariance of Inclusion Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Translation of a Nonzero Inclusion Target
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a generalized inclusion target to a zero-target residual without restating the deferred canonical zero certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a target \(w\in H\), define the translated relation \(B(x)=A(x)-w\). Whenever \(A(x)\ne\varnothing\), \[\operatorname{dist}(w,A(x))=\operatorname{dist}(0,B(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero-target inclusion residual reduces by translation to a zero-target distance residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Translation of a Nonzero Inclusion Target

assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) has nonempty values at the point considered.

notation.meaning: distance from a point to a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise residual for the generalized equation \(0\in A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}A\), the inclusion residual for \(0\in A(x)\) is \[r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=\operatorname{dist}(0,A(x))=\inf_{v\in A(x)}\lVert v\rVert.\] If \(A(x)\) is closed, then \[r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in A(x).\] When the infimum is attained, any \(v_x\in A(x)\) satisfying \(\lVert v_x\rVert=r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\) is a residual vector and the pair \((x,v_x)\) is a directly checkable inclusion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inclusion residual is the smallest norm of an operator value at the candidate point; for closed values, it vanishes exactly at a solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distance residual and the closed-value condition give the stated zero certificate, and definition is the correct kind. No authoritative set-valued-analysis source or specific locator is provided.

children.title: Graph Residuals
children.top_down_role: Distance or perturbation views based on operator graphs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-graph regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(H\) is finite-dimensional and \(\operatorname{gph}A\) is nonempty and closed, then for every \(x\) there exists \((y,v)\in\operatorname{gph}A\) such that \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)^2=\|x-y\|^2+\|v\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed finite-dimensional graph admits a nearest graph pair realizing the graph residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Attained Nearest-Graph Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Is Necessary for Exact Zero Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonclosed graph with zero graph distance but failed inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(A:\mathbb R\rightrightarrows\mathbb R\) by \(A(y)=\{y\}\) for \(y\ne0\) and \(A(0)=\{1\}\). Then \((0,0)\in\overline{\operatorname{gph}A}\setminus\operatorname{gph}A\), so \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(0)=0\quad\text{but}\quad0\notin A(0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonclosed graph, zero graph distance need not imply the original inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Is Necessary for Exact Zero Certification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Dependence on the Target Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric regularity of graph distance independent of operator regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty \(G=\operatorname{gph}A\subset H\times H\), the map \(z\mapsto\operatorname{dist}(z,G)\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz. In particular, \[|r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)-r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x')|\le\|x-x'\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph residual changes by at most the perturbation of the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Dependence on the Target Pair

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph Residual Is Invariant Under Graph Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure invariance of distance in the product Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty graph \(G=\operatorname{gph}A\subset H\times H\) and every \(x\in H\), \[\operatorname{dist}((x,0),G)=\operatorname{dist}((x,0),\overline G).\] Thus graph residuals measure distance to the graph closure and cannot distinguish a graph from its closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing an operator graph does not change any graph-residual value.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Residual Is Invariant Under Graph Closure

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)=0\iff (x,0)\in\overline{\operatorname{gph}A}\), and closedness replaces the closure by \(\operatorname{gph}A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space distance from the target pair \((x,0)\) to an operator graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in H\), the graph residual for the inclusion \(0\in A(x)\) is \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x):=\operatorname{dist}\bigl((x,0),\operatorname{gph}A\bigr)=\inf_{(y,v)\in\operatorname{gph}A}\sqrt{\lVert x-y\rVert^2+\lVert v\rVert^2}.\] It satisfies \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (x,0)\in\overline{\operatorname{gph}A}.\] If \(\operatorname{gph}A\) is closed, this is equivalent to \(0\in A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graph residual measures the joint perturbation in point and operator value needed to reach the operator graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-space distance formula and closure-qualified zero characterization are coherent and fit the graph-residual leaf, but they are unsupported by a cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Inclusion-to-Graph Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural links between inclusion certificates plus graph-based certificates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality Criterion for Same-Point Graph Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality when a nearest graph certificate does not perturb the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume both residual infima are attained and a nearest graph pair has the form \((x,v_x)\) with \(v_x\in A(x)\). Then \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)=r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\] if and only if \(v_x\) is a minimum-norm element of \(A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residuals agree when a nearest graph pair keeps the candidate point fixed and uses a minimum-norm operator value.
assumptions_latex: The graph-distance and inclusion-distance infima are attained.
A nearest graph pair has first coordinate \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)=r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\) exactly when the second coordinate is minimum norm in \(A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Criterion for Same-Point Graph Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Reverse Conversion Without Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed finite graphs with arbitrarily large inclusion-to-graph residual ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(\operatorname{dom}A_\varepsilon=\{0,\varepsilon\}\), \(A_\varepsilon(0)=\{1\}\), and \(A_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=\{0\}\). Its graph is closed, and at \(x=0\), \[r_{\mathrm{inc}}(0)=1,\qquad r_{\mathrm{gra}}(0)\le\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearby exact graph zero can make graph residual tiny while the same-point inclusion residual remains large.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No operator-independent constant \(C\) satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{inc}}\le C r_{\mathrm{gra}}\) for all such operators.
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Reverse Conversion Without Regularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse Conversion Under a Local Value Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient regularity condition converting nearby graph certificates to a same-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose graph pairs approaching \((x,0)\) satisfy \[r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\le\kappa\|x-y\|+\|v\|\qquad((y,v)\in\operatorname{gph}A)\] for some \(\kappa\ge0\), and the graph residual is approximable by such pairs. Then \[r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\le\sqrt{\kappa^2+1}\,r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error-transfer condition supplies an explicit reverse bound from graph residual to inclusion residual.
assumptions_latex: The displayed local value error bound holds for graph pairs approaching \((x,0)\).
The graph residual is approximable by those local pairs.
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Conversion Under a Local Value Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph Residual as a Spatial Infimum of Inclusion Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variational conversion between nearby-point graph distance and same-point inclusion distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adopt \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\varnothing)=+\infty\). For every \(x\in H\), \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)^2=\inf_{y\in H}\bigl\{\|x-y\|^2+r_{\mathrm{inc}}(y)^2\bigr\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph distance is the lower envelope combining movement to a nearby point with the inclusion residual at that point.

notation.meaning: distance from (x,0) to the graph of A

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Residual as a Spatial Infimum of Inclusion Residuals

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)\le r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\), while every approximate graph minimizer supplies a nearby perturbed inclusion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion between same-point inclusion errors and nearby-point graph certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Restricting the graph-distance infimum to pairs \((x,v)\) with \(v\in A(x)\) yields \[r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)\le r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x).\] Conversely, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \((y,v)\in\operatorname{gph}A\) such that \[\sqrt{\lVert x-y\rVert^2+\lVert v\rVert^2}\le r_{\mathrm{gra}}(x)+\varepsilon.\] Thus a graph residual of size \(\delta\) converts into a perturbed inclusion \(v\in A(y)\) with both \(\lVert x-y\rVert\le\delta+\varepsilon\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le\delta+\varepsilon\); no converse same-point bound follows without regularity of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion residual bounds the graph residual, while a small graph residual yields a nearby point with a small inclusion vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-to-Graph Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided inequality and approximate graph-certificate conversion are mathematically plausible and appropriately classified as a representation, but no supporting source is cited.

children.title: Model-Step Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates derived from the size or geometry of a model step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Stability of the Model-Step Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of the proximal-gradient residual when the smooth gradient is Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(G_\alpha(x):=\alpha^{-1}(x-T_\alpha(x))\), where \(T_\alpha(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g}(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))\). If \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, then \[\|G_\alpha(x)-G_\alpha(z)\|\le\left(\frac{2}{\alpha}+L\right)\|x-z\|.\] Hence \(r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)=\|G_\alpha(x)\|\) is Lipschitz with the same bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a Lipschitz-gradient assumption, the vector model-step residual and its norm are globally Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable with an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.

notation.meaning: norm of the vector model-step residual

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Stability of the Model-Step Residual

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) is Fréchet differentiable and \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\alpha>0\) and the quadratic model has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled step residual generated by the standard proximal quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), define \[m_x(y):=f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\lVert y-x\rVert^2+g(y),\qquad T_\alpha(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in H}m_x(y).\] The model-step residual is \[r_{\mathrm{step}}(x):=\frac{1}{\alpha}\lVert x-T_\alpha(x)\rVert.\] Since the model is strongly convex, its minimizer is unique and \[r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T_\alpha(x)=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model-step residual is the proximal-model step length divided by the stepsize and vanishes exactly at composite stationary points.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Step Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal-model step residual and its stationary-point zero set are standard and fit a definition leaf, but the record supplies no authoritative proximal-model citation or locator.

children.title: Model-Decrement Residuals
children.top_down_role: Certificates based on predicted model improvement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Model Decrement Need Not Imply Actual Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes predicted model improvement from objective decrease without a majorization or stepsize condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac L2x^2\), \(g\equiv0\), \(L>0\), and use the quadratic linearization model with \(\alpha L>2\). For \(x\ne0\), \(T_\alpha(x)=(1-\alpha L)x\) and \(\Delta_\alpha(x)=\tfrac{\alpha L^2}{2}x^2>0\), whereas \[f(T_\alpha(x))-f(x)=\frac L2\big((1-\alpha L)^2-1\big)x^2>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive predicted model decrement can coexist with an increase in the true objective when the stepsize is too large.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic linearization model uses \(\alpha L>2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Model Decrement Need Not Imply Actual Descent

assumptions_latex: \(m_x\) and \(T_\alpha(x)\) are the quadratic model and minimizer defined for the composite objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-root normalization of the predicted decrease in a proximal quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The predicted model decrement and its residual normalization are \[\Delta_\alpha(x):=m_x(x)-m_x(T_\alpha(x)),\qquad r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x):=\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta_\alpha(x)}{\alpha}}.\] Strong convexity of \(m_x\) implies \(\Delta_\alpha(x)\ge0\). Moreover, \[r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Delta_\alpha(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=T_\alpha(x),\] so the decrement residual and the model-step residual have the same zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decrement residual is the normalized square root of predicted model decrease and has the same zeros as the model step.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Decrement Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decrement construction is coherent, but its assumptions refer to an externally defined composite objective without explicitly restating the ambient space, functions, and positive stepsize. An authoritative source and complete local hypotheses are required.

children.title: Step-to-Decrement Calibration
children.top_down_role: Regimes supporting comparison between step size plus model decrement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse Calibration Fails for a Nonsmooth Proximal Term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a uniform decrement-by-step bound under convexity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\), \(g(u)=|u|\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(0<x<\alpha\). Then \(T_\alpha(x)=0\) and \[r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)=\frac{x}{\alpha},\qquad r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x)=\sqrt{\frac{2x}{\alpha}-\frac{x^2}{\alpha^2}},\qquad \frac{r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x)}{r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)}=\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha}{x}-1}.\] The ratio tends to \(+\infty\) as \(x\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the absolute-value proximal term, the decrement-to-step residual ratio is unbounded near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x)/r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)\to+\infty\) as \(x\downarrow0\), so no finite local reverse-calibration constant exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Calibration Fails for a Nonsmooth Proximal Term

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Sided Calibration for a Smooth Proximal Term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse step-to-decrement comparison when the convex proximal term has a Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the quadratic composite model, suppose \(g\) is differentiable and \(\nabla g\) is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz. With \(d=T_\alpha(x)-x\), \[\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|d\|^2\le\Delta_\alpha(x)\le\left(\frac{1}{2\alpha}+\frac{\beta}{2}\right)\|d\|^2.\] Equivalently, \[r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)\le r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x)\le\sqrt{1+\alpha\beta}\,r_{\mathrm{step}}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz gradient for the proximal term makes the step and decrement residuals two-sided equivalent.
assumptions_latex: The standard quadratic composite model is used with \(\alpha>0\).
\(g\) is convex and differentiable with a \(\beta\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Calibration for a Smooth Proximal Term

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided calibration induced by strong convexity of the proximal quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(m_x\) is \(\alpha^{-1}\)-strongly convex and \(T_\alpha(x)\) is its minimizer, \[m_x(x)-m_x(T_\alpha(x))\ge\frac{1}{2\alpha}\lVert x-T_\alpha(x)\rVert^2.\] Equivalently, \[\Delta_\alpha(x)\ge\frac{\alpha}{2}r_{\mathrm{step}}(x)^2,\qquad r_{\mathrm{dec}}(x)\ge r_{\mathrm{step}}(x).\] Therefore a small decrement residual guarantees a small step residual. A reverse inequality requires additional structure and is not implied by convexity of \(g\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity calibrates predicted decrease against step length: the normalized decrement dominates the scaled model-step residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Step-to-Decrement Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided calibration follows from the stated strong-convexity structure and property is the correct role, but the ambient space and domains of several symbols are not explicitly introduced and no source is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Primal-Dual Residuals Need Not Give a Distance Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual-to-solution distance control without metric-subregularity or growth assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(Y=\{0\}\), \(K=0\), \(f(x)=x^4\), \(g(0)=0\), and \(\tau>0\). If \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x)\), then \(x=z+4\tau z^3\) and \(r_{\mathrm p}(x)=4|z|^3\). Consequently, \(r_{\mathrm p}^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), but \(|x|/r_{\mathrm p}(x)\to+\infty\) as \(x\to0\). Thus no \(c,\varepsilon>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\{0\})\le c r_{\mathrm p}(x)\) for all \(|x|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quartic convex objective shows that exact residual vanishing alone does not make residual magnitude control distance to the primal-dual solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm p}^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), while every local bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\{0\})\le c r_{\mathrm p}(x)\) fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Primal-Dual Residuals Need Not Give a Distance Error Bound

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal fixed-point certificate for Fenchel primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal objective \(f(x)+g(Kx)\), define \[r_{\mathrm p}(x,y):=\frac{1}{\tau}\left\lVert x-\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x-\tau K^*y)\right\rVert,\] \[r_{\mathrm d}(x,y):=\frac{1}{\sigma}\left\lVert y-\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y+\sigma Kx)\right\rVert.\] Then \[(r_{\mathrm p}(x,y),r_{\mathrm d}(x,y))=(0,0)\] holds exactly when \[-K^*y\in\partial f(x),\qquad Kx\in\partial g^*(y),\] which are the primal-dual optimality inclusions. Thus the pair is an exact, directly evaluable certificate of a primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two proximal fixed-point residuals jointly vanish exactly when the Fenchel primal-dual optimality inclusions hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Residual Pairs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two proximal residuals encode the displayed Fenchel optimality inclusions, and certificate fits this terminal container. The nontrivial primal-dual characterization lacks an authoritative citation and locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Moreau envelope and its gradient-residual representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Moreau envelope and proximal mapping are \[e_\lambda h(x):=\inf_{y\in H}\left\{h(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\},\qquad p:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda h}(x).\] The minimizer \(p\) is unique, and \[e_\lambda h(x)=h(p)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert p-x\rVert^2.\] Moreover, \(e_\lambda h\) is Fréchet differentiable with \[\nabla e_\lambda h(x)=\frac{x-p}{\lambda}=R_\lambda(x).\] Hence the envelope gradient is precisely the scaled proximal displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moreau envelope smooths a closed convex function, and its gradient equals the scaled displacement to the proximal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Moreau–Yosida Envelopes

source_witnesses.locator: G. Moreau Envelopes p. 20

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of proximal uniqueness and envelope differentiability outside the convex regime.

Thus \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda h}(0)=\{-1,1\}\), and the left and right derivatives of \(e_\lambda h\) at zero are \(1/\lambda\) and \(-1/\lambda\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex two-point indicator has a multivalued proximal map and a nondifferentiable Moreau envelope at the midpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda h}(0)=\{-1,1\}\) and \(e_\lambda h\) is not differentiable at zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Smoothness Without Convexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual decomposition for convex proximal mappings and envelopes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_\mu h\le e_\lambda h\le h\) and \(e_\lambda h(x)\uparrow h(x)\) as \(\lambda\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(q_\lambda(x)=\|x\|^2/(2\lambda)\), \[e_\lambda h=h\mathbin{\square}q_\lambda=\left(h^*+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\cdot\|^2\right)^*.\]

assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Minimizers of the Forward-Backward Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-minimizer exactness in the convex smooth-plus-convex regime with an admissible forward step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, where \(f\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(0<\gamma<1/L\), let \(\varphi_\gamma\) be the forward-backward envelope and \(T_\gamma=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(I-\gamma\nabla f)\). Then \[\inf\varphi_\gamma=\inf F.\] Moreover, \[\operatorname*{argmin}\varphi_\gamma=\operatorname*{argmin}F=\operatorname{Fix}T_\gamma,\] with all three sets simultaneously empty when the common infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the convex composite regime with a sub-reciprocal-Lipschitz step, the forward-backward envelope and original objective have the same minimum value and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and continuously differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Minimizers of the Forward-Backward Envelope

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard forward-backward envelope representation for a smooth-plus-convex composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the forward-backward envelope by \[\varphi_\gamma(x):=f(x)- rac{\gamma}{2}\lVert
abla f(x)Vert^2+g^\gamma igl(x-\gamma
abla f(x) igr).\] With \(T_\gamma(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma
abla f(x))\), the Moreau representation gives \[\varphi_\gamma(x)=f(x)+g(T_\gamma(x))+\langle
abla f(x),T_\gamma(x)-xangle+ rac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert T_\gamma(x)-xVert^2.\] Thus the envelope value equals the minimum value of the proximal quadratic model based at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forward-backward envelope is the proximal quadratic-model value, equivalently a Moreau envelope evaluated after a gradient step.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward-Backward Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two forward-backward-envelope formulas agree and representation is an appropriate content kind, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity equivalence under an exact composite subdifferential chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\partial(h\circ c)(x)=\nabla c(x)^*\partial h(c(x))\), then \[p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial(h\circ c)(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an exact chain rule, zero prox-linear displacement is equivalent to composite stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Stationarity Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity and Uniqueness of the Prox-Linear Model Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness under properness of the affine-composite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[M_x(y)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2.\] If the first term is proper, closed, and convex, then \(M_x\) is \(1/\lambda\)-strongly convex and coercive, and therefore has a unique minimizer \(p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed affine-composite model plus a positive quadratic has a unique prox-linear point.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity and Uniqueness of the Prox-Linear Model Point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz-outer and Lipschitz-Jacobian regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h\) is \(L_h\)-Lipschitz on the relevant segments and \(\nabla c\) is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz, then \[|h(c(y))-h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))|\le\frac{L_h\beta}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] For \(p=p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\), \[h(c(p))\le h(c(x))-\left(\frac{1}{2\lambda}-\frac{L_h\beta}{2}\right)\|p-x\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic model accuracy converts prox-linear model decrease into objective descent below the curvature threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is convex and \(L_h\)-Lipschitz on the relevant set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(p)\le F(x)-(1/(2\lambda)-L_h\beta/2)\|p-x\|^2\), so strict descent holds when \(\lambda L_h\beta<1\) and \(p\ne x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Model Accuracy and Descent Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of the prox-linear envelope value with the objective at its model point under quadratic model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\), \(d=p-x\), and suppose \[|F(p)-h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)d)|\le\frac{\kappa}{2}\|d\|^2.\] Then \[F(p)+\left(\frac1{2\lambda}-\frac\kappa2\right)\|d\|^2\le F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\le F(p)+\left(\frac1{2\lambda}+\frac\kappa2\right)\|d\|^2.\] Moreover, using \(y=x\) as a model competitor gives \(F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\le F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The prox-linear envelope lies below the current objective and differs from the objective at its model point by only the quadratic regularizer and model error.
assumptions_latex: The prox-linear model has the unique minimizer \(p\).
The displayed quadratic model-accuracy bound holds at \(p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Envelope–Objective Sandwich

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Prox-Linear Envelope Need Not Be Differentiable in Its Base Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unqualified base-point smoothness when the inner map is only continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(h(z)=z\), \(c(x)=x+\tfrac12x|x|\), and \(\lambda>0\). Then \(c\) is continuously differentiable with \(c'(x)=1+|x|\), and \[F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)=\min_d\left\{c(x)+c'(x)d+\frac{d^2}{2\lambda}\right\}=c(x)-\frac{\lambda}{2}(1+|x|)^2.\] Its right derivative at zero is \(1-\lambda\), whereas its left derivative is \(1+\lambda\). Thus the envelope is not differentiable at zero despite uniqueness of every model minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique prox-linear model point does not ensure differentiability of the envelope in its base point when the inner Jacobian is merely continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}\) has unequal left and right derivatives \(1+\lambda\) and \(1-\lambda\) at \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Prox-Linear Envelope Need Not Be Differentiable in Its Base Point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiability Formula under Smooth Outer and Inner Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-point sensitivity under smooth data and locally compact control of the unique model minimizer.

Fix \(\lambda>0\) and define \[E_\lambda(x)=\min_y\left\{h igl(c(x)+
abla c(x)(y-x) igr)+ rac1{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2ight\}.\] Suppose \(c\) is \(C^2\) near \( ar x\), and \(h\) is proper, closed, convex, and finite and \(C^1\) on an open set containing all relevant affine-model arguments. Suppose also that for every \(x\) near \( ar x\) the model has its unique minimizer \(p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\), and these minimizers lie in one compact set. Set \(p=p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}( ar x)\), \(d=p- ar x\), \(a=c( ar x)+
abla c( ar x)d\), and \(B_{ ar x,d}u=D^2c( ar x)[u,d]\). Then \(E_\lambda\) is differentiable at \( ar x\) and \[

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under twice-differentiable inner data, a smooth outer function, and local compactness of the unique model minimizers, the prox-linear envelope has an explicit gradient containing both a Hessian-contraction term and the scaled displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, convex, and finite and continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of the relevant affine-model arguments.
For every nearby base point the affine-composite model has its unique minimizer, and all such minimizers lie in a common compact set.

affine-model argument at the prox-linear point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Dual Representation of the Prox-Linear Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dual value formula and primal recovery for the quadratic affine-composite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\), set \(a=c(x)\) and \(J=\nabla c(x)\), and suppose \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\cap(a+\operatorname{range}J)\ne\varnothing\). Then, for \(\lambda>0\), \[F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)=\min_d\left\{h(a+Jd)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|d\|^2\right\}=\max_u\left\{\langle u,a\rangle-h^*(u)-\frac{\lambda}{2}\|J^*u\|^2\right\}.\] The dual maximum is attained. For every dual optimizer \(u^\star\), the unique primal displacement satisfies \(d^\star=-\lambda J^*u^\star\), and hence \(p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)=x-
\lambda J^*u^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, the prox-linear envelope equals a Fenchel dual maximum, and any dual optimizer recovers the unique model displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the outer convex function
dual optimizer of the affine-composite model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp descent coefficient obtained from convex optimality of the affine-composite model and quadratic model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_x(y)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))\), let \(p\) minimize \(q_x(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\lambda)\), and put \(d=p-x\). If \(q_x\) is proper, closed, and convex and \[F(p)\le q_x(p)+\frac{\kappa}{2}\|d\|^2,\qquad F(x)=q_x(x),\] then \[F(p)\le F(x)-\left(\frac1\lambda-\frac\kappa2\right)\|d\|^2.\] Consequently, every nonzero model step strictly decreases \(F\) whenever \(\lambda\kappa<2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex optimality gives a sharper prox-linear descent coefficient than comparison with the base point alone: nonzero steps decrease the objective when lambda times the model-error constant is below two.

notation.meaning: affine-composite model at the base point

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Model-Point Descent Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical coefficient-one-over-two-lambda affine-composite envelope convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=h\circ c\), where \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex and \(c\) is differentiable. For \(\lambda>0\), when \(y\mapsto h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))\) is proper, define \[F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)=\min_y\left\{h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+\frac1{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\}.\] The objective is strongly convex and has the unique minimizer \(p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\). Define \[R_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The prox-linear envelope is the value of a quadratically regularized affine-composite model; its unique minimizer and scaled displacement define the prox-linear point and residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\), \(p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\), and \(R_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\) are well-defined with the displayed convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Envelope, Point, and Residual

assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\), and the displayed model has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\) is the optimal value of the regularized affine-composite model, and \(P_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\) is its minimizer set.
review_flags: A precise source for this envelope convention is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the quadratic coefficient \(1/(2\lambda)\) and permits a set-valued prox-linear point mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the prox-linear envelope and point mapping by
\[
F_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x):=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x)\bigr)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\},
\]
\[
P_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x)\bigr)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
When the minimizer is unique, it is denoted by \(p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x)\), and the associated residual is \(R_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x):=\lambda^{-1}(x-p_\lambda^{\mathrm{pl}}(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The prox-linear envelope minimizes a quadratic-regularized affine model of the inner mapping; its displacement defines the prox-linear residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Prox-Linear Envelopes container, but no inspectable source supports the chosen quadratic parameterization or notation. Moreover, once the displayed convex model has a finite minimizer, its positive quadratic term makes that minimizer unique, so the set-valued/conditional-uniqueness wording needs reconciliation with the stated assumptions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the algebraic resolvent equivalence from assumptions ensuring a globally defined single-valued residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), \(\lambda>0\), and suppose \(p\in J_{\lambda A}(x):=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}(x)\). Then \((x-p)/\lambda\in A(p)\), regardless of monotonicity. Maximal monotonicity is a sufficient condition ensuring that \(J_{\lambda A}\) is everywhere defined and single-valued on a Hilbert space; without existence or uniqueness, the residual \(\lambda^{-1}(I-J_{\lambda A})\) may be undefined or set-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise inclusion identity needs only membership in the resolvent relation; maximal monotonicity is used to obtain a globally defined single-valued residual.
assumptions_latex: For the pointwise identity, \(p\in J_{\lambda A}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Assumptions for Resolvent Conversion

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.
review_flags: The supplied fixed-point locator is only indirect support for the resolvent identity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent form for maximal-monotone inclusions in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in H\), set \(p:=J_{\lambda A}x\). By the definition of the inverse relation,
\[
p=J_{\lambda A}x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in p+\lambda A(p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_\lambda(x):=\frac{x-p}{\lambda}\in A(p).
\]
Consequently,
\[
x=J_{\lambda A}x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_\lambda(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in A(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resolvent fixed point is exactly a zero of the underlying maximal monotone operator; the resolvent displacement supplies the inclusion vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point-to-Inclusion Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point/inclusion equivalence is mathematically standard and locally relevant, but the record has no citation with an inspectable locator. It is more naturally a conversion principle than a generic property, and the statement includes derivational proof text that should be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.
review_flags: A direct authoritative locator for the residual certificate is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts a resolvent residual at \(x\) into stationarity at the resolvent point \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The resolvent identity gives
\[
R_\lambda(x):=\frac{x-p}{\lambda}\in A(p).
\]
Therefore the computable pair \((p,R_\lambda(x))\) certifies
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,A(p))\leq \lVert R_\lambda(x)\rVert,
\qquad
\lVert x-p\rVert=\lambda\lVert R_\lambda(x)\rVert.
\]
In particular, \(\lVert R_\lambda(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) produces a point within distance \(\lambda\varepsilon\) of \(x\) whose stationarity defect is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small resolvent residual yields a nearby point with a proportionally small operator-stationarity defect.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Stationarity Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and its constants are correct for the stated resolvent convention and fit the terminal container, but no source is supplied. The displayed derivation also constitutes proof text and should be replaced by a direct certificate statement after sourcing.

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a real Hilbert space.
\(\lambda>0\), \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\), and \(f_\lambda\) is the Moreau envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The envelope gap identifies the nearby point \(p\) and its displacement: \(\lVert x-p\rVert=\lambda\lVert\nabla f_\lambda(x)\rVert\).
review_flags: A direct Moreau-envelope source locator is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Moreau-envelope conversion in the closed convex Hilbert-space setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
f_\lambda(x):=\min_{y\in H}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Then the unique minimizer \(p\) satisfies
\[
g:=\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\frac{x-p}{\lambda}\in\partial f(p),
\qquad
\lVert x-p\rVert=\lambda\lVert g\rVert,
\]
and the attained-value identity is
\[
f(p)=f_\lambda(x)-\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert g\rVert^2.
\]
Thus an envelope gradient bound \(\lVert g\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) explicitly identifies a nearby point \(p\) at distance at most \(\lambda\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moreau envelope gradient recovers a nearby proximal point, its exact distance from the base point, and its objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-to-Nearby-Point Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact Moreau-envelope identities fit the conversion container and the certificate content kind, but no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Distance Conversion under an Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract local conversion from residual size to distance from the residual zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:X\to Y\) be a mapping between normed spaces, let \(S=R^{-1}(0)\), and suppose that for a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\in S\) and \(\kappa\geq0\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\lVert R(x)\rVert\qquad(x\in U).\] Then every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(\lVert R(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) obeys \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\varepsilon\). The certificate is local and therefore requires verified membership in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound converts residual tolerance into solution-distance tolerance only inside its validity neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The displayed error bound holds on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local Distance Conversion under an Error Bound

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal and \(\mu\)-strongly monotone with \(\mu>0\).
review_flags: A direct source for this strong-monotonicity error bound is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global solution-distance conversion under strong monotonicity; weaker metric-subregular variants are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Strong monotonicity makes \(A^{-1}(0)\) the singleton \(\{x^\star\}\). Since \(R_\lambda(x)\in A(p)\) and \(0\in A(x^\star)\),
\[
\lVert p-x^\star\rVert\leq\frac{1}{\mu}\lVert R_\lambda(x)\rVert.
\]
Using \(x-p=\lambda R_\lambda(x)\) gives the computable error bound
\[
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,A^{-1}(0)\bigr)=\lVert x-x^\star\rVert
\leq\left(\lambda+\frac{1}{\mu}\right)\lVert R_\lambda(x)\rVert.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity converts the resolvent residual into a global upper bound on distance to the unique solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Solution-Distance Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound is mathematically valid under the stated strong-monotonicity assumptions, but it is an error-bound certificate rather than merely a generic property. It has no source, and the statement contains a derivation rather than only the knowledge statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fundamental Proximal Inequality and Objective Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex proximal point method with a nonempty minimizer set for the convergence conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x^k)\), where \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(z\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[2\lambda_k(f(x^{k+1})-f(z))\le \|x^k-z\|^2-\|x^{k+1}-z\|^2-\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\] Hence \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)\). If \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\), then \[f(x^N)-f(x^*)\le\frac{\|x^0-x^*\|^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\lambda_k}.\] If additionally \(\inf_k\lambda_k>0\), then \(x^k\) converges weakly to a minimizer; in finite dimensions it converges strongly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex proximal step satisfies the fundamental three-point inequality, an accumulated-step objective rate, and weak iterate convergence when step sizes stay positive.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
A minimizer exists for the rate and convergence conclusions.
knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental Proximal Inequality and Objective Rate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-convergence specialization of convex proximal minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\), it has at most one minimizer \(x^*\), and whenever that minimizer exists, \[\|x^{k+1}-x^*\|\le\frac{1}{1+\lambda_k\mu}\|x^k-x^*\|.\] Consequently, \[\|x^N-x^*\|\le\prod_{k=0}^{N-1}(1+\lambda_k\mu)^{-1}\|x^0-x^*\|.\] If \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\), convergence is Q-linear with factor at most \((1+\underline\lambda\mu)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity makes the proximal map contractive and yields global linear convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Proximal Contraction

assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a real Hilbert space.
\(\lambda_k>0\), and each proximal subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(r^{k+1}:=\lambda_k^{-1}(x^k-x^{k+1})\in\partial f(x^{k+1})\), and fixed points are minimizers of \(f\).
review_flags: The supplied proximal-gradient locator does not directly certify the proximal point method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal point method for unconstrained closed convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in H\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\) compute
\[
x^{k+1}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in H}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert y-x^k\rVert^2\right\}
=\bigl(I+\lambda_k\partial f\bigr)^{-1}x^k.
\]
The subproblem optimality condition is
\[
r^{k+1}:=\frac{x^k-x^{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\in\partial f(x^{k+1}).
\]
Stop when a prescribed residual criterion such as \(\lVert r^{k+1}\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) holds; output \(x^{k+1}\) with its stationarity certificate \(r^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each convex proximal point step exactly minimizes a quadratic regularization and returns a subgradient residual at the new iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Minimization Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly specializes the proximal point method to closed convex minimization and fits this regime container. The inventory's proximal-gradient locator is not evidence for this record, and the candidate itself contains no source reference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal-monotone PPA under positive strong monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) is maximal and \(\mu\)-strongly monotone with \(\mu>0\), then it has at most one zero \(x^*\), and \[\|J_{\lambda_kA}x-J_{\lambda_kA}y\|\le\frac{1}{1+\lambda_k\mu}\|x-y\|.\] Whenever a zero exists, \[\|x^{k+1}-x^*\|\le(1+\lambda_k\mu)^{-1}\|x^k-x^*\|.\] Thus \(\inf_k\lambda_k>0\) gives global Q-linear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity makes the resolvent contractive and gives linear convergence to the unique zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Monotonicity Linear Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal-Monotone Proximal Point Convergence and Residual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact PPA for a maximal monotone operator with a nonempty zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=A^{-1}(0)\ne\varnothing\) and \(x^{k+1}=J_{\lambda_kA}x^k\). For every \(z\in S\), \[\|x^{k+1}-z\|^2+\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le\|x^k-z\|^2.\] If \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\), then \(x^k\) converges weakly to a point of \(S\), strongly in finite dimensions, and for \(r^{k+1}=(x^k-x^{k+1})/\lambda_k\), \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|r^{k+1}\|\le\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x^0,S)}{\underline\lambda\sqrt N}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact maximal-monotone PPA is Fejér monotone, converges weakly to a zero, and has an inverse-square-root best certified-residual bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal-Monotone Proximal Point Convergence and Residual Bound

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iterate is uniquely defined by \(x^{k+1}=J_{\lambda_k A}x^k\) and yields \(r^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1})\).
review_flags: A direct maximal-monotone proximal point source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal point iteration for finding a zero of a maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Starting from \(x^0\in H\), define
\[
x^{k+1}:=J_{\lambda_k A}x^k=\bigl(I+\lambda_k A\bigr)^{-1}x^k,
\qquad
r^{k+1}:=\frac{x^k-x^{k+1}}{\lambda_k}.
\]
Maximal monotonicity makes the resolvent single-valued and everywhere defined, while the resolvent identity gives
\[
r^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1}).
\]
Given a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), stop when \(\lVert r^{k+1}\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) and output the certified pair \((x^{k+1},r^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximal-monotone proximal point method applies the resolvent and obtains an explicit inclusion residual at every iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximal-Monotone Inclusion Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resolvent iteration, well-posedness assertion, and inclusion residual are standard and fit the algorithmic regime, but no authoritative maximal-monotone proximal point locator is cited.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex for some \(\rho\geq 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the proximal point \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) is unique, the Moreau envelope \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\in\partial f(p)\).
review_flags: The cited locator should be checked against the finite-dimensional domain and subdifferential convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional weakly convex Moreau-envelope regime under the unambiguous threshold condition \(\lambda\rho<1\).

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[
f_\lambda(x):=\min_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\},
\qquad
p:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x).
\]
The minimizer \(p\) is unique, and \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable with
\[
\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\frac{x-p}{\lambda}\in\partial f(p),
\qquad
\lVert x-p\rVert=\lambda\lVert\nabla f_\lambda(x)\rVert.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional weakly convex function and a parameter below the weak-convexity threshold, the proximal point is unique and the Moreau envelope gradient equals the scaled proximal displacement, which is a limiting subgradient at the proximal point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent, Residual Complexity, and Stationary Cluster Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean proximal-point iteration for a lower-bounded weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x^k)\), \(g^{k+1}=(x^k-x^{k+1})/\lambda_k\), and \(0<\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_k\leq\overline\lambda<1/\rho\). Then
\[
g^{k+1}\in\partial f(x^{k+1}),\qquad
f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1})\geq\lambda_k\left(1-\frac{\rho\lambda_k}{2}\right)\|g^{k+1}\|^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\min_{0\leq k<N}\|g^{k+1}\|^2\leq
\frac{f(x^0)-\inf f}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\lambda_k(1-\rho\lambda_k/2)},
\]
and \(g^{k+1}\to0\). Any cluster subsequence satisfying \(f(x^{k_j+1})\to f(\bar x)\) has \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact weakly convex proximal steps decrease the objective, yield an explicit subgradient and a best-iterate residual bound, and have stationary compatible cluster points.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and bounded below.
\(\partial f\) is the limiting subdifferential; cluster-point passage uses the displayed function-value compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The descent and best-iterate bounds hold, \(g^{k+1}\to0\), and every qualifying cluster point is limiting-stationary.
review_flags: The builder's descent estimate was valid but nonsharp; strong convexity gives the displayed coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent, Residual Complexity, and Stationary Cluster Points

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Convexity and Proximal Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining curvature condition for the weakly convex proximal-point regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper function \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex when \(f+(\rho/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex. For \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\),
\[
y\mapsto f(y)+\frac1{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2
\]
is \((\lambda^{-1}-\rho)\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding curvature rho makes a weakly convex function convex; below the reciprocal threshold every proximal subproblem is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Convexity and Proximal Strong Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Reciprocal Curvature Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform proximal uniqueness and existence at or above the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\), \(\rho>0\), and center \(x=0\), the proximal objective is
\[
\frac12(\lambda^{-1}-\rho)y^2.
\]
At \(\lambda=1/\rho\) every \(y\) is a minimizer; for \(\lambda>1/\rho\) it is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict reciprocal-curvature threshold is sharp for uniform uniqueness and well-posedness.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\), \(f(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\), and the proximal center is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\lambda\rho=1\) uniqueness fails, and at \(\lambda\rho>1\) existence can fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Reciprocal Curvature Threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact PPA Residual Bound and Weak Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variable-step proximal point iterations for a maximal monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^{k+1}=J_{\lambda_kA}x^k\) and \(r^{k+1}=(x^k-x^{k+1})/\lambda_k\in A(x^{k+1})\). For every \(z\in A^{-1}(0)\) and \(N\geq1\),
\[
\min_{0\leq k<N}\|r^{k+1}\|^2\leq\frac{\|x^0-z\|^2}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\lambda_k^2}.
\]
If \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\lambda_k^2=\infty\), then \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\in A^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact proximal-point iterates have an inverse accumulated-squared-stepsize best-residual bound and converge weakly when the squared step sizes have divergent sum.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone, and \(A^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual bound holds; if \(\sum_k\lambda_k^2=\infty\), then \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\in A^{-1}(0)\).
review_flags: The divergent squared-step condition is sharper than the builder's sufficient lower-bound assumption.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact proximal step is Fejér monotone with respect to the zero set and decreases squared distance by at least the squared step length.
