knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Squared Step Length Can Prevent Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitation of unconditional exact-PPA convergence for variable step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2\) be the quarter-turn \(A(u_1,u_2)=(-u_2,u_1)\), so \(A\) is maximal monotone and \(A^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\). If \(\lambda_k>0\) and \(\sum_k\lambda_k<\infty\), then
\[
x^{k+1}=(I+\lambda_kA)^{-1}x^k
\]
converges from every \(x^0\neq0\) to a nonzero point. In particular, \(\sum_k\lambda_k^2<\infty\) supplies no universal convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With rapidly vanishing step sizes, an exact proximal iteration can converge to a non-solution even for a linear maximal monotone operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is the quarter-turn operator on \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact iterates converge to a point outside \(A^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Squared Step Length Can Prevent Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone, and \(x^0\in H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact update returns \(x^{k+1}\) with zero resolvent-equation error and residual \(r^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1})\).
review_flags: A source distinguishing exact and inexact proximal point variants is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact resolvent evaluation with iteration-dependent positive step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute the resolvent exactly:
\[
x^{k+1}:=\bigl(I+\lambda_k A\bigr)^{-1}x^k.
\]
Equivalently, find \(x^{k+1}\in H\) and \(r^{k+1}\in H\) satisfying
\[
r^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1}),
\qquad
x^k=x^{k+1}+\lambda_k r^{k+1}.
\]
Thus the resolvent-equation error is exactly zero. For a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), stop when \(\lVert r^{k+1}\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) and output \((x^{k+1},r^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact proximal point step solves the resolvent equation without error and directly returns a certified operator value.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal Point Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact resolvent algorithm and zero equation-error characterization fit the Exact Proximal Point Variants container, but no source distinguishes and supports this exact variant.

children.title: Inexact Proximal Point Variants
children.top_down_role: Variants allowing controlled proximal subproblem error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard inexact proximal-point variant distinct from additive resolvent-equation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
A^{[\varepsilon]}(y):=\{v:\langle v-a,y-u\rangle\geq-\varepsilon\ \text{for all }(u,a)\in\operatorname{gra}A\}.
\]
Choose \(y^k,v^k,\varepsilon_k\) satisfying
\[
v^k\in A^{[\varepsilon_k]}(y^k),\qquad
\|\lambda_kv^k+y^k-x^k\|^2+2\lambda_k\varepsilon_k\leq\sigma^2\|y^k-x^k\|^2,
\]
and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\lambda_kv^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid proximal–extragradient variant permits an enlarged graph value and controls its equation and enlargement errors by a relative test.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is an enlargement-based inexact proximal-point step satisfying the displayed relative-error test.
review_flags: This convention is inequivalent to the additive resolvent-equation convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Enlargement-Based Hybrid Proximal–Extragradient Step

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.
\(\lambda_k>0\), and an error tolerance \(\eta_k\geq0\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed triple obeys an inexact resolvent equation with verifiable error at most \(\eta_k\).
review_flags: Multiple inequivalent inexact proximal point models exist.
A source for the selected additive resolvent-error convention is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive resolvent-equation error model; enlargement-based variants are not silently identified with it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^k\in H\), compute \(x^{k+1},v^{k+1},e^{k+1}\in H\) such that
\[
v^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1}),
\qquad
x^k=x^{k+1}+\lambda_k v^{k+1}+e^{k+1},
\qquad
\lVert e^{k+1}\rVert\leq\eta_k.
\]
The exact method is recovered when \(\eta_k=0\). Stop according to a stated pair of accuracy tests, for example \(\lVert v^{k+1}\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\eta_k\leq\lambda_k\varepsilon\); output \(x^{k+1}\) together with \(v^{k+1}\) and \(e^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal step permits a bounded additive error in the resolvent equation while retaining an explicit operator value at the computed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Point Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive resolvent-equation error model is internally coherent and appropriately kept distinct from enlargement-based models, but it is only one of several inequivalent inexact proximal point conventions. A direct source for this convention and its terminology is required.

children.title: Proximal Inexactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Absolute, relative, or summable error criteria used to classify inexact variants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniformly Bounded Errors Need Not Converge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a nondecaying absolute additive-error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed absolute error allowance can sustain a non-solution forever.
assumptions_latex: The additive inexact resolvent equation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform boundedness of additive errors does not imply convergence to \(A^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Bounded Errors Need Not Converge

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed resolvent iteration under summable equation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[
x^k=x^{k+1}+\lambda_kv^{k+1}+e^{k+1},\qquad v^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1}),
\]
with \(\inf_k\lambda_k>0\) and \(\sum_k\|e^{k+1}\|<\infty\). If \(A^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\), then \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\in A^{-1}(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable additive equation errors preserve weak convergence when step sizes stay bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space and \(A^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x^\star\in A^{-1}(0)\) such that \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\).
review_flags: The error sign must remain consistent with the displayed equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Additive-Error Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Displacement-Relative Error Can Prevent Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal-monotone rotational counterexample to the stated relative additive-error predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(J(x_1,x_2)=(-x_2,x_1)\) and \(A=J\), which is maximal monotone with \(A^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\). Set \(\lambda_k=1\), choose \(x^0\ne0\), and define \[x^{k+1}=-Jx^k,\qquad v^{k+1}=Jx^{k+1}=x^k,\qquad e^{k+1}=Jx^k.\] Then \[x^k=x^{k+1}+v^{k+1}+e^{k+1},\qquad \|e^{k+1}\|=\frac1{\sqrt2}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\] Nevertheless \(\|x^k\|=\|x^0\|\) and the iterates cycle, so they do not converge to the zero of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed displacement-relative additive error factor below one does not by itself guarantee proximal-point convergence.
assumptions_latex: The additive inexact resolvent equation is used.
\(A=J\) is the planar ninety-degree rotation and \(\lambda_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(\|e^{k+1}\|\le\sigma_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\) with a fixed \(\sigma_k<1\) does not ensure convergence under maximal monotonicity alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Displacement-Relative Error Can Prevent Convergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative inexactness coupling an enlargement error and the resolvent-equation residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^k\), choose \(\lambda_k>0\), \(y^{k+1}\), \(v^{k+1}\), and \(\varepsilon_{k+1}\ge0\) such that \[v^{k+1}\in A^{[\varepsilon_{k+1}]}(y^{k+1}),\] \[\|\lambda_kv^{k+1}+y^{k+1}-x^k\|^2+2\lambda_k\varepsilon_{k+1}\le \sigma^2\|y^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,\qquad 0\le\sigma<1.\] The associated extragradient update is \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\lambda_kv^{k+1}\). When \(\sigma=0\), the inequality forces \(\varepsilon_{k+1}=0\), zero equation residual, and an exact resolvent step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid proximal-extragradient regime jointly controls enlargement error and resolvent-equation error relative to the trial displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: epsilon-enlargement of the maximal monotone operator

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Proximal-Extragradient Relative-Error Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fejér Decrease under the Hybrid Relative-Error Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step solution-distance decrease for the hybrid proximal-extragradient regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the hybrid relative-error criterion, set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\lambda_kv^{k+1}\). For every \(x^\star\in A^{-1}(0)\), \[\|x^{k+1}-x^\star\|^2\le \|x^k-x^\star\|^2-(1-\sigma^2)\|y^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\] Hence the iterates are Fejér monotone with respect to \(A^{-1}(0)\), and the trial displacements are square summable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid relative-error test gives Fejér decrease and square summability of trial displacements.
assumptions_latex: The hybrid proximal-extragradient criterion holds with a fixed \(0\le\sigma<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fejér Decrease under the Hybrid Relative-Error Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical error predicates for an additive inexact resolvent equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(v^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1})\), \(\lambda_k>0\), and \[x^k=x^{k+1}+\lambda_kv^{k+1}+e^{k+1}.\] The step is exact if \(e^{k+1}=0\); it has absolute allowance \(\eta_k\) if \(\|e^{k+1}\|\le\eta_k\); the absolute-error regime is summable if \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\); and it is displacement-relative with factor \(\sigma_k\) if \(\|e^{k+1}\|\le\sigma_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\). These are distinct admissibility predicates and do not share convergence consequences without further hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive resolvent errors can be exact, absolutely bounded, summably bounded, or relative to displacement; the regimes are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: \(v^{k+1}\in A(x^{k+1})\), \(\lambda_k>0\), and the displayed additive equation holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equations define distinct exact, absolute, summable, and displacement-relative error regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Resolvent-Error Regimes

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absolute, summable, and relative inexactness are distinct predicates on \(e^{k+1}\), with exactness given by \(e^{k+1}=0\).
review_flags: Convergence consequences depend on additional step-size and solution-existence assumptions.
A source comparing these inexactness predicates is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies error predicates for the additive inexact resolvent equation without asserting convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The step is exact when \(e^{k+1}=0\). It satisfies absolute inexactness with allowance \(\eta_k\geq0\) when
\[
\lVert e^{k+1}\rVert\leq\eta_k.
\]
The absolute errors are summable when
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.
\]
It satisfies displacement-relative inexactness with \(0\leq\sigma_k<1\) when
\[
\lVert e^{k+1}\rVert\leq\sigma_k\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert.
\]
These predicates specify different admissible error sets and must be paired with the convergence theorem appropriate to the selected regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal errors may be zero, absolutely bounded, summably bounded, or bounded relative to the step displacement; these regimes are not interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Inexactness Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits this terminal container, and the record avoids unsupported convergence claims. However, no source supports the selected absolute, summable, and displacement-relative predicates or their association with the stated additive-error equation.

children.title: Relaxed Proximal Point Variants
children.top_down_role: Under-relaxed, over-relaxed, or averaged proximal point constructions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxed Resolvent Fejer Inequality and Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed proximal point iteration for a maximal monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone with \(S=A^{-1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), let \(p^k=J_{\lambda_kA}x^k\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\theta_k(p^k-x^k)\). For every \(z\in S\), \[\|x^{k+1}-z\|^2\le\|x^k-z\|^2-\theta_k(2-\theta_k)\|x^k-p^k\|^2.\] If \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\) and \(0<\underline\theta\le\theta_k\le\overline\theta<2\), then \(x^k-p^k\to0\) and \(x^k\) converges weakly to a point of \(S\); in finite dimensions the convergence is strong.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation uniformly inside zero and two preserves Fejér decrease and convergence, including with varying proximal parameters bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space and \(A^{-1}(0)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Resolvent Fejer Inequality and Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxed update is \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\theta_k(J_{\lambda_k A}x^k-x^k)\), and its step is a scaled resolvent residual.
review_flags: A direct source for the relaxation interval and convergence setting is required.
No convergence claim is made without additional parameter assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Underrelaxed and overrelaxed exact resolvent steps in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in H\), at iteration \(k\) compute
\[
p^k:=J_{\lambda_k A}x^k,
\qquad
x^{k+1}:=x^k+\theta_k(p^k-x^k).
\]
Equivalently, with \(R_{\lambda_k}(x^k):=\lambda_k^{-1}(x^k-p^k)\),
\[
x^{k+1}-x^k=-\theta_k\lambda_k R_{\lambda_k}(x^k),
\qquad
R_{\lambda_k}(x^k)\in A(p^k).
\]
Values \(0<\theta_k<1\), \(\theta_k=1\), and \(1<\theta_k<2\) give underrelaxed, exact, and overrelaxed updates, respectively. Stop when \(\lVert R_{\lambda_k}(x^k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed proximal point step moves a fraction or overstep toward the exact resolvent point while preserving its inclusion residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Proximal Point Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxed resolvent update and residual identity fit the algorithmic variant container. The restriction 0<θ_k<2 is a substantive regime choice that requires a direct locator, especially because no convergence theorem or additional sequence assumptions are stated.

children.title: Variable-Metric Proximal Point Variants
children.top_down_role: Proximal point constructions using iteration-dependent metrics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact convex PPA with uniformly equivalent, summably varying metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\) and \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|y-x_k\|_{H_k}^2\right\}.\] For every \(z\in S\), \[\|x_{k+1}-z\|_{H_k}^2\le\|x_k-z\|_{H_k}^2-\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|_{H_k}^2.\] If \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\), \(H_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)H_k\), \(\eta_k\ge0\), \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), and \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\), then \(x_k\) converges to a point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly coercive metrics with summably controlled variation preserve quasi-Fejér geometry and convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with a nonempty minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Quasi-Fejer Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(H_k\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\), \(\lambda_k>0\), and \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Squared norm induced by the positive-definite metric

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical finite-dimensional variable-metric proximal-point update and its convex optimality condition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex variant with uniformly positive-definite metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), generate \(x_{k+1}\) by
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|y-x_k\|_{H_k}^2\right\}.
\]
The objective is strongly convex, so the minimizer is unique. Its optimality condition is
\[
0\in\partial f(x_{k+1})+\frac{1}{\lambda_k}H_k(x_{k+1}-x_k).
\]
The algorithm stops when a prescribed displacement or inclusion-residual tolerance is met and returns the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, minimize the objective plus a quadratic regularizer defined by a uniformly positive-definite, iteration-dependent metric; the resulting strongly convex subproblem has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Proximal Point Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional variable-metric update, uniqueness claim, and optimality condition are mathematically standard and fit the algorithm container, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Bregman Proximal Point Variants
children.top_down_role: Proximal point constructions based on non-Euclidean Bregman geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Three-Point Inequality and Objective Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex Bregman proximal steps with interior minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in U}\{f(y)+\lambda_k^{-1}D_h(y,x_k)\}.\] For every admissible \(z\), \[\lambda_k(f(x_{k+1})-f(z))\le D_h(z,x_k)-D_h(z,x_{k+1})-D_h(x_{k+1},x_k).\] Hence \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)\). If an admissible minimizer \(x^*\) exists, then \[f(x_N)-f(x^*)\le\frac{D_h(x^*,x_0)}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\lambda_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman proximal steps obey a three-point divergence inequality, decrease the objective, and attain an inverse accumulated-step objective rate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on \(U=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\).
All iterates and comparison points are admissible, every subproblem has an interior minimizer, and \(\lambda_k>0\).
An admissible minimizer exists for the rate conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Inequality and Objective Rate

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on \(U=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), and each displayed subproblem has a minimizer in \(U\).

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by the kernel

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical Bregman proximal-point update and first-order optimality condition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Bregman proximal point method with interior iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in U}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{\lambda_k}D_h(y,x_k)\right\}.
\]
Strict convexity of \(h\) makes the minimizer unique whenever it exists and \(f\) is convex. Every interior minimizer satisfies
\[
0\in\partial f(x_{k+1})+\frac{1}{\lambda_k}\bigl(\nabla h(x_{k+1})-\nabla h(x_k)\bigr).
\]
Stop under a prescribed Bregman-displacement or inclusion-residual tolerance and return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bregman proximal point method replaces squared Euclidean distance by a kernel-generated divergence; an interior solution balances an objective subgradient against the change in the kernel gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Proximal Point Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bregman proximal update and interior optimality condition are plausible under the stated existence and strict-convexity assumptions and fit the algorithm container, but they lack an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Variant Well-Posedness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Metric, relaxation, or kernel regimes where standard residual interpretations cease to apply.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Bregman Kernel Does Not Ensure Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Bregman proximal existence despite a smooth strictly convex kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(h(y)=e^y\), \(f(y)=y\), take the center \(x=0\), and set \(\lambda=1\). Then \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex and \[f(y)+D_h(y,0)=y+(e^y-1-y)=e^y-1.\] Its infimum is \(-1\), approached as \(y\to-\infty\), but it has no minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict kernel geometry ensures uniqueness only if a minimizer exists; it does not by itself ensure attainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Bregman proximal subproblem has a finite unattained infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Bregman Kernel Does Not Ensure Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of relaxed proximal convergence at and beyond relaxation two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=N_{\{0\}}\) on \(\mathbb R\). Then \(J_{\lambda A}x=0\) and the relaxed update is \[x^{k+1}=(1-\theta)x^k.\] For \(x^0\ne0\), \(\theta=2\) gives the two-cycle \(x^{k+1}=-x^k\), while \(\theta>2\) gives \(|x^k|=|1-\theta|^k|x^0|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation two can cycle, and larger relaxation can diverge even for a simple maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration cycles at \(\theta=2\) and diverges for \(\theta>2\).

notation.meaning: normal-cone operator of the singleton zero

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Endpoint Cycling and Divergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniqueness or existence without a positive-definite quadratic metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R^2\). If \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_y\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|_H^2=\{(x_1,t):t\in\mathbb R\}.\] If \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), the quadratic proximal objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular metric can make the proximal point nonunique, while an indefinite metric can destroy existence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Singular \(H\) may destroy uniqueness; indefinite \(H\) may destroy existence.

notation.meaning: quadratic form \(\langle Hz,z\rangle\), not necessarily a norm

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate and Indefinite Metric Failures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of single-valuedness when the kernel supplies no strict geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(f\equiv0\) and \(h\equiv0\). Then \(D_h(y,x)=0\) for all \(x,y\), so for every \(\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{f(y)+\lambda^{-1}D_h(y,x)\}=\mathbb R.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity and differentiability of a kernel without strict geometry do not ensure a unique Bregman proximal point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Bregman proximal argmin is all of \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Strict Bregman Kernel Nonuniqueness

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) has a unique minimizer exactly when \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\); at and beyond \(\rho^{-1}\), uniqueness or existence fails.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit negative-quadratic example establishes the sharp weak-convexity parameter boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp Euclidean well-posedness boundary for a weakly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex. If \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), then \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) is strongly convex and has the unique minimizer
\[
y=\frac{x}{1-\lambda\rho}.
\]
If \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), then \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) is affine in \(y\): it is unbounded below when \(x\neq0\), while every \(y\) minimizes it when \(x=0\). If \(\lambda>\rho^{-1}\), its quadratic coefficient is negative and it is unbounded below. Thus the strict parameter inequality cannot generally be relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative quadratic shows the boundary is sharp: below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus the proximal point is unique, while at or above it existence or uniqueness can fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Variant Well-Posedness Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-quadratic example correctly exhibits the sharp boundary at lambda equal to the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus and appropriately has kind failure_boundary, but no source locator is supplied.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 4.4.3, Weakly Convex Functions; Section 7.2.1, Moreau Surrogation
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth of the Proximal Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth geometry about the unique minimizer of a subthreshold weakly convex proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=\operatorname*{argmin}_y Q_{\lambda,x}(y)\), where \(Q_{\lambda,x}(y)=f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\) and \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\). Then for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[Q_{\lambda,x}(y)\ge Q_{\lambda,x}(p)+\frac{\lambda^{-1}-\rho}{2}\|y-p\|^2.\] Consequently, \(Q_{\lambda,x}(y)-Q_{\lambda,x}(p)\le\varepsilon\) implies \(\|y-p\|\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon/(\lambda^{-1}-\rho)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity yields quadratic growth and converts proximal-subproblem objective error into distance from the unique proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth of the Proximal Subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean regularization of a proper lower-semicontinuous weakly convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[
Q_{\lambda,x}(y)=f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2.
\]
Then \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and \((\lambda^{-1}-\rho)\)-strongly convex. Consequently, it has a unique minimizer in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus, the quadratically regularized subproblem is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and strongly convex with modulus equal to the reciprocal parameter minus the weak-convexity modulus; hence it has a unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) is coercive and \((\lambda^{-1}-\rho)\)-strongly convex, and therefore has a unique minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary optimality equation for quadratic regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The one-way first-order condition stated for a minimizer of a convex differentiable objective with Euclidean quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be convex and differentiable, let x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n, and let \delta>0. Define
\[
f_\delta(x)=f(x)+\frac{\delta}{2}\lVert x-x_0\rVert^2.
\]
If x_\delta^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f_\delta(x), then
\[
\nabla f(x_\delta^*)+\delta(x_\delta^*-x_0)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If x_delta* minimizes the convex differentiable objective obtained by adding delta times one half of the squared distance to x0, then the gradient of f at x_delta* plus delta times its displacement from x0 is zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratically regularized objective and its optimal points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean quadratic regularization of a differentiable objective about a fixed reference point; the definition does not assert that a minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be differentiable, let x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n, and let \delta>0. Define
\[
f_\delta(x):=f(x)+\frac{\delta}{2}\lVert x-x_0\rVert^2.
\]
A point x_\delta^*\in\mathbb{R}^n is an optimal point of f_\delta if x_\delta^* minimizes f_\delta over \mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable objective f, a reference point x0, and a positive parameter delta, the quadratically regularized objective is f_delta(x) = f(x) + (delta/2) times the squared distance from x to x0. A point is called optimal for f_delta when it is a global minimizer over R^n; existence is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_\delta(x)=f(x)+\frac{\delta}{2}\lVert x-x_0\rVert^2,\qquad x_\delta^*\text{ is optimal for }f_\delta\iff x_\delta^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f_\delta(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance inequality for a quadratically regularized minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fejér-type geometry relating a regularized minimizer, its regularization center, and a minimizer of the original convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be convex and differentiable, let x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x), fix x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n and \delta>0, and define
\[
f_\delta(x)=f(x)+\frac{\delta}{2}\lVert x-x_0\rVert^2.
\]
If x_\delta^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f_\delta(x), then
\[
\lVert x_\delta^*-x_0\rVert^2+\lVert x_\delta^*-x^*\rVert^2\leq \lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2.
\]
In particular, if R_0\geq\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert, then \lVert x_\delta^*-x_0\rVert\leq R_0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a minimizer x* of the original convex differentiable objective, the squared distance from the quadratically regularized minimizer to the regularization center plus its squared distance to x* is at most the squared distance from the center to x*. Thus any upper bound R0 on the latter distance also bounds the regularized minimizer's displacement from the center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert x_\delta^*-x_0\rVert^2+\lVert x_\delta^*-x^*\rVert^2\leq\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2;\qquad R_0\geq\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert\implies\lVert x_\delta^*-x_0\rVert\leq R_0

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global finite-dimensional single-valuedness and Lipschitz regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the proximal subproblem is coercive and \((\lambda^{-1}-\rho)\)-strongly convex, so it has a unique minimizer. Thus \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) is defined on all of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Furthermore, for all \(x,z\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\|\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(z)\|\leq\frac{1}{1-\lambda\rho}\|x-z\|.
\]
In particular, the proximal mapping is globally single-valued and Lipschitz throughout the strict parameter regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly convex objective and a parameter below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus, every proximal subproblem has one solution and the resulting mapping is globally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Valued Proximal-Mapping Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global single-valuedness and Lipschitz bound are standard for a finite-dimensional rho-weakly convex function in the strict parameter regime, and theorem is the correct kind, but no authoritative locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Reciprocal Weak-Convexity Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional quadratic examples realizing the critical and supercritical failures in the parameter classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho>0\) and \(f(y)=-\frac{\rho}{2}y^2\). At \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), the proximal objective is constant when \(x=0\), so every \(y\in\mathbb R\) minimizes it, while for \(x\ne0\) it is nonconstant affine and unbounded below. If \(\lambda>\rho^{-1}\), then at \(x=0\) its quadratic coefficient is \(\frac12(\lambda^{-1}-\rho)<0\), so it is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concave quadratic realizes critical nonuniqueness, critical nonexistence, and supercritical unboundedness, showing that weak convexity alone cannot improve the reciprocal threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), uniqueness or existence may fail, and for \(\lambda>\rho^{-1}\) the proximal subproblem may be unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Reciprocal Weak-Convexity Threshold

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The guaranteed single-valued regime is \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\); \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\) is critical, and \(\lambda>\rho^{-1}\) is generally ill-posed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter classification for Euclidean weakly convex proximal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The regularized objective has net curvature modulus \(\lambda^{-1}-\rho\). Accordingly:
\[
0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}
\]
is the uniform well-posedness regime, in which every centered subproblem is strongly convex and has a unique minimizer. At \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), strong convexity vanishes and existence or uniqueness requires additional structure. For \(\lambda>\rho^{-1}\), the regularizer need not dominate negative curvature, so the subproblem may be nonconvex or unbounded below. When \(\rho=0\), every finite \(\lambda>0\) lies in the first regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reciprocal weak-convexity modulus separates guaranteed unique proximal solutions from a critical boundary and a supercritical regime where the regularized problem may be ill-posed.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Parameter Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subcritical, critical, and supercritical parameter classification is mathematically consistent and condition is an appropriate content kind, but the record has no inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity at the proximal point, not necessarily at the center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The first-order optimality condition for the proximal subproblem gives
\[
0\in\partial f(p)+\frac{1}{\lambda}(p-x).
\]
Equivalently, \(v=\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\in\partial f(p)\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p))\leq\|v\|=\frac{1}{\lambda}\|x-p\|.
\]
Thus a small proximal displacement at \(x\) produces a nearby point \(p\) with a correspondingly small subgradient; zero displacement is equivalent to stationarity of \(x=p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled displacement from a center to its proximal point is a subgradient at the proximal point, so a small displacement transfers directly to nearby approximate stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Stationarity Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal optimality condition correctly transfers scaled displacement to a limiting subgradient at the proximal point, and the property fits the container, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cocoercivity of the Convex Proximal Displacement Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity of the scaled displacement for a proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
R_\lambda(x)=\frac1\lambda\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\bigr),
\]
one has
\[
\langle R_\lambda(x)-R_\lambda(y),x-y\rangle\geq\lambda\|R_\lambda(x)-R_\lambda(y)\|^2.
\]
Consequently \(R_\lambda\) is monotone and \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, scaled proximal displacement is lambda-cocoercive, monotone, and inverse-lambda Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Cocoercivity of the Convex Proximal Displacement Residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled Euclidean displacement for a single-valued proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the proximal displacement residual vector and its scalar magnitude by
\[
R_\lambda(x)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\bigr),
\qquad
r_\lambda(x)=\|R_\lambda(x)\|.
\]
The scaling gives \(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=\lambda R_\lambda(x)\). Hence \(R_\lambda(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\) is a fixed point of the proximal mapping. Under the usual proximal optimality condition, any such fixed point satisfies \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal displacement residual is the center-to-proximal-point displacement divided by the parameter; it vanishes exactly at fixed points of the proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Displacement Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled displacement residual and its fixed-point zero characterization are standard and appropriately recorded as a definition, but the record lacks source evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cocoercivity and Lipschitz Continuity of the Resolvent Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global regularity of the Yosida residual for a maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For all \(x,y\in H\),
\[
\langle F_{\lambda A}(x)-F_{\lambda A}(y),x-y\rangle\geq\lambda\|F_{\lambda A}(x)-F_{\lambda A}(y)\|^2.
\]
Consequently \(F_{\lambda A}\) is monotone and \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal-monotone resolvent residual is lambda-cocoercive, monotone, and inverse-lambda Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cocoercivity and Lipschitz Continuity of the Resolvent Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Resolvent Residual as the Yosida Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical operator-theoretic representation of scaled resolvent displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
A_\lambda:=\frac1\lambda(I-J_{\lambda A}),
\]
one has
\[
A_\lambda=(A^{-1}+\lambda I)^{-1},
\qquad A_\lambda(x)\in A(J_{\lambda A}x).
\]
Thus \(F_{\lambda A}=A_\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled resolvent displacement is the Yosida approximation, equivalently the inverse of the regularized inverse operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Residual as the Yosida Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal-monotone resolvent residual in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[
F_{\lambda A}(x)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\bigl(x-J_{\lambda A}x\bigr).
\]
Writing \(y=J_{\lambda A}x\), the resolvent identity gives
\[
F_{\lambda A}(x)=\frac{x-y}{\lambda}\in A(y).
\]
Moreover,
\[
F_{\lambda A}(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x=J_{\lambda A}x
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in A(x).
\]
Thus its zero set is precisely the solution set of the monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled difference between a point and its resolvent image is a fixed-point residual whose zeros are exactly the zeros of the underlying maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Fixed-Point Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resolvent residual identity and zero-set equivalence are correct for a maximal monotone operator, and definition fits the leaf, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Inclusion Stationarity Need Not Solve the Proximal Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of sufficiency for a limiting-subdifferential inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(y)=-y^2\), \(x=0\), and \(\lambda=1\). Then
\[
0\in\partial f(0)+(0-x)/\lambda,
\]
but \(f(y)+\tfrac12(y-x)^2=-\tfrac12y^2\) is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconvex objective, zero limiting-subdifferential inclusion residual may indicate only stationarity, not proximal optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero inclusion residual is not sufficient for proximal-subproblem optimality without a sufficiency condition such as convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Inclusion Stationarity Need Not Solve the Proximal Subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero inclusion residual for a convex proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, then
\[
0\in\partial f(y)+\frac1\lambda(y-x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
y=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x).
\]
The proximal point is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex objective, zero proximal inclusion residual is necessary and sufficient for the unique exact proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(\partial f\) is its convex subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for the proximal subproblem optimality inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x,y)=\operatorname{dist}\left(0,\partial f(y)+\frac{1}{\lambda}(y-x)\right)
=\inf_{v\in\partial f(y)}\left\|v+\frac{1}{\lambda}(y-x)\right\|.
\]
A supplied \(v\in\partial f(y)\) verifies the upper bound
\[
r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x,y)\leq\left\|v+\frac{1}{\lambda}(y-x)\right\|.
\]
The residual vanishes exactly when \(y\) satisfies the proximal optimality inclusion; whenever that inclusion is sufficient for global optimality, zero residual certifies that \(y\) solves the proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inclusion residual is the distance from zero to the proximal optimality set; a subgradient provides a verifiable bound, and zero residual certifies the exact inclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Inclusion Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distance-to-inclusion construction fits the certificate container, but the precise subdifferential notion should be stated explicitly and the claim lacks an inspectable source. Source support is needed before fixing the intended nonconvex subdifferential convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance to the Exact Convex Proximal Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative consequence of an additive inclusion residual for a convex proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be proper, closed, and convex, \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\), and
\[
v\in\partial f(y),\qquad e=v+\frac1\lambda(y-x).
\]
Then \(\|y-p\|\leq\lambda\|e\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex proximal subproblem, additive inclusion error bounds distance to the unique exact proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\), \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\), and \(v\in\partial f(y)\), where \(\partial f\) is the convex subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of numerical tolerances on residual units and the proximal parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(e=v+\lambda^{-1}(y-x)\), the equation-unit residual is \(\lambda e=\lambda v+y-x\). Thus
\[
\|e\|\leq\varepsilon\quad\text{and}\quad\|\lambda e\|\leq\varepsilon
\]
are inequivalent unless the tolerance is rescaled with \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradient-unit and equation-unit residuals differ by the proximal parameter, so their numerical tolerances are not interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equation residual is \(\lambda e\), and tolerances must be rescaled accordingly.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Convention and Scaling Dependence

assumptions_latex: \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\lambda>0\), and a vector \(v\in\partial f(y)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|e\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(e\in\partial f(y)+\lambda^{-1}(y-x)\) with inclusion error at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-error certificate for an approximate proximal subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form the error vector
\[
e=v+\frac{1}{\lambda}(y-x).
\]
Then
\[
e\in\partial f(y)+\frac{1}{\lambda}(y-x),
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{inc}}(x,y)\leq\|e\|.
\]
The pair \((y,v)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-inexact proximal point when \(\|e\|\leq\varepsilon\). The certificate is exact at \(\varepsilon=0\). For a sequence of inexact subproblems, the tolerance may depend on the iteration; convergence claims require a separately specified absolute, relative, or summability rule for those tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate point and one of its subgradients yield a computable inclusion error; bounding its norm certifies an inexact proximal solution at the chosen tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive inclusion-error certificate is internally coherent and certificate is the correct kind, but the subdifferential notion is not identified and no source supports the selected inexactness convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the infimum defining \(f_\lambda(x)\) is attained at the unique point \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). The function \(f_\lambda:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and continuously differentiable, and
\[
\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\frac{1}{\lambda}(x-p)
=\frac{1}{\lambda}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\bigr).
\]
Its gradient is \(\lambda^{-1}\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, \(\inf f_\lambda=\inf f\), and the two functions have the same minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive parameter, a proper closed convex function has a finite convex smooth Moreau envelope whose gradient equals the scaled proximal displacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Envelope Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Convex Envelope Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Moreau envelope in the subthreshold weak-convexity regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, meaning \(f+(\rho/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex. For \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with \(1/0=+\infty\), define \[f_\lambda(x)=\inf_y\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\}.\] The proximal subproblem is strongly convex, so \(P_\lambda(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) is single-valued. Moreover, \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable, \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\), and \(f_\lambda\) is \(\rho/(1-\lambda\rho)\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the reciprocal weak-convexity threshold, the proximal map is single-valued, the Moreau envelope is continuously differentiable with gradient equal to the scaled proximal residual, and the envelope is weakly convex with modulus rho divided by one minus lambda rho.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\lambda\) is single-valued, \(\nabla f_\lambda=\lambda^{-1}(I-P_\lambda)\), and \(f_\lambda\) is \(\rho/(1-\lambda\rho)\)-weakly convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative regularity below the weak-convexity threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and let \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). Then \[\|P_\lambda(x)-P_\lambda(z)\|\le\frac{1}{1-\lambda\rho}\|x-z\|\] and \[\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)-\nabla f_\lambda(z)\|\le\max\left\{\frac1\lambda,\frac{\rho}{1-\lambda\rho}\right\}\|x-z\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the weak-convexity threshold, the proximal map and envelope gradient are globally Lipschitz with explicit parameter-dependent bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Regime Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp transition at the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper lower-semicontinuous \(\rho\)-weakly convex function, the uniform guarantee of strong convexity of the proximal subproblem holds precisely when \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). The boundary is sharp: for \(f(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), the objective defining \(f_\lambda(x)\) has quadratic coefficient \((1-\lambda\rho)/(2\lambda)\). At \(\lambda=1/\rho\), it is unbounded below for \(x\ne0\) and has every \(y\) as a minimizer for \(x=0\); for \(\lambda>1/\rho\), it is unbounded below for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the reciprocal weak-convexity threshold, proximal uniqueness and envelope finiteness can fail; beyond it, even a quadratic example has an unbounded proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda<1/\rho\) is the sharp uniform envelope-regime threshold for the class of \(\rho\)-weakly convex functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Gradient Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual representation in the single-valued weakly convex proximal regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and let \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). With \(P_\lambda(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\), define the proximal residual \(R_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\). Then \[R_\lambda(x)=\nabla f_\lambda(x)\quad\text{and}\quad R_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(P_\lambda(x)).\] Consequently, \(\|R_\lambda(x)\|\) is both the envelope-gradient norm and a subgradient norm evaluated at the proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled displacement from a point to its proximal point equals the Moreau-envelope gradient and is a subgradient at that proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.

The equality remains valid when both argmin sets are empty.

children.title: Stationary-Point Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between envelope stationarity plus stationarity of the original objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary-Point Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity equivalence below the weak-convexity proximal threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). Then, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[\nabla f_\lambda(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=P_\lambda(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x).\] Thus the stationary points of the differentiable envelope coincide with the limiting-stationary points of \(f\), and every such point is a fixed point of the proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the weak-convexity threshold, envelope stationarity, proximal fixed-point status, and limiting-subdifferential stationarity are equivalent at the same point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.

children.title: Correspondence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Parameter or regularity regimes where minimizer or stationary-point transfer weakens.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Need Not Imply a Proximal Fixed Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stationary-point transfer beyond the weak-convexity parameter threshold despite pointwise proximal uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=y^4-2y^3\) on \(\mathbb R\) and \(\lambda=1\). Then \(f'(0)=0\), whereas the proximal objective at zero is \(q(y)=f(y)+\tfrac12y^2=y^2(y^2-2y+\tfrac12)\), whose unique global minimizer is \(u=(3+\sqrt5)/4\). Consequently, \[0\in\partial f(0),\qquad P_1f(0)=\{u\},\qquad 0\notin P_1f(0).\] Thus pointwise uniqueness of the proximal solution alone does not make original stationarity equivalent to proximal fixed-point stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside the curvature-controlled parameter regime, an original stationary point need not be a proximal fixed point even when its proximal subproblem has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Need Not Imply a Proximal Fixed Point
Correspondence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of proximal uniqueness destroys the differentiable stationarity correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak convexity or another condition ensuring a single-valued proximal map cannot simply be omitted. For \(f(x)=-|x|\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) and any \(\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\{-\lambda,\lambda\}.\] Moreover, direct minimization gives \(f_\lambda(x)=-|x|-\lambda/2\), so \(f_\lambda\) is not differentiable at \(0\). Hence neither a single envelope-gradient residual at \(0\) nor the equivalence \(\nabla f_\lambda(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow0\in\partial f(0)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without proximal uniqueness, the envelope may remain nonsmooth. The function minus absolute value has two proximal points and no envelope gradient at the origin.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementary decomposition of quadratic energy into envelopes of a convex function and its conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and define \(e_\gamma g(z)=\inf_w\{g(w)+\|z-w\|^2/(2\gamma)\}\). For every \(\lambda>0\) and \(x\in H\), \[e_\lambda f(x)+e_{1/\lambda}f^*(x/\lambda)=\frac{\|x\|^2}{2\lambda}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moreau envelopes of a convex function and its conjugate, evaluated at complementary scales, sum to the scaled squared norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau Envelope Value Decomposition
Moreau Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical scaled Moreau decomposition for convex conjugate pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). Writing \(f^*(v)=\sup_u\{\langle v,u\rangle-f(u)\}\), every \(x\in H\) satisfies \[x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)+\lambda\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\lambda}(x/\lambda).\] Equivalently, \(I=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}+\lambda\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\lambda}\circ(\lambda^{-1}I)\). Both proximal points are uniquely defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point splits uniquely into a primal proximal point plus the parameter-scaled proximal point of the convex conjugate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Proximal Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual proximal map associated with a convex function and scale parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). The dual proximal map at \(x\in H\) is \[D_\lambda^f(x):=\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\lambda}(x/\lambda)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in H}\left\{f^*(v)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\left\|v-\frac{x}{\lambda}\right\|^2\right\}.\] Strong convexity of the displayed objective makes \(D_\lambda^f(x)\) single-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual proximal map applies the proximal operator of the scaled Fenchel conjugate to the correspondingly scaled input.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

children.title: Primal-Dual Proximal Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Translation of residual information across primal plus dual proximal representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero Fenchel-Young gap certifies complementary primal and dual proximal points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). For \(u,v\in H\) satisfying \(x=u+\lambda v\), the following are equivalent: \[u=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\ \text{ and }\ v=\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\lambda}(x/\lambda);\] \[f(u)+f^*(v)-\langle u,v\rangle=0.\] Thus the nonnegative Fenchel-Young gap is an exact certificate for a complementary proximal pair once the affine decomposition is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the affine relation between the components, zero Fenchel-Young gap exactly certifies the primal and dual proximal points.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((u,v)\) is the complementary proximal pair if and only if \(f(u)+f^*(v)=\langle u,v\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Young Certificate for Proximal Pairing
Primal-Dual Proximal Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-subgradient correspondence between the two Moreau proximal components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the hypotheses of the convex Moreau decomposition, set \(u=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) and \(v=\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\lambda}(x/\lambda)\). Then \[x=u+\lambda v,\qquad v\in\partial f(u),\qquad u\in\partial f^*(v).\] Conversely, if \(u,v\in H\) satisfy \(x=u+\lambda v\) and \(v\in\partial f(u)\), then they are exactly these primal and dual proximal points. Thus either proximal component uniquely determines the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual proximal points sum to the input after scaling, and they are paired by mutually inverse convex subdifferentials.
assumptions_latex: \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Recovery of the Original Convex Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order and zero-parameter limit of convex Moreau smoothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. If \(0<\lambda<\mu\), then \[f_\mu(x)\le f_\lambda(x)\le f(x)\quad(x\in H).\] Moreover, \(f_\lambda(x)\uparrow f(x)\) as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), in the extended-real sense.

children.title: Envelope Conditioning Effects

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Curvature Creation without Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a positive uniform envelope curvature guarantee for general convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), one has \(P_\lambda=I\) and \(f_\lambda\equiv0\) for every \(\lambda>0\). Thus Moreau regularization alone does not create positive strong convexity, and no finite smooth condition-number guarantee based on positive curvature holds uniformly over merely convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moreau smoothing does not create strong convexity from a flat convex objective.
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Curvature Creation without Strong Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning of Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition bounds requiring strong convexity but not smoothness of the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, with \(\mu>0\), and let \(\lambda>0\). Then \(P_\lambda=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) is \((1+\lambda\mu)^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, while \(f_\lambda\) is \(\mu/(1+\lambda\mu)\)-strongly convex and has \(1/\lambda\)-Lipschitz gradient. Hence \[\kappa(f_\lambda)\le\frac{1+\lambda\mu}{\lambda\mu}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity alone gives a contractive proximal map and an explicit smooth condition-number bound for the envelope.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex.

notation.meaning: ratio of a gradient-Lipschitz bound to a strong-convexity modulus

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning of Strongly Convex Nonsmooth Envelopes
Envelope Conditioning Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guaranteed curvature transformation for smooth strongly convex objectives under Moreau regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable with \(\mu I\preceq\nabla^2f(y)\preceq LI\) for every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(0<\mu\le L\), and let \(\lambda>0\). Then \(f_\lambda\) is \(\mu/(1+\lambda\mu)\)-strongly convex and its gradient is \(L/(1+\lambda L)\)-Lipschitz. Consequently, a smooth condition-number upper bound is \[\kappa_\lambda=\frac{L(1+\lambda\mu)}{\mu(1+\lambda L)}\le\frac{L}{\mu}.\] This bound decreases monotonically toward \(1\) as \(\lambda\) increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth strongly convex objective with curvature between mu and L, Moreau regularization guarantees transformed curvature bounds and a condition-number upper bound that decreases toward one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\lambda\) is \(\mu/(1+\lambda\mu)\)-strongly convex, \(\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f_\lambda)\le L/(1+\lambda L)\), and \(\kappa_\lambda\le L/\mu\).

notation.meaning: condition-number upper bound for the envelope

children.title: Smoothing–Conditioning Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Parameter-dependent balance between regularity gains plus conditioning changes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Lipschitz Smoothing Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A convex function simultaneously attaining the envelope-bias and gradient-smoothness bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=G|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(G>0\). Then \[f_\lambda(x)=\begin{cases}x^2/(2\lambda),&|x|\le\lambda G,\\G|x|-\lambda G^2/2,&|x|\ge\lambda G.\end{cases}\] Consequently, \(\sup_x(f(x)-f_\lambda(x))=\lambda G^2/2\) and \(\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f_\lambda)=1/\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute-value function simultaneously attains the linear bias and reciprocal smoothness bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Lipschitz Smoothing Tradeoff
Smoothing–Conditioning Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative approximation-versus-smoothness tradeoff for Lipschitz convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be proper, closed, convex, and \(G\)-Lipschitz, and let \(\lambda>0\). Then for every \(x\), \[0\le f(x)-f_\lambda(x)\le\frac{\lambda G^2}{2},\qquad \operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f_\lambda)\le\frac{1}{\lambda}.\] Hence decreasing \(\lambda\) reduces the worst-case envelope bias linearly but increases the guaranteed gradient-Lipschitz constant reciprocally; increasing \(\lambda\) reverses these effects. In particular, the product of the two displayed worst-case bounds equals \(G^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller envelope parameter improves approximation to a Lipschitz convex function but worsens the guaranteed gradient smoothness constant; the two bounds scale reciprocally.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step Moreau-envelope decrease generated by an exact proximal-point update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and let \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with \(1/0=+\infty\). Define \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda h}(x)\). Then \(h_\lambda\) is differentiable at \(x\), \(\nabla h_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-p)\), and \[h_\lambda(p)\le h_\lambda(x)-\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-p\|^2=h_\lambda(x)-\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\nabla h_\lambda(x)\|^2.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Envelope Decrease
Envelope Decrease Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract sufficient-decrease mechanism for a differentiable Moreau envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}\) be bounded below, and suppose iterates satisfy \[E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-a_k\|
abla E(x_k)\|^2+e_k,\qquad a_k>0,\quad e_k\ge0.\] Then, for every \(N\ge1\), \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\|
abla E(x_k)\|^2\le E(x_0)-\inf E+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k.\] Thus envelope decrease converts directly into a weighted residual bound; when \(E=f_\lambda\), the residual is \(\|
abla f_\lambda(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient envelope decrease telescopes into a bound on the weighted sum of squared stationarity residuals.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: telescoping a sufficient-decrease inequality is standard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping statement is mathematically correct and the principle fits the container, but no citation with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent-to-Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate complexity obtained from uniform envelope decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(E:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}\) is bounded below and \[E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-a\|
abla E(x_k)\|^2\] for every \(k\), where \(a>0\). Writing \(\Delta=E(x_0)-\inf E\), one has \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|
abla E(x_k)\|^2\le  rac{\Delta}{aN}.\] Consequently, an iterate satisfying \(\|
abla E(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\) is guaranteed within \(N\ge\lceil\Delta/(a\varepsilon^2)ceil\) iterations, under the unit-cost iteration model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform envelope descent yields an order-one-over-epsilon-squared iteration bound for finding an epsilon-stationary iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\ge\lceil\Delta/(a\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) suffices for some \(k<N\) to satisfy \(\|\nabla E(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Deterministic Envelope Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Envelope Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise certificate from a deterministic envelope-descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let deterministic iterates satisfy \[E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-a_k\|G(x_k)\|^2+e_k\] for \(0\le k<N\), with \(a_k>0\), \(e_k\ge0\), and \(E_*\le\inf E\). Then the computable quantity \[C_N:=\frac{E(x_0)-E_*+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k}\] certifies \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|G(x_k)\|^2\le C_N.\] If \(G=\nabla f_\lambda\), this is a deterministic Moreau-envelope stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pathwise descent record and a valid envelope lower bound certify the smallest observed residual.
assumptions_latex: \(a_k>0\), \(e_k\ge0\), and the displayed descent inequalities hold.

children.title: Stochastic Envelope Certificates
children.top_down_role: Expectation, probability, or sampling-based envelope guarantees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-run probability certificate obtained from an expected squared residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a random output \(X\) satisfies \(\mathbb E\|G(X)\|^2\le C\), where \(C\ge0\). Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P(\|G(X)\|>\varepsilon)\le \min\{1,C/\varepsilon^2\}.\] Consequently, if \(0<\delta<1\), then \(C\le\delta\varepsilon^2\) certifies \(\|G(X)\|\le\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expected squared envelope residual gives a one-run probability certificate through Markov's inequality, with inverse-confidence dependence.

notation.meaning: upper bound on expected squared residual
