failure_boundary: this conversion incurs inverse-confidence dependence and is not a stronger concentration result
knowledge_statements.title: Markov High-Probability Envelope Certificate
Stochastic Envelope Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected stationarity certificate under conditional envelope descent with deterministic descent weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^{N}\) be a filtration, let \(x_k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(x_0\) be deterministic. Suppose all displayed random variables are integrable and, for every \(0\le k<N\), \[\mathbb E[E(x_{k+1})\mid\mathcal F_k]\le E(x_k)-a_k\|G(x_k)\|^2+e_k,\] where \(a_k>0\) and \(e_k\ge0\) are deterministic and \(E_*\le\inf_x E(x)\). Let \(R\) be independent of \((x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1})\) with \[\mathbb P(R=k)=\frac{a_k}{\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}a_j},\qquad 0\le k<N.\] Then \[\mathbb E\|G(x_R)\|^2\le\frac{E(x_0)-E_*+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional expected descent with deterministic weights certifies the expected residual of an independently sampled iterate whose sampling probabilities are proportional to those weights.
assumptions_latex: \(N\ge1\), \((\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^{N}\) is a filtration, \(x_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and \(x_0\) is deterministic.
All displayed random variables are integrable; \(a_k>0\) and \(e_k\ge0\) are deterministic; and \(E_*\le\inf_x E(x)\).
\(R\) is independent of the trajectory and follows the displayed sampling law.

notation.meaning: deterministic lower bound on the envelope

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tower property and independent weighted sampling yield the expected residual bound

children.title: Deterministic-to-Stochastic Certificate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Structural requirements for adapting deterministic envelope arguments to stochastic settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic-to-Stochastic Certificate Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-expectation transfer of a telescoping envelope certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k=0}^{N}\) be a filtration, let \(x_k\) and the nonnegative residual \(r_k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(x_0\) be deterministic. Suppose all displayed random variables are integrable and, for every \(0\le k<N\), \[\mathbb E[E(x_{k+1})\mid\mathcal F_k]\le E(x_k)-a_k r_k^2+e_k,\] where \(a_k>0\) and \(e_k\ge0\) are deterministic and \(E_*\le\inf_x E(x)\). Then \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\mathbb E[r_k^2]\le E(x_0)-E_*+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k.\] This transfer gives an expectation certificate; it does not by itself give a pathwise or high-probability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing deterministic one-step descent by conditional expected descent preserves the telescoping residual certificate in expectation, but not pathwise or with high probability without additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(N\ge1\), \(x_k\) and \(r_k\ge0\) are \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and \(x_0\) is deterministic.
All displayed random variables are integrable.

notation.meaning: deterministic lower bound on the envelope

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional expectation and the tower property yield the transfer

children.title: Last-Iterate Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual or envelope guarantees attached to the final computed iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric final-iterate guarantee under uniform residual contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\ge0\) and suppose \(r_{k+1}\le q r_k\) for every \(k\), where \(0<q<1\). Then \[r_N\le q^N r_0.\] Hence, for \(0<\varepsilon<r_0\), every \[N\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log(r_0/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil\] certifies \(r_N\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform residual contraction gives a geometric certificate for the final iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_N\le q^N r_0\), with the displayed logarithmic iteration count sufficient for \(r_N\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: residual of the final reported iterate

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated application of the contraction inequality
knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Last-Iterate Certificate
Last-Iterate Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate requiring a residual monotonicity or contraction property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a nonnegative residual sequence satisfies \(r_{k+1}\le r_k\) and \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k r_k^2\le B_N\] with \(a_k>0\). Then the last included iterate is certified by \[r_{N-1}^2\le\frac{B_N}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k}.\] For envelope residuals \(r_k=\|\nabla E(x_k)\|\), ordinary envelope-value descent alone does not establish the required residual monotonicity; that property must follow from the algorithm or an additional contraction argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted aggregate bound certifies the last iterate only when residual monotonicity or a comparable regularity property is available.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotonicity bounds the last residual by its weighted average

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The last-iterate certificate is correct under residual monotonicity and is appropriately classified, but no authoritative citation with a locator is provided.

children.title: Sampled-Iterate Certificates
children.top_down_role: Guarantees attached to an iterate selected through a prescribed sampling scheme.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail-probability conversion for the prescribed weighted random output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) determine \(r_k\ge0\), \(a_k>0\), and \(B_N\), with \(\sum_{k<N}a_kr_k^2\le B_N\) almost surely. If \(A_N=\sum_{k<N}a_k\) and \(\mathbb P(R=k\mid\mathcal F)=a_k/A_N\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P(r_R\ge\varepsilon\mid\mathcal F)\le \min\left\{1,\frac{B_N}{A_N\varepsilon^2}\right\}.\] Hence \(B_N\le\delta A_N\varepsilon^2\) implies \(\mathbb P(r_R<\varepsilon\mid\mathcal F)\ge1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted aggregate residual budget yields a high-probability certificate for the prescribed randomly sampled iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Sampled-Iterate Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure under an Unprescribed Output Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of the declared sampling distribution for the weighted-average certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_0=a_1=1\), \(r_0=0\), and \(r_1=1\). Proportional sampling gives \(\mathbb E[r_R^2]=1/2\). If instead \(R=1\) almost surely, then \(\mathbb E[r_R^2]=1\). Thus an arbitrary output rule need not satisfy the weighted-average identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted sampled-output certificate can fail when the output index does not follow the prescribed law.
assumptions_latex: The alternative rule selects \(R=1\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure under an Unprescribed Output Rule
Sampled-Iterate Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted random-output conversion of an aggregate residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_0,\ldots,r_{N-1}\ge0\) and \(a_0,\ldots,a_{N-1}>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{k<N}a_k r_k^2\le B_N\). Draw \(R\) independently of the residual values with \[\mathbb P(R=k)=\frac{a_k}{\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}a_j}.\] Then \[\mathbb E[r_R^2]=\frac{\sum_{k<N}a_k r_k^2}{\sum_{k<N}a_k}\le\frac{B_N}{\sum_{k<N}a_k}.\] The same identity holds after total expectation when the residual sequence is random and the conditional sampling rule is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling in proportion to descent weights converts an aggregate residual budget exactly into an expected output certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) follows the displayed conditional or unconditional sampling law.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the certificate follows from the definition of weighted sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-sampling identity is correct and fits the certificate container, but it lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Output-Selection Certificate Gap
children.top_down_role: Differences in strength or prerequisites caused by the iterate-selection rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of predetermined, best, and weighted-random outputs under only an aggregate residual budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k>0\), \(r_k\ge0\), \(A_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\), and suppose \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k r_k^2\le B\). Then \[\min_{k<N}r_k^2\le B/A_N.\] If \(R\) is sampled with \(\mathbb P(R=k)=a_k/A_N\), then \(\mathbb E[r_R^2]\le B/A_N\). In contrast, a predetermined index \(j\) is guaranteed only \[r_j^2\le B/a_j,\] and this is sharp under the aggregate assumption alone: equality is attained by setting \(r_j^2=B/a_j\) and all other residuals to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate weighted budget controls best and weight-sampled outputs at the averaged scale, but a predetermined output only at its individual-weight scale; these bounds are sharp.
assumptions_latex: The predetermined index \(j\) is fixed without using residual values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{k<N}r_k^2\le B/A_N\), \(\mathbb E[r_R^2]\le B/A_N\), but universally only \(r_j^2\le B/a_j\) for predetermined \(j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct consequences of the aggregate sum, with an explicit extremal sequence proving sharpness
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Weighted Output-Selection Gap
Output-Selection Certificate Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate descent does not generally certify a predetermined final output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An aggregate guarantee \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k r_k^2\le B\), with \(a_k>0\), need not bound a prescribed residual \(r_j\) by \(B/\sum_{k<N}a_k\). For example, with \(a_k=1\), choose \(r_{N-1}^2=B\) and \(r_k=0\) for \(k<N-1\). The aggregate inequality holds, but \(r_{N-1}^2=B\), whereas the sampled-iterate scale is \(B/N\). Thus best-iterate or randomized-output certificates cannot be relabeled as last-iterate certificates without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate residual bound may coexist with a final residual N times larger than the randomized-output scale.
assumptions_latex: Only the aggregate inequality is assumed; no residual monotonicity is imposed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit finite-sequence counterexample verifies the selection gap

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit sequence correctly demonstrates the output-selection gap and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no authoritative locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique or Set-Valued Proximal Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a single-valued proximal residual when a proximal subproblem has multiple minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(\lambda>0\), define \[P_\lambda f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^d}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\}.\] If this subproblem has two or more minimizers, then \(P_\lambda f(x)\) is set-valued and \(\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda f(x))\) is a set rather than a single residual vector. For example, let \(d=1\), let \(f(y)=-\tfrac12y^2\) for \(y\in[-1,1]\) and \(f(y)=+\infty\) otherwise, and take \(\lambda=1\). Then \[P_1f(0)=[-1,1].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple proximal minimizers make the proximal mapping and its associated residual set-valued; in the displayed example every point of the interval is a proximal minimizer at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(\lambda>0\).
The proximal minimum at the point under consideration is attained by more than one point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\lambda f(x)\) and \(\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda f(x))\) are set-valued; in the example, \(P_1f(0)=[-1,1]\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Set-Valued Mappings p. 148

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Set-Valued Mappings p. 148

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal subproblem can have a finite infimum but no proximal point because minimizing sequences escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=e^{-y}-\tfrac12y^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), take \(\lambda=1\), and center the proximal subproblem at \(x=0\). Then \[f(y)+\frac12|y|^2=e^{-y}.\] Hence \[f_1(0)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}e^{-y}=0,\qquad P_1f(0)=\varnothing,\] because the infimum is approached only as \(y\to+\infty\). Thus finiteness of the envelope value does not imply attainment or existence of a proximal residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal objective may have a finite infimum approached only at infinity, leaving the proximal map empty even though the envelope value is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite but Unattained Proximal Value
Ill-Posed Proximal Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of proximal existence when quadratic regularization does not dominate negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=-c\|y\|^2\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), where \(c>0\). The proximal objective at \(x=0\) is \[f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y\|^2=\left(\frac{1}{2\lambda}-c\right)\|y\|^2.\] If \(\lambda>1/(2c)\), this objective tends to \(-\infty\) as \(\|y\|\to\infty\). Hence the proximal subproblem has no minimizer, the Moreau envelope equals \(-\infty\) at zero, and no proximal residual is defined there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If negative curvature dominates the proximal quadratic, the subproblem is unbounded below and produces no residual.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit quadratic calculation establishes unboundedness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic calculation and conclusions are correct, and an explicit counterexample is suitable for this failure container. An authoritative proximal well-posedness locator is still required.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Nondifferentiability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonunique proximal point coinciding with a cusp of the Moreau envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be given by \(f(y)=-\tfrac12y^2\) for \(y\in[-1,1]\) and \(f(y)=+\infty\) otherwise. With \(\lambda=1\), its Moreau envelope is \[f_1(x)=\min_{|y|\le1}\left\{-\frac12y^2+\frac12(y-x)^2\right\}=\frac12x^2-|x|.\] Hence \(f_1\) is not differentiable at \(x=0\), and the proximal set there is \[P_1f(0)=[-1,1].\] Thus \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda f(x))\) cannot be interpreted as a single-vector gradient at this point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the displayed example, the proximal set at zero is the whole interval and the Moreau envelope has a cusp there, so the usual single-vector envelope-gradient identity fails.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct minimization gives the displayed envelope, proximal set, and cusp

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative error budget that preserves strict residual descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \[E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-a\|G(x_k)\|^2+e_k,\qquad 0\le e_k\le\sigma a\|G(x_k)\|^2,\] where \(a>0\) and \(0\le\sigma<1\), then \[E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-(1-\sigma)a\|G(x_k)\|^2.\] If \(E\) is bounded below, then \(\sum_k\|G(x_k)\|^2<\infty\), \(G(x_k)\to0\), and \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|G(x_k)\|^2\le\frac{E(x_0)-\inf E}{(1-\sigma)aN}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error consuming strictly less than all nominal decrease is absorbed into the descent coefficient.
assumptions_latex: The displayed recursion and relative-error bound hold with \(0\le\sigma<1\).

notation.meaning: fraction of nominal descent consumed by error

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Error Absorption Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness example for the nonvanishing residual floor allowed by persistent additive error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), \(G(x)=x\), and \(x_k=1\) for every \(k\). For any \(a>0\), choosing \(e_k=a\) gives \[E(x_{k+1})=E(x_k)-a|G(x_k)|^2+e_k.\] Thus \(e_k\le\bar e\) with \(\bar e=a\), but \(|G(x_k)|^2=1=\bar e/a\) for all \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant iterate can attain the persistent-error floor exactly, so bounded nonsummable errors do not force stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Error Floor Is Attainable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of finite total additive error in an envelope-descent recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-a\|G(x_k)\|^2+e_k\), where \(a>0\), \(e_k\ge0\), \(\inf E> -\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty\), then \[a\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|G(x_k)\|^2\le E(x_0)-\inf E+\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty.\] Consequently, \(G(x_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable additive errors make the squared residuals summable and force the full residual sequence to vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable-Error Residual Convergence
Inexactness Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent proximal errors create a nonvanishing stationarity floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an inexact envelope method satisfies \[E(x_{k+1})\le E(x_k)-a\|G(x_k)\|^2+e_k,\qquad a>0,\quad e_k\ge0,\] and let \(\Delta=E(x_0)-\inf E\). Then \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|G(x_k)\|^2\le\frac{\Delta+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e_k}{aN}.\] Consequently, summable errors preserve convergence of the best residual to zero, whereas persistent errors with \(e_k\le\bar e\) yield only the asymptotic bound \(\liminf_k\|G(x_k)\|^2\le\bar e/a\); vanishing stationarity is not certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulated inexactness enters the residual budget additively; persistent error leaves a nonzero stationarity floor.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inexact descent inequality holds with \(a>0\) and \(e_k\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: telescoping shows additive accumulation and the persistent-error floor

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The aggregate bound, summable-error consequence, and liminf bound under e_k≤bar e are mathematically correct and fit the failure-boundary container, but no authoritative inexact-method locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient decrease at the smoothness parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialization of the nonconvex composite sufficient-decrease inequality to the positive parameter L=L_f.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let F=f+g and suppose L_f>0. For every x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),
\[
F(x)-F\bigl(T_{L_f}^{f,g}(x)\bigr)\geq \frac{1}{2L_f}\,\lVert G_{L_f}^{f,g}(x)\rVert^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the composite proximal-gradient assumptions, when the positive proximal parameter is chosen as L_f, the objective decreases by at least the squared proximal-gradient-mapping norm divided by 2L_f.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records component regularity, domain compatibility, smoothness, and attainment without assuming convexity of f or F.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{E}\). Assume that \(g:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex; \(f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and closed; \(\operatorname{dom}(f)\) is convex; \(\operatorname{dom}(g)\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}(f))\); and \(f\) is \(L_f\)-smooth on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}(f))\). A minimizer exists; the solution set and attained optimal value are denoted X* and F_opt.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the majorization-minimization construction and its convex-composite proximal-gradient specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A majorization-minimization iteration for $\varphi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ has the form
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\widehat\varphi(x,x^k),
\]
where $\widehat\varphi(\cdot,y)$ is convex, $\widehat\varphi(x,y)\geq\varphi(x)$ for all $x$, and $\widehat\varphi(y,y)=\varphi(y)$. If $\nabla f$ is $L$-Lipschitz and $0<\lambda\leq1/L$, then
\[
\widehat f_\lambda(x,y)=f(y)+\nabla f(y)^T(x-y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-y\|_2^2
\]
majorizes $f$. For closed proper convex $g$,
\[
q_\lambda(x,y)=\widehat f_\lambda(x,y)+g(x)
\]
majorizes $f+g$, and
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_x q_\lambda(x,x^k)
=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}\!\left(x^k-\lambda\nabla f(x^k)\right).
\]
Thus the proximal-gradient update is the corresponding majorization-minimization step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Majorization-minimization repeatedly minimizes a convex upper model that touches the objective at the reference point. For an L-smooth term f and a step no larger than 1/L, the regularized first-order model majorizes f; adding a closed proper convex g gives a surrogate whose minimizer is exactly the proximal-gradient update.
assumptions_latex: \widehat\varphi(\cdot,y)\text{ is convex for every reference point }y
f\text{ is differentiable and }\nabla f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz}
g\text{ is closed, proper, and convex in the composite specialization}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cocoercivity and Lipschitz Continuity of the Convex Proximal-Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative regularity of the proximal-gradient mapping in the convex composite regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f$ be convex and $L_f$-smooth on $\mathbb E$, where $L_f>0$, and let $g:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]$ be proper, closed, and convex. Then, for every $x,y\in\mathbb E$, $$\langle G_{L_f}(x)-G_{L_f}(y),x-y\rangle\ge \frac{3}{4L_f}\|G_{L_f}(x)-G_{L_f}(y)\|^2.$$ Thus $(3/(4L_f))G_{L_f}$ is firmly nonexpansive, and $$\|G_{L_f}(x)-G_{L_f}(y)\|\le \frac{4L_f}{3}\|x-y\|.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex Lf-smooth function and a proper closed convex composite term, the proximal-gradient mapping at parameter Lf is 3/(4Lf)-cocoercive. Its scaling by 3/(4Lf) is firmly nonexpansive, and the mapping is Lipschitz with constant 4Lf/3.

g:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex composite proximal gradient, including its fixed-step rate, larger convergence interval, and majorization boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For closed proper convex functions $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and $g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$, with $f$ differentiable, the proximal-gradient iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda^k g}\!\left(x^k-\lambda^k\nabla f(x^k)\right),\qquad \lambda^k>0.
\]
If $\nabla f$ is $L$-Lipschitz and $\lambda^k=\lambda\in(0,1/L]$, the method converges at rate $O(1/k)$. Fixed steps $\lambda\in(0,2/L)$ also yield convergence, although steps above $1/L$ no longer give the majorization-minimization interpretation. When $L$ is unknown, a line search may select the step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed proper convex composite objective, proximal gradient takes a gradient step on the differentiable term and then applies the proximal map of the other term. With an L-Lipschitz gradient and a fixed step at most 1/L, the stated rate is O(1/k). Fixed steps below 2/L still converge, but those above 1/L lose the majorization-minimization interpretation. A line search can be used when L is unknown.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex proximal-gradient descent, residual complexity, and stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded convergence theorem for proximal gradient under the source's named Assumption 10.1, covering both the specified constant curvature parameter and backtracking procedure B1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=f(x)+g(x)\) on \(\mathbb E\), suppose Assumption 10.1 holds, and let \(\{x^k\}_{k\ge 0}\) be generated by the proximal-gradient method for \(\min_{x\in\mathbb E}F(x)\). Use either \(L_k=\bar L\in(L_f/2,\infty)\), or backtracking procedure B1 with \(s>0\), \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and \(\eta>1\). Define
\[
d=\begin{cases}\bar L,&\text{constant parameter},\\s,&\text{backtracking},\end{cases}
\qquad
M=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\bar L-L_f/2}{\bar L^2},&\text{constant parameter},\\[2mm]\dfrac{\gamma}{\max\{s,\eta L_f/[2(1-\gamma)]\}},&\text{backtracking}.\end{cases}
\]
Then \(\{F(x^k)\}\) is nonincreasing, and \(F(x^{k+1})<F(x^k)\) if and only if \(x^k\) is not stationary. Moreover, \(G_d(x^k)\to0\), and for every \(k\ge0\),
\[
\min_{0\le n\le k}\|G_d(x^n)\|\le \frac{\sqrt{F(x^0)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}}}{\sqrt{M(k+1)}}.
\]
Every limit point of \(\{x^k\}\) is a stationary point of \(\min_{x\in\mathbb E}F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 10.1, proximal gradient with either the specified constant curvature parameter or B1 backtracking produces nonincreasing objective values, with strict decrease exactly when the current iterate is nonstationary. The prescribed proximal-gradient residual converges to zero, its smallest norm through iteration k satisfies the stated inverse-square-root bound, and every limit point is stationary for the composite problem on the source space.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\ge0}\text{ is generated by proximal gradient for }\min_{x\in\mathbb E}F(x)
L_k=\bar L\in(L_f/2,\infty)\quad\text{or B1 is used with }s>0,\ \gamma\in(0,1),\ \eta>1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k),\quad F(x^{k+1})<F(x^k)\iff x^k\text{ is nonstationary};\qquad G_d(x^k)\to0;\qquad \forall k\ge0,\ \min_{0\le n\le k}\|G_d(x^n)\|\le\frac{\sqrt{F(x^0)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}}}{\sqrt{M(k+1)}};\qquad \text{every limit point of }\{x^k\}\text{ is stationary for }\min_{x\in\mathbb E}F(x).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Composite Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex regime for proximal-gradient residual and envelope calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and continuously differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. The convex composite regime consists of minimizing \(F\). For \(0<t<1/L\), define \(T_t(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x-t\nabla f(x))\) and \(G_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-T_t(x))\). Then \(G_t(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\), equivalently \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth convex term plus a proper closed convex term forms the convex composite regime; zeros of its proximal-gradient mapping are exactly global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, continuously differentiable, and \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating global convex-composite optimality certificates from nonconvex stationarity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The operative boundary is convexity of the total objective \(F=f+g\), not convexity of a chosen term in isolation. If \(F\) is convex, \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\) is necessary and sufficient for global minimality. Without total convexity it is generally only a stationarity condition: for \(g=0\) and \(f(u)=(u^2-1)^2\), \(u=0\) is stationary but is a strict local maximizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal gradient specialized to a closed convex constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(g=\delta_C\), where \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise. Since \(\operatorname{prox}_{t\delta_C}=P_C\) for every \(t>0\), the proximal-gradient step for \(f+\delta_C\) is exactly projected gradient: \(x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-t_k
abla f(x^k))\). Its residual is \(G_{t_k}(x^k)=t_k^{-1}(x^k-P_C(x^k-t_k
abla f(x^k)))\), and its zeros are precisely solutions of \(0\in
abla f(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the indicator of a closed convex set turns the proximal-gradient update and residual exactly into projected gradient and its stationarity mapping.

children.title: Backtracking Variants
children.top_down_role: Proximal-gradient variants using iterative stepsize contraction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination and contraction complexity of the basic quadratic-majorization backtracking loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L>0\). For every \(t\le L^{-1}\), the descent lemma ensures that the quadratic-majorization test holds at \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x-t\nabla f(x))\). Thus, for \(t_j=\beta^j\bar t\), the first accepted index satisfies
\[
j_*\le\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(\bar tL)}{\log(1/\beta)}\right\rceil\right\},
\qquad
t_{j_*}\ge\min\{\bar t,\beta/L\}.
\]
Hence uniformly positive initial trials yield uniformly positive accepted stepsizes whenever one common positive Lipschitz constant applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic-majorization backtracking terminates after finitely many contractions, with an explicit contraction count and a positive lower bound on the accepted stepsize.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, with \(L>0\), on a convex region containing every trial segment.
\(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: Index of the first accepted trial

review_flags: No supporting locator was supplied; this is the standard descent-lemma termination bound for geometric proximal-gradient backtracking.
The explicit assumption L>0 is required by the logarithmic bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Backtracking Termination
Backtracking Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric backtracking on the proximal-gradient trial stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^k\), trial stepsize \(\bar t_k>0\), contraction \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(F=f+g\), initialize \(t=\bar t_k\). Form \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x^k-t\nabla f(x^k))\). While \(f(z)>f(x^k)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),z-x^k\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert z-x^k\rVert^2\), replace \(t\leftarrow\beta t\) and recompute \(z\). On acceptance, set \(t_k=t\) and \(x^{k+1}=z\). Stop when a prescribed residual tolerance, such as \(\lVert t_k^{-1}(x^k-x^{k+1})\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly contract the trial stepsize until the smooth term satisfies its local quadratic upper model, then accept the resulting proximal-gradient point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz gradient.
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}(x^k-t_k\nabla f(x^k))\quad\text{with the quadratic-model acceptance inequality satisfied}.\]

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable near the trial segment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo relaxation along a nonzero proximal-gradient displacement; contraction mechanics and acceptance-test taxonomy remain sibling-owned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}(x^k-t_k\nabla f(x^k))\) and \(d^k=z^k-x^k\). If \(d^k\ne0\), choose the smallest \(m_k\ge0\) such that, for \(\alpha_k=\beta^{m_k}\), \(F(x^k+\alpha_kd^k)\le F(x^k)-\sigma\alpha_kt_k^{-1}\|d^k\|^2\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kd^k\). Convexity of \(g\) gives \(F'(x^k;d^k)\le-t_k^{-1}\|d^k\|^2\), so such an index exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a proximal-gradient displacement and shorten it until composite Armijo decrease holds; convexity of the proximal term guarantees finite acceptance for every nonzero displacement.

\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(d^k=z^k-x^k\), choose \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in[0,1]}F(x^k+\alpha d^k)\) and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kd^k\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For a current point \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a trial stepsize \(t>0\), and \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x-t\nabla f(x))\), two monotone acceptance regimes are the majorization test \(f(z)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),z-x\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert z-x\rVert^2\) and the sufficient-decrease test \(F(z)\leq F(x)-\frac{c}{2t}\lVert z-x\rVert^2\) for a prescribed \(c\in(0,1]\). The majorization test, together with proximal optimality and convexity of \(g\), implies the sufficient-decrease test with \(c=1\), and hence with every \(c\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-gradient trial point may be accepted through smooth-term majorization or explicit composite-objective decrease. Under convexity of the nonsmooth term, majorization yields the unit sufficient-decrease constant.

children.title: Variable-Metric Proximal Gradient
children.top_down_role: Proximal-gradient variants using changing quadratic geometries or preconditioners.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal-gradient iteration in a uniformly bounded positive-definite changing metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose symmetric \(H_k\) with \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\), and let \(x^{k+1}\) be the unique minimizer of \(g(z)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),z-x^k\rangle+\tfrac12\|z-x^k\|_{H_k}^2\). Equivalently, \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{H_k}_g(x^k-H_k^{-1}\nabla f(x^k))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the smooth term and minimize the resulting composite model in a uniformly positive-definite metric that may change each iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Proximal Gradient

assumptions_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) exactly solves the metric proximal-gradient subproblem.

notation.meaning: explicit stationarity subgradient at the new iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable stationarity bound at an exact variable-metric update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(v^{k+1}\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\) from the subproblem condition \(v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^k)+H_k(x^{k+1}-x^k)=0\). Then \(s^{k+1}=v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^{k+1})\in\partial(f+g)(x^{k+1})\), and \(\|s^{k+1}\|\le(M+L)\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement of an exact metric step controls an explicit composite-stationarity residual at the new iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Step Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The metric subproblem is solved exactly and \(F\) is bounded below for the asymptotic conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)-\frac{m-L}{2}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,\quad\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2<\infty,\] \[0\in\nabla f(\bar x)+\partial g(\bar x)\quad\text{for every accumulation point }\bar x.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent and stationary-cluster convergence under uniform metric domination of smooth curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the exact metric update, let \(d^k=x^{k+1}-x^k\). If \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) and \(m>L\), then \(F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)-\tfrac12(\|d^k\|_{H_k}^2-L\|d^k\|^2)\le F(x^k)-\tfrac{m-L}{2}\|d^k\|^2\). If \(F\) is bounded below, the steps are square summable and every accumulation point is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every metric uniformly dominates the smooth curvature, exact variable-metric proximal-gradient steps decrease the objective and every cluster point is stationary.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Descent and Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite metric scaling of the composite proximal-gradient subproblem, including Newton and constrained-Newton special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(H_k=H_k^\top\succ0\), define
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\ell(x;x_k)+h(x)+\frac12(x-x_k)^\top H_k(x-x_k)\right\}.
\]
Choosing \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\succ0\) gives proximal Newton, while \(H_k=\alpha_k^{-1}I\) gives ordinary proximal gradient. If \(h=\delta_X\), the Hessian choice gives constrained Newton; if additionally \(X=\mathbb R^n\), it gives classical Newton. If \(f\) is a positive-definite quadratic and \(H_k=\nabla^2f\), the unit-step method solves the composite problem in one iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric proximal gradient replaces the scalar quadratic regularizer by a positive-definite matrix. A Hessian metric produces proximal Newton, an inverse-stepsize identity metric recovers proximal gradient, and an indicator term produces constrained Newton. For a positive-definite quadratic smooth term with the exact Hessian, a unit step reaches the composite optimum in one iteration. Diagonal and quasi-Newton metrics are possible, but descent and superlinear convergence require additional conditions not specified in the extract.

children.title: Inexact Proximal Gradient
children.top_down_role: Variants permitting approximate proximal or gradient information.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two standard, verifiable inexact proximal-gradient subproblem criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Q_k(z)=g(z)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),z-x^k\rangle+(2t_k)^{-1}\|z-x^k\|^2\) and \(p^k=\operatorname*{argmin}Q_k\). A residual-inexact update admits \(v^{k+1}\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\) with \(\|v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^k)+t_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k\). An objective-gap update satisfies \(Q_k(x^{k+1})\le Q_k(p^k)+\delta_k\), which implies \(\|x^{k+1}-p^k\|\le\sqrt{2t_k\delta_k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal-gradient step can be certified by a subproblem optimality residual or by an objective gap; the latter bounds distance to the exact step.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual and Objective-Gap Inexact Updates

assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of finite-dimensional convex inexact forward-backward iteration with summable subproblem residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each update admits \(v^{k+1}\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\) and \(r^{k+1}\) such that \(v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^k)+t^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)=r^{k+1}\). If \(f\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, \(g\) is proper closed convex, \(0<t<2/L\), the solution set is nonempty, and \(\sum_k\|r^{k+1}\|<\infty\), then \(x^k\) converges to a minimizer of \(f+g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the convex fixed-step regime, summable proximal optimality residuals preserve convergence to a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable-Residual Convergence
Inexact Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient update solved to a verifiable first-order residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^k\), stepsize \(t_k>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), choose \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname{dom}g\) and \(v^{k+1}\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\) such that \(\lVert v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^k)+t_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\). This replaces exact minimization of the proximal subproblem by an approximate first-order condition. Stop when both the step residual \(t_k^{-1}\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\) and the allowed subproblem error meet prescribed tolerances; otherwise output the generated sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal subproblem may be solved approximately when its first-order residual is bounded by a declared tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-compatible relative-error calibration for an inexact variable-metric proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d^k=x^{k+1}-x^k\) and \(r^{k+1}=v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^k)+H_kd^k\). A scale-compatible relative-error condition is \(\|r^{k+1}\|_{H_k^{-1}}\le\eta_k\|d^k\|_{H_k}\). Under \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\), both sides are uniformly comparable with their Euclidean counterparts; without uniform spectral bounds, changing geometry can distort the reported error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure the subproblem residual in the dual metric and the update in the primal metric, with uniform spectral bounds preventing metric-induced distortion.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Compatible Relative Error
Metric–Inexactness Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-scaled relative-error condition coupling variable geometry and proximal inexactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\), set \(d^k=x^{k+1}-x^k\), and choose \(v^{k+1}\in\partial g(x^{k+1})\). Define the metric subproblem residual \(r^{k+1}=v^{k+1}+\nabla f(x^k)+H_kd^k\). A scale-compatible relative-error condition is \(\lVert r^{k+1}\rVert_{H_k^{-1}}\leq\eta_k\lVert d^k\rVert_{H_k}\), where \(0\leq\eta_k<1\). Uniform spectral bounds make this condition comparable to Euclidean residual control and prevent changes of metric from artificially shrinking the reported inexactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure subproblem error in the dual metric and compare it with step size in the primal metric, under uniform spectral bounds.

children.title: Inertial Proximal Gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-step proximal-gradient method with extrapolation from the preceding displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^{-1}=x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\), stepsizes \(t_k>0\), and inertial parameters \(\beta_k\geq0\), form \(y^k=x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1})\) and update \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}(y^k-t_k\nabla f(y^k))\). A monotone safeguarded variant rejects or restarts the extrapolation when its prescribed descent test fails. Stop when \(\lVert t_k^{-1}(y^k-x^{k+1})\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(x^{k+1}\); without a tolerance, output the generated sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolate from the previous displacement, then take a proximal-gradient step at the extrapolated point, optionally restarting when descent fails.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

children.title: Accelerated Proximal Gradient

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
Each block performs \(m\) exact classical accelerated iterations and then resets momentum.

notation.meaning: iterate at the beginning of restart block j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic restart of classical acceleration under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(u^j\), run \(m\) classical accelerated proximal-gradient iterations with stepsize \(1/L\), reset momentum, and call the output \(u^{j+1}\). Strong convexity and the convex accelerated bound give \(F(u^{j+1})-F(x^\star)\le q_m(F(u^j)-F(x^\star))\), where \(q_m=4L/[\mu(m+1)^2]\). Thus \(m+1>2\sqrt{L/\mu}\) yields geometric block convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-period restart converts the accelerated convex rate into geometric convergence for strongly convex composite objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Periodic-Restart Acceleration

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical FISTA recurrence and objective-gap rate for fixed-step convex composite minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0=y^0\) and \(q_0=1\). For \(k\ge0\), set \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L}(y^k-L^{-1}\nabla f(y^k))\), \(q_{k+1}=(1+\sqrt{1+4q_k^2})/2\), and \(y^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\frac{q_k-1}{q_{k+1}}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Then, for \(k\ge1\), \(F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\le2L\|x^0-x^\star\|^2/(k+1)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical accelerated proximal gradient uses Nesterov extrapolation and achieves a quadratic-in-iteration objective-gap rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Accelerated Proximal Gradient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schur Stability Does Not Imply Objective Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar quadratic example separating asymptotic momentum stability from one-step objective descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\), \(g=0\), and apply \(y_k=x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\), \(x_{k+1}=y_k-\alpha y_k\) with \(\alpha=\beta=1/2\). Then \(x_{k+1}=\tfrac34x_k-\tfrac14x_{k-1}\), whose characteristic roots have modulus \(1/2\), so \(x_k\to0\) for every initialization. For \(x_{-1}=-1\) and \(x_0=1/10\), however, \(x_1=13/40\) and \(f(x_1)=169/3200>1/200=f(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Schur-stable scalar inertial gradient recurrence can increase the objective on an individual step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to0\) for every initialization, while the displayed initialization satisfies \(f(x_1)>f(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Schur Stability Does Not Imply Objective Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Momentum Stability for Positive-Definite Quadratics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multidimensional extension of scalar Schur stability through orthogonal Hessian modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx\), where \(Q=Q^\top\succ0\), let \(g=0\), and consider \[y_k=x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1}),\qquad x_{k+1}=y_k-\alpha Qy_k,\] with \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\). For each \(\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(Q)\), set \(q_\lambda=1-\alpha\lambda\). Then \(x_k\to0\) for every initialization if and only if, for every \(\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(Q)\), \[|q_\lambda\beta|<1,\qquad 1-q_\lambda>0,\qquad 1+q_\lambda(1+2\beta)>0.\] Equivalently, every polynomial \(r^2-q_\lambda(1+\beta)r+q_\lambda\beta\) is Schur stable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Momentum on a positive-definite quadratic is stable exactly when the scalar Jury conditions hold for every Hessian eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to0\) for every initial state exactly under the stated uniform spectral Jury conditions.

notation.meaning: forward-step multiplier for the eigenmode with eigenvalue lambda

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Momentum Stability for Positive-Definite Quadratics
Momentum Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar-quadratic stability boundary for an inertial forward step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\lambda x^2/2\), \(g=0\), \(\lambda>0\), and consider \(y_k=x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\), \(x_{k+1}=y_k-\alpha f'(y_k)\). With \(q=1-\alpha\lambda\), the iterates satisfy \(x_{k+1}=q(1+\beta)x_k-q\beta x_{k-1}\). They converge to zero for every initialization exactly when the roots of \(r^2-q(1+\beta)r+q\beta\) lie in the open unit disk, equivalently \(|q\beta|<1\), \(1-q>0\), and \(1+q(1+2\beta)>0\). Equality in any condition is a stability boundary; violation permits a nondecaying trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar quadratic, momentum is stable exactly under three Jury inequalities. Crossing any boundary produces a characteristic root of modulus at least one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to0\) for every initialization if and only if \(|q\beta|<1\), \(1-q>0\), and \(1+q(1+2\beta)>0\).\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth reduction and stationarity characterization of the proximal-gradient mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the smooth special case and characterizes stationarity by vanishing of the mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let L>0 and let g_0\equiv0. Then
\[
G_L^{f,g_0}(x)=\nabla f(x)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f).
\]
Moreover, for every x^*\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f),
\[
G_L^{f,g}(x^*)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x^*\text{ is stationary for }\min_x\{f(x)+g(x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the nonsmooth term is zero, the proximal-gradient mapping equals the ordinary gradient. For the composite problem, a point in the interior of the domain of f is stationary if and only if its proximal-gradient mapping vanishes.

knowledge_statements.title: Forward-Backward Fixed-Point Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean residual for a convex nonsmooth term and smooth forward step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(\alpha>0\), define the forward-backward operator and its residual by \[T_\alpha(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g}\bigl(x-\alpha\nabla f(x)\bigr),\qquad R_\alpha(x)=x-T_\alpha(x).\] The scaled proximal-gradient residual is \(G_\alpha(x)=\alpha^{-1}R_\alpha(x)\). Moreover, \(R_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\), so its zeros are precisely composite stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forward-backward residual is the displacement from a point to one proximal-gradient update; it vanishes exactly at composite stationary points.

Stepsize-Dependent Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling and zero-set behavior of Euclidean forward-backward residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\alpha>0\), let \(R_\alpha(x)=x-\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g}(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))\) and \(G_\alpha(x)=R_\alpha(x)/\alpha\). The two residual conventions obey the exact scaling identity \(R_\alpha(x)=\alpha G_\alpha(x)\). Although their magnitudes depend on \(\alpha\), their zero set does not: for every positive stepsize, \[R_\alpha(x)=0\iff G_\alpha(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x).\] Hence residual tolerances must specify whether the scaled or unscaled convention is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the stepsize changes residual magnitude, while every positive stepsize retains the same stationary zero set. Scaled and unscaled residuals differ by the stepsize.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite stationarity certificate at a variable-metric forward-backward trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y=T_H(x)\) solve the metric forward-backward subproblem and let \(r=x-y\). If \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm, then \[w:=Hr+
abla f(y)-
abla f(x)\in\partial(f+g)(y),\] and \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(f+g)(y))\le\|w\|\le(\|H\|_2+L)\|r\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric displacement yields an explicit subgradient at the trial point controlled by the metric size and gradient Lipschitz constant.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable with an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Well-Definedness without Positive Definiteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness for a singular metric and unboundedness for a negative-curvature metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g=0\). If \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), then the metric subproblem at \(x\) minimizes \(\tfrac12(z_1-x_1)^2\), so every \(z\) with \(z_1=x_1\) is a minimizer and \(T_H(x)\) is not single-valued. If \(H=-I\), the objective \(-\tfrac12\|z-x\|^2\) is unbounded below. Thus symmetry alone, or positive semidefiniteness without definiteness, does not ensure a well-defined single-valued residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular metric can make the metric step nonunique, while negative metric curvature can make the subproblem unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\succ0 is essential for unconditional existence and uniqueness of the metric proximal point in this setting.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Well-Definedness without Positive Definiteness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent representations of a positive-definite metric forward-backward point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H=H^\top\succ0\), define \(\operatorname{prox}^{H}_{g}(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_z\{g(z)+\tfrac12\|z-u\|_H^2\}\). The metric forward-backward point satisfies \[T_H(x)=\operatorname{prox}^{H}_{g}\bigl(x-H^{-1}\nabla f(x)\bigr).\] With \(u=H^{1/2}x\) and \(\bar g(v)=g(H^{-1/2}v)\), it equivalently satisfies \[H^{1/2}T_H(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\bar g}\bigl(u-H^{-1/2}\nabla f(x)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric forward-backward step is a metric proximal map and becomes an ordinary Euclidean proximal step after a square-root coordinate transformation.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(f\) is differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_H(x)=\operatorname{prox}^{H}_{g}(x-H^{-1}\nabla f(x)), with the stated Euclidean coordinate form.

notation.meaning: symmetric positive-definite square root of H

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Proximal and Euclidean Coordinate Representations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical variable-metric forward-backward step and its primal and metric-scaled residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^\top\succ0\). Define \[T_H(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{g(z)+\langle\nabla f(x),z-x\rangle+\tfrac12\|z-x\|_H^2\right\},\quad R_H(x)=x-T_H(x),\quad G_H(x)=HR_H(x).\] If \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, then \(T_H(x)\) is single-valued and \[R_H(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow G_H(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric defines a unique forward-backward point; both its primal displacement and metric-scaled residual vanish exactly at composite stationary points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward residual induced by a symmetric positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and write \(\|u\|_H^2=u^\top Hu\). Define \[T_H(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z}\left\{g(z)+\langle\nabla f(x),z-x\rangle+\tfrac12\|z-x\|_H^2\right\},\quad R_H(x)=x-T_H(x),\quad G_H(x)=H R_H(x).\] When \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(T_H(x)\) is single-valued and \(R_H(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Renormalization Across Geometries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-invariant normalization of primal and dual metric residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H=H^\top\succ0\), let \(r=R_H(x)\) and \(v=Hr=G_H(x)\). Primal and dual normalizations coincide exactly: \[\|r\|_H=\|v\|_{H^{-1}}.\] More generally, if \(mI\preceq H\preceq MI\), then \[\sqrt m\,\|r\|\le\|r\|_H\le\sqrt M\,\|r\|,\qquad M^{-1/2}\|v\|\le\|v\|_{H^{-1}}\le m^{-1/2}\|v\|.\] These identities provide the conversion factors required when residual tolerances are reported in Euclidean, primal-metric, or dual-metric geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal metric residual and its metric-scaled dual form have identical intrinsic norm. Spectral bounds convert either normalization to Euclidean units.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Length Error Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*=\{x:0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\}\) be nonempty and fix \(\alpha>0\). A local step-length error bound holds on a set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) if there exists \(\kappa>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\kappa\|x-T_\alpha(x)\|\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] Equivalently, in the scaled convention, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\kappa\alpha\|G_\alpha(x)\|\). The condition is local when \(U\) is a neighborhood of a specified stationary point or solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step-length error bound controls distance to stationarity by the displacement generated by one proximal-gradient step, locally or on a specified region.

Quadratic-Growth Equivalences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equivalence for convex piecewise linear-quadratic composite objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex quadratic, let \(g\) be proper, closed, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic, and suppose \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\ne\varnothing\). Fix \(0<\alpha<1/L\), where \(L\) is a Lipschitz constant for \(\nabla f\). Near \(X^*\), the following are equivalent, possibly with different positive constants: \[F(x)-F^*\ge\tfrac\mu2\operatorname{dist}^2(x,X^*),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\le\kappa\|x-T_\alpha(x)\|.\] Thus local quadratic growth and a local proximal-gradient step-length error bound characterize the same regularity in this convex piecewise linear-quadratic setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Linear-Convergence Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract local contraction consequence of sufficient decrease and a residual-to-gap estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have finite minimum \(F^*=\min F\) and nonempty solution set \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}F\). Let \(T_\alpha\) be the forward-backward operator, let \(R_\alpha(x)=x-T_\alpha(x)\), and generate \(x_{k+1}=T_\alpha(x_k)\). Suppose the iterates remain in a neighborhood \(U\) of \(X^*\) and, for constants \(0<c<C\), satisfy \[F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-c\|R_\alpha(x_k)\|^2,\qquad F(x_k)-F^*\le C\|R_\alpha(x_k)\|^2.\] Then \[F(x_{k+1})-F^*\le\left(1-\frac cC\right)\bigl(F(x_k)-F^*\bigr).\] Hence the objective gaps converge locally \(Q\)-linearly. If, in addition, \(F(x)-F^*\ge(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}^2(x,X^*)\) on \(U\) for some \(\mu>0\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)\) converges \(R\)-linearly to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease and an upper bound of the objective gap by the squared residual yield a local geometric contraction of objective gaps. Local quadratic growth additionally yields R-linear convergence of distance to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_{k+1})-F^*\le(1-c/C)(F(x_k)-F^*)\); under local quadratic growth, \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X^*)\) converges \(R\)-linearly to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Objective Contraction Implies Finite-Length Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trajectory consequence supplementing the accepted objective-gap contraction theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=T_\alpha(x_k)\), let \(R_\alpha(x)=x-T_\alpha(x)\), and suppose for \(c>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(\Delta_0\ge0\) that \[F(x_k)-F^*\le\Delta_0q^k,\qquad F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-c\|R_\alpha(x_k)\|^2.\] Then \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\le\sqrt{\Delta_0/c}\,q^{k/2}\), the sequence has finite length, and it converges to a point \(\bar x\) satisfying \[\|x_k-\bar x\|\le\frac{\sqrt{\Delta_0/c}}{1-\sqrt q}\,q^{k/2}.\] If \(T_\alpha\) is continuous at \(\bar x\), then \(R_\alpha(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric objective-gap decay plus residual sufficient decrease gives finite trajectory length and R-linear convergence to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty\) and \(\|x_k-\bar x\|\le\frac{\sqrt{\Delta_0/c}}{1-\sqrt q}q^{k/2}\); continuity of \(T_\alpha\) at \(\bar x\) implies \(R_\alpha(\bar x)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient-Decrease Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable descent inequality for a possibly nonconvex smooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(g\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(x^+\) be a global minimizer of \[z\mapsto g(z)+\langle\nabla f(x),z-x\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z-x\|^2.\] Then \[F(x^+)\le F(x)-\frac{1-\alpha L}{2\alpha}\|x^+-x\|^2.\] For \(0<\alpha<1/L\), the positive coefficient and the observed step provide a sufficient-decrease certificate. Equivalently, the guaranteed decrease is at least \(\alpha(1-\alpha L)\|G_\alpha(x)\|^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally solved proximal model guarantees objective decrease when the stepsize is below the reciprocal smoothness constant; the observed step quantifies that decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Stepsize Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform stepsize range ensuring proximal sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and every proximal model is solved globally. A fixed stepsize \(\alpha\) lies in the strict descent regime when \(0<\alpha<1/L\). Then every update satisfies \[F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-c_\alpha\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\qquad c_\alpha=\frac{1-\alpha L}{2\alpha}>0.\] More generally, choosing \(\alpha\in[\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha]\) with \(0<\underline\alpha\le\overline\alpha<1/L\) gives the uniform certificate \(c_\alpha\ge(1-\overline\alpha L)/(2\overline\alpha)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any fixed stepsize strictly below the reciprocal smoothness constant guarantees descent. A compact interval below that threshold gives a uniform decrease constant.
assumptions_latex: Each proximal model is solved to global optimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration proximal-trial overhead and accepted-stepsize floor for geometric backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar\alpha=(1-\sigma)/L\). If \(j_k\) is the number of reductions before acceptance, then
\[
j_k\le \max\left\{0,\left\lceil
\frac{\log(\alpha_k^{(0)}/\bar\alpha)}{\log(1/\tau)}
\right\rceil\right\},
\qquad
\alpha_k\ge\min\{\alpha_k^{(0)},\tau\bar\alpha\}.
\]
Consequently, bounds \(0<\underline\alpha\le\alpha_k^{(0)}\le\overline\alpha<\infty\) give a uniform positive lower bound on accepted stepsizes and a uniform bound on the number \(j_k+1\) of proximal trials per iteration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Failure Beyond the Nonconvex Descent Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar composite examples showing actual objective increase above the standard nonconvex threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(L>0\) and \(\gamma>1/L\). Choose \(\mu\) with \(0<\mu<\min\{L,1/\gamma\}\) and \(\gamma(L+\mu)>2\). For \(f(x)=Lx^2/2\) and \(g(x)=-\mu x^2/2\), the proximal-gradient model has the unique global minimizer \[x^+=\frac{1-\gamma L}{1-\gamma\mu}x.\] Since \(F(x)=(L-\mu)x^2/2\), every \(x\ne0\) satisfies \(F(x^+)>F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every stepsize above 1/L, an exactly solved scalar nonconvex proximal-gradient step can increase the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^+)>F(x)\), although the proximal model is solved globally.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Failure Beyond the Nonconvex Descent Threshold
Decrease Failure Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the standard descent certificate for a proximal-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\), where \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and choose \(x^+\in T_\gamma(x)\). The proximal comparison inequality and the descent lemma give
\[
F(x^+)\le F(x)-\frac{1-\gamma L}{2\gamma}\lVert x^+-x\rVert^2.
\]
Thus \(0<\gamma<1/L\) yields certified strict decrease whenever \(x^+\ne x\). At \(\gamma=1/L\) the coefficient vanishes, so only nonincrease is certified. For \(\gamma>1/L\) this inequality has a negative coefficient and cannot furnish a universal sufficient-decrease certificate without additional curvature or line-search information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard proximal-gradient decrease certificate is positive below stepsize 1/L, degenerates at 1/L, and provides no universal decrease guarantee above that threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and the indicated proximal subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^+)\le F(x)-\frac{1-\gamma L}{2\gamma}\lVert x^+-x\rVert^2\), with a positive certified decrease coefficient exactly when \(\gamma<1/L\).

notation.meaning: Set of minimizers of the proximal-gradient model at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon residual complexity implied by the cumulative summability estimate.

If \(c\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\|^2\le F(x^0)-F_*\), then
\[
\min_{0\le k<N}\|G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\|\le \sqrt{\frac{F(x^0)-F_*}{cN}}.
\]
Consequently, some iterate among the first \(N\) has residual at most \(\varepsilon\) whenever \(N\ge [F(x^0)-F_*]/(c\varepsilon^2)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square summability obtained by telescoping a uniform proximal-descent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a sequence satisfies
\[
F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)-c\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2
\]
for every \(k\), with \(c>0\), and suppose \(F_*:=\inf_k F(x^k)>-\infty\). Summing from \(k=0\) to \(N-1\) yields
\[
c\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2\le F(x^0)-F(x^N)\le F(x^0)-F_*.
\]
Consequently, \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2<\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing successive-step and residual behavior under bounded stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the iterates obey \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\gamma_kG_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\). If
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2<\infty
\]
and \(0<\underline\gamma\le\gamma_k\le\overline\gamma<\infty\), then
\[
G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\to0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\to0.
\]
Hence the iteration is asymptotically regular, although these conditions alone do not imply convergence of the full sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Square-summable residuals vanish; bounded stepsizes then force successive proximal-gradient iterates to become arbitrarily close.

notation.meaning: Uniform lower and upper stepsize bounds

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this asymptotic-regularity formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Square summability implies residual convergence to zero, and the stated update with an upper stepsize bound implies vanishing increments. The property fits the container, but no source locator is supplied.

children.title: Summability-to-Regularity Transfer
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions supporting passage from cumulative control to asymptotic regularity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing why residual square summability alone does not imply vanishing steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Residual square summability alone does not control an unrelated step sequence. For example, in \(\mathbb R\), let \(r_k=(k+1)^{-1}\) and \(d_k=1\). Then
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|r_k|^2<\infty,\qquad r_k\to0,
\]
but \(d_k\not\to0\), and no finite constant \(M\) satisfies \(|d_k|\le M|r_k|\) for all \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Square-summable residuals need not produce vanishing steps unless a uniform residual-to-step bound or an equivalent condition is imposed.
review_flags: Elementary sequence counterexample; no external source locator is needed for mathematical verification.
knowledge_statements.title: Necessity of Uniform Residual-to-Step Control
Summability-to-Regularity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract transfer from summable residual energy to asymptotic regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any normed-space sequences \((r_k)\) and \((d_k)\), suppose
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert r_k\rVert^2<\infty,
\qquad
\lVert d_k\rVert\le M\lVert r_k\rVert
\]
for some finite \(M\). Then \(r_k\to0\) and \(d_k\to0\). Applied with \(r_k=G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\) and \(d_k=x^{k+1}-x^k=-\gamma_kr_k\), any uniform upper bound on \(\gamma_k\) transfers residual square summability into asymptotic regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step uniformly controlled by a square-summable residual must vanish, transferring residual summability into asymptotic regularity.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the abstract transfer principle.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract summability-to-regularity principle is correct and appropriately distinguished from the two sibling properties, but it lacks an inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected and probabilistic residual bounds for a uniformly sampled iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \[F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)-c\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2,\qquad F(x^k)\ge F_{\inf},\] with \(c>0\). For \(N\ge1\), let \(K\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\). Then \[\mathbb E\lVert G_{\gamma_K}(x^K)\rVert^2\le\frac{F(x^0)-F_{\inf}}{cN},\] and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\lVert G_{\gamma_K}(x^K)\rVert>\varepsilon\right)\le\frac{F(x^0)-F_{\inf}}{cN\varepsilon^2}.\] Consequently, failure probability at most \(\delta\in(0,1)\) is guaranteed when \(N\ge [F(x^0)-F_{\inf}]/(c\delta\varepsilon^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform random output gives an expected squared residual of order 1/N and an explicit probability guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The uniform sufficient-decrease inequality holds with \(c>0\).
The attained objective values are bounded below by \(F_{\inf}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\|G_{\gamma_K}(x^K)\|^2\le [F(x^0)-F_{\inf}]/(cN)\), with the displayed tail and \((\varepsilon,\delta)\) bounds.

notation.meaning: Requested upper bound on failure probability

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized-Output Stationarity Complexity
Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case proximal-gradient residual complexity under uniform sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume
\[
F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)-c\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2,
\qquad F(x^k)\ge F_{\inf},
\]
with \(c>0\). Then, for every integer \(N\ge1\),
\[
\min_{0\le k<N}\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2
\le \frac{F(x^0)-F_{\inf}}{cN}.
\]
Therefore an index satisfying \(\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\) is guaranteed within
\[
N\ge \frac{F(x^0)-F_{\inf}}{c\varepsilon^2}
\]
iterations, giving an \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) first-order stationarity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform sufficient decrease yields an O(1/N) best squared residual and O(ε⁻²) iterations to an ε-stationary iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\le k<N}\lVert G_{\gamma_k}(x^k)\rVert^2\le [F(x^0)-F_{\inf}]/(cN)\), hence the iteration complexity is \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\).

notation.meaning: Known lower bound on the attained objective values

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the proximal-gradient stationarity-complexity bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The best-iterate bound and resulting order O(epsilon^{-2}) stationarity complexity follow from the stated uniform decrease and lower bound. The selected complexity-bound kind fits, but no source is cited.
