children.title: Error-Bound Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local or global rates derived from residual-to-distance error bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite, geometric, and polynomial objective-gap regimes induced by power residual domination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k:=F(x^k)-F_*\ge0\). Suppose eventually \[s_{k+1}\le s_k-a\lVert G_\gamma(x^k)\rVert^2,\qquad s_k\le b\lVert G_\gamma(x^k)\rVert^p,\] where \(a,b>0\) and \(p>0\). Then \[s_{k+1}\le s_k-a b^{-2/p}s_k^{2/p}.\] If \(0<p<2\), then \(s_k=O(k^{-p/(2-p)})\). If \(p=2\), either the gap has already vanished or \(a\le b\) and \(s_{k+1}\le(1-a/b)s_k\). If \(p>2\), the nonnegative gap reaches zero in finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power residual domination gives polynomial decay below exponent two, geometric decay at exponent two, and finite termination above exponent two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective gaps have polynomial, geometric, or finite-termination behavior according as \(p<2\), \(p=2\), or \(p>2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Power Residual-Dominance Rate Regimes

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eventually, \(F(x^{k+1})-F_*\le q\bigl(F(x^k)-F_*\bigr)\), where \(q=1-a/b\in[0,1)\), so the objective gaps converge Q-linearly.

notation.meaning: Reference or limiting objective value that lower-bounds the eventual objective values
Proximal-gradient residual mapping with fixed parameter gamma

review_flags: A source with an exact locator for this residual-dominance rate theorem remains required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-linear objective-gap decay induced by local residual domination and sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_*\in\mathbb{R}\). Suppose that, for all sufficiently large integers \(k\),
\[
F_*\le F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k),
\qquad
F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)-a\lVert G_\gamma(x^k)\rVert^2,
\]
and
\[
F(x^k)-F_*\le b\lVert G_\gamma(x^k)\rVert^2,
\]
where \(0<a\le b<\infty\). Then
\[
F(x^{k+1})-F_*
\le q\bigl(F(x^k)-F_*\bigr),
\qquad
q:=1-\frac{a}{b}\in[0,1).
\]
Thus the objective gaps converge Q-linearly. A rate for \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X_*)\) requires an additional estimate that bounds this distance in terms of a quantity already known to decay geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual domination of a nonnegative objective gap, combined with sufficient decrease, gives Q-linear objective-gap convergence. A distance rate requires an additional compatible estimate.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Rate Regimes

children.title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Convergence-rate classifications associated with Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate taxonomy under explicit descent, relative-error, and power-KL inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the preceding finite-length hypotheses, set \(s_k=F(x^k)-F_*\). Assume additionally that, eventually, \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\ge \kappa s_{k+1}^{\theta},\qquad \kappa>0,\quad \theta\in[0,1).\] Then \(\theta=0\) gives finite termination; \(0<\theta\le1/2\) gives geometric objective-gap decay and R-linear convergence of \(x^k\) to \(\bar x\); and \(1/2<\theta<1\) gives \[s_k=O\!\left(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)}\right),\qquad \lVert x^k-\bar x\rVert=O\!\left(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With explicit descent and relative-error inequalities, a power KL exponent yields finite, linear, or polynomial convergence regimes.
assumptions_latex: The hypotheses of Finite-Length Consequence of KL Descent hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rates are finite for \(\theta=0\), linear for \(0<\theta\le1/2\), and polynomial with the displayed exponents for \(1/2<\theta<1\).

notation.meaning: Objective gap relative to the limiting value
KL exponent under the slope convention displayed

knowledge_statements.title: Quantified KL Exponent Rate Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite trajectory length and full-sequence convergence under quantified descent, relative error, and a uniformized KL inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(F(x^k)\downarrow F_*\), and suppose eventually \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert,\] with \(a,b>0\). Assume the tail lies in a neighborhood on which one KL inequality is valid, and that it has a cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfying \(F(\bar x)=F_*\). Then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert<\infty\qquad\text{and}\qquad x^k\to\bar x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantified descent, relative error, and a uniformized KL inequality yield finite trajectory length and convergence of the whole sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and \(F(x^k)\downarrow F_*\).
The displayed sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities hold eventually with \(a,b>0\).
The tail remains in a common KL neighborhood and has a cluster point \(\bar x\) with \(F(\bar x)=F_*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Length Consequence of KL Descent
Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard KL-exponent taxonomy under descent and relative-error conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^k\to\bar x\), set \(s_k=F(x^k)-F(\bar x)\), and assume sufficient decrease, a relative-error bound, and the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality with desingularizer \(\varphi(s)=cs^{1-\theta}\), where \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\). Then the standard regimes are: \(\theta=0\), finite termination; \(0<\theta\le1/2\), geometric decay of \(s_k\) and R-linear convergence of \(x^k\); and \(1/2<\theta<1\),
\[
s_k=O\!\left(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)}\right),
\qquad
\lVert x^k-\bar x\rVert=O\!\left(k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard descent and relative-error hypotheses, the KL exponent gives finite, linear, or polynomial convergence regimes.
assumptions_latex: The sequence satisfies sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities near \(\bar x\).
\(F\) has KL desingularizer \(\varphi(s)=cs^{1-\theta}\) at \(\bar x\), with \(\theta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rate is finite for \(\theta=0\), linear for \(0<\theta\le1/2\), and polynomial with the displayed exponents for \(1/2<\theta<1\).

notation.meaning: Objective gap relative to the limiting critical value

review_flags: An authoritative locator for the exact KL hypotheses and exponent convention is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed KL exponent taxonomy is recognizable, but “sufficient decrease” and “relative-error bound” are not stated as quantified inequalities with constants. Exact rate exponents depend on those hypotheses and the KL-exponent convention, and no authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Rate-Regime Comparison
children.top_down_role: Overlap, separation, or transfer between the two geometric rate frameworks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transfer Between Quadratic Residual Domination and KL Exponent One-Half
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local comparison under two-sided equivalence between a selected residual and the subdifferential slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s(x):=F(x)-F_*\ge0\) and \(R(x)\ge0\) on a neighborhood, and assume \[mR(x)\le \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\le MR(x)\] for constants \(m,M>0\). The exponent-one-half KL inequality \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge c\sqrt{s(x)}\] implies \[s(x)\le (M/c)^2R(x)^2.\] Conversely, \(s(x)\le bR(x)^2\) implies \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge m b^{-1/2}\sqrt{s(x)}.\] Thus the two conditions are locally equivalent under two-sided slope-residual comparability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic residual domination and the exponent-one-half KL inequality are equivalent when the selected residual is locally comparable in both directions with the subdifferential slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exponent-one-half KL geometry and quadratic residual domination transfer to one another with the displayed constants.
knowledge_statements.title: Transfer Between Quadratic Residual Domination and KL Exponent One-Half
Rate-Regime Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of residual error-bound and KL mechanisms for local rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under a common sufficient-decrease inequality, a residual-dominance error bound
\[
F(x)-F_*\le b\lVert G_\gamma(x)\rVert^2
\]
directly yields geometric objective decay. A KL inequality with exponent \(\theta\) is more general and yields finite termination for \(\theta=0\), a linear regime for \(0<\theta\le1/2\), and a polynomial regime for \(1/2<\theta<1\). Hence the residual-dominance regime matches the linear KL range at the level of rate conclusions, but neither condition is identified with the other without additional regularity connecting objective gaps, distances, and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual domination directly gives linear decay; KL geometry also permits finite and sublinear regimes, and equivalence requires additional regularity.
assumptions_latex: A common sufficient-decrease inequality holds near the limiting stationary set.
The compared error-bound and KL statements use the same objective gap and residual convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual domination gives a linear regime, while the KL exponent partitions behavior into finite, linear, and polynomial regimes; equivalence is not automatic.
review_flags: A source explicitly comparing these rate mechanisms under aligned conventions is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the comparison leaf and appropriately avoids claiming equivalence, but its KL side inherits an underspecified theorem and there is no source aligning the two conventions.

children.title: Convex Forward-Backward Envelope Regime
children.top_down_role: Envelope geometry for convex smooth-plus-proximable composites.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\gamma\) is finite-valued, continuously differentiable, and convex.

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of the convex proximal term.

review_flags: The closed threshold preserves convexity but need not preserve the original minimizer set; minimizer equivalence uses the strict threshold stated in the seed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral convexity mechanism for a positive-semidefinite quadratic forward term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex quadratic forward term,
\[
F_\gamma(x)=\frac12\langle x,(Q-\gamma Q^2)x\rangle+
\langle q-\gamma Qq,x\rangle+c-\frac\gamma2\|q\|^2
+g^\gamma((I-\gamma Q)x-\gamma q).
\]
When \(0<\gamma\le1/\lambda_{\max}(Q)\), the quadratic matrix \(Q-\gamma Q^2\) is positive semidefinite, while the last term is a convex function composed with an affine map. Hence \(F_\gamma\) is convex and continuously differentiable. The strict inequality is additionally required for the general minimizer-correspondence statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic forward term, the envelope is a convex quadratic plus a convex Moreau envelope composed with an affine map; convexity persists at the closed spectral threshold, while general minimizer preservation requires a strict threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Convexity Decomposition

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\gamma\) is finite-valued, convex, and continuously differentiable, and \(\operatorname*{argmin}F_\gamma=\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\).

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of g with parameter gamma
Hessian of the convex quadratic smooth term

review_flags: An exact source locator for the strict-stepsize convex quadratic regime remains required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient convexity and minimizer-equivalence regime for a convex quadratic smooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be given by
\[
f(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,Qx\rangle+\langle q,x\rangle+c,
\]
where \(Q=Q^\top\succeq0\), and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. If \(Q\ne0\), assume
\[
0<\gamma<\frac{1}{\lambda_{\max}(Q)};
\]
if \(Q=0\), let \(\gamma>0\). Then the forward-backward envelope
\[
F_\gamma(x)=f(x)-\frac{\gamma}{2}\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert^2+g^\gamma\!\left(x-\gamma\nabla f(x)\right)
\]
is finite-valued, continuously differentiable, and convex. Moreover,
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}F_\gamma=
\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex quadratic smooth term and a proper closed convex nonsmooth term, a strictly subcritical stepsize makes the forward-backward envelope smooth and convex, with the same minimizers as the original objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Forward-Backward Envelope Regime

children.title: Nonconvex Forward-Backward Envelope Regime
children.top_down_role: Envelope geometry for nonconvex smooth-plus-proximable composites.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\gamma(x)=-\tfrac a2(1+\gamma a)x^2\), so \(F_\gamma\) is strictly concave although its critical point agrees with the zero of \(G_\gamma\).

notation.meaning: Forward-backward envelope and gradient mapping in the scalar example.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid subcritical regime with a nonconvex smooth term and convex proximal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
f(x)=-\frac a2x^2,\qquad g(x)=0,
\]
the gradient of \(f\) is \(a\)-Lipschitz. Every \(0<\gamma<1/a\) lies in the standard subcritical regime, yet
\[
F_\gamma(x)=f(x)-\frac\gamma2|f'(x)|^2
=-\frac a2(1+\gamma a)x^2.
\]
Thus the envelope is strictly concave. Nevertheless,
\[
G_\gamma(x)=-ax,
\qquad F_\gamma'(x)=(1+\gamma a)G_\gamma(x),
\]
so both stationarity tests vanish exactly at \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concave quadratic smooth term with no nonsmooth term gives a strictly concave forward-backward envelope even at every admissible subcritical stepsize, while critical-point correspondence remains valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Subcritical Nonconvex-Envelope Example
Nonconvex Forward-Backward Envelope Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth merit-function behavior without global envelope convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(g\) be proper, closed, and convex, and take \(0<\gamma<1/L\). The forward-backward envelope is continuously differentiable with
\[

abla F_\gamma(x)= igl(I-\gamma
abla^2f(x) igr)G_\gamma(x).
\]
Because \(I-\gamma
abla^2f(x)\) is nonsingular, \(
abla F_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(G_\gamma(x)=0\), equivalently \(0\in
abla f(x)+\partial g(x)\). The envelope need not be convex when \(f\) is nonconvex, but it remains a smooth stationarity merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a small stepsize, a nonconvex smooth term still yields a differentiable envelope whose critical points equal proximal-gradient stationary points.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the envelope-gradient identity and critical-point correspondence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated C2, Lipschitz-gradient, convex-g, and strict stepsize assumptions, the envelope-gradient identity and critical-point correspondence are mathematically consistent. The property fits the nonconvex regime leaf, but no supporting locator is supplied.

children.title: Envelope Regime Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Stepsize or curvature thresholds separating valid envelope interpretations from failure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla F_\gamma(x)=0\) for every \(x\), while \(G_\gamma(x)=x/\gamma+b\), which is nonzero unless \(x=-\gamma b\).

notation.meaning: Forward-backward envelope and gradient mapping for the scalar example.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar counterexample at singularity of the forward-step Jacobian factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{x^2}{2\gamma},\qquad g(x)=bx,\qquad b\ne0.
\]
Here \(L=1/\gamma\), so \(I-\gamma\nabla^2f=0\). Moreover,
\[
T_\gamma(x)=-\gamma b,
\qquad G_\gamma(x)=\frac{x}{\gamma}+b,
\qquad F_\gamma(x)=-\frac\gamma2b^2.
\]
Thus every point is critical for the envelope, but the proximal-gradient residual vanishes only at \(x=-\gamma b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the reciprocal-curvature threshold, a convex scalar composite can have a constant forward-backward envelope even though its proximal-gradient residual is nonzero at all but one point.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Factor Stationarity Counterexample

assumptions_latex: \(a>0\) and \(g(y)=-\tfrac a2\lVert y\rVert^2\) in the prox-boundedness example.
Where the gradient identity is valid, \(\nabla F_\gamma(x)=\bigl(I-\gamma\nabla^2f(x)\bigr)G_\gamma(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the example, \(g^\gamma(z)=-\infty\) for every \(z\) when \(\gamma>1/a\), while at \(\gamma=1/a\) it is finite only at \(z=0\). If \(I-\gamma\nabla^2f(x)\) is singular, envelope criticality alone no longer guarantees \(G_\gamma(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of g with parameter gamma

review_flags: A source locator for the prox-boundedness boundary and gradient-conversion boundary remains required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of global envelope finiteness and loss of guaranteed stationarity conversion at boundary parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The forward-backward envelope construction has distinct finiteness and stationarity-conversion boundaries. Let
\[
g(y)=-\tfrac a2\lVert y\rVert^2,
\qquad a>0.
\]
Its Moreau envelope satisfies
\[
g^\gamma(z)=\inf_y\left\{-\tfrac a2\lVert y\rVert^2+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert y-z\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
If \(\gamma>1/a\), then \(g^\gamma(z)=-\infty\) for every \(z\). If \(\gamma=1/a\), then \(g^\gamma(0)=0\), whereas \(g^\gamma(z)=-\infty\) for every \(z\ne0\); hence the envelope is not globally finite at the threshold. Separately, wherever
\[
\nabla F_\gamma(x)=\bigl(I-\gamma\nabla^2f(x)\bigr)G_\gamma(x)
\]
holds, singularity of \(I-\gamma\nabla^2f(x)\) means that \(\nabla F_\gamma(x)=0\) no longer guarantees \(G_\gamma(x)=0\), because a nonzero residual may lie in the matrix null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At or beyond the prox-boundedness threshold, the Moreau envelope can cease to be globally finite. Separately, a singular gradient-conversion matrix removes the guarantee that envelope criticality implies a zero proximal-gradient residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Regime Failure Boundary

children.title: Forward-Backward Envelope Representation
children.top_down_role: Merit-function representation supplied by the forward-backward envelope.

assumptions_latex: \(\gamma>0\) is chosen so that \(g^\gamma(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\) is finite at the point under consideration.

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope defined by an infimum

review_flags: An exact source locator for the forward-backward envelope representation remains required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function and Moreau-envelope representations of the forward-backward envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and prox-bounded, and define
\[
g^\gamma(z):=\inf_y\left\{g(y)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert y-z\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
For \(\gamma>0\) and every \(x\) for which the value is finite, define the forward-backward envelope by
\[
F_\gamma(x):=\inf_y\left\{f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+g(y)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Completing the square gives
\[
F_\gamma(x)=f(x)-\frac{\gamma}{2}\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert^2+g^\gamma\!\left(x-\gamma\nabla f(x)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forward-backward envelope is the infimum value of the proximal linearization model, equivalently a shifted Moreau envelope plus a gradient correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward-Backward Envelope Representation

children.title: Gradient-Mapping Representation
children.top_down_role: Stationarity representation supplied by the proximal-gradient mapping.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice continuously differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
review_flags: source_supports_proximal-gradient setting; exact envelope identity requires locator verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean forward-backward envelope with a convex proximal term and smooth, possibly nonconvex, forward term.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the Moreau envelope \(g^\gamma\) is continuously differentiable and the chain rule gives
\[
\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)=\bigl(I-\gamma\nabla^2f(x)\bigr)\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-T_\gamma(x)\bigr)=Q_\gamma(x)G_\gamma(x).
\]
Consequently, the envelope gradient is the proximal-gradient mapping transformed by the Jacobian of the forward map \(x\mapsto x-\gamma\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forward-backward envelope gradient equals the proximal-gradient mapping multiplied by the Jacobian factor of the forward step.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Mapping Representation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable.
\(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp stepsize assumptions for the Euclidean gradient-mapping factorization with a convex proximal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\gamma>0\), the convex Moreau envelope \(g^\gamma\) is continuously differentiable, and the forward-backward envelope satisfies
\[
\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)=\bigl(I-\gamma\nabla^2f(x)\bigr)G_\gamma(x).
\]
Thus a restriction such as \(\gamma<1/L\) is unnecessary for the factorization itself; such a restriction is used when invertibility or merit inequalities are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope-gradient factorization holds for every positive stepsize; subcritical stepsizes are needed for conversion or merit properties, not for the identity itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrestricted-Stepsize Gradient Factorization

children.title: Envelope-to-Mapping Conversion
children.top_down_role: Regularity or metric conditions supporting translation between envelope gradients plus mapping residuals.

assumptions_latex: The assumptions and notation of the gradient-mapping representation hold.
\(Q_\gamma(x)\) is nonsingular at the point under consideration.

notation.meaning: Forward-backward point, mapping, and envelope inherited from the prerequisite.

review_flags: source_supports_proximal-gradient setting; conversion formula requires locator verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise conversion when the forward-step Jacobian factor is invertible.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At every \(x\) for which \(Q_\gamma(x)\) is nonsingular,
\[
G_\gamma(x)=Q_\gamma(x)^{-1}\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sigma_{\min}(Q_\gamma(x))\|G_\gamma(x)\|\leq\|\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)\|\leq\sigma_{\max}(Q_\gamma(x))\|G_\gamma(x)\|.
\]
Thus \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)=0\). If additionally \(\|\nabla^2f(x)\|\leq L\) and \(\gamma L<1\), then the two singular-value constants may be replaced by \(1-\gamma L\) and \(1+\gamma L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible forward-step factor converts the envelope gradient back to the proximal-gradient mapping, with explicit norm equivalence and identical zeros.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-to-Mapping Conversion

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Forward-Step Factor Destroys Reverse Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar boundary showing why invertibility of the envelope-to-mapping factor is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\gamma>0\), let \(f(x)=x^2/(2\gamma)\), and let \(g=0\). Then
\[
T_\gamma(x)=0,\qquad G_\gamma(x)=\frac{x}{\gamma},\qquad Q_\gamma(x)=1-\gamma f''(x)=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x)=f(x)-\frac{\gamma}{2}|f'(x)|^2=0.
\]
Thus \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)=0\) for every \(x\), whereas \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) only at \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the forward-step factor is singular, the envelope gradient can vanish identically while the proximal-gradient mapping remains nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)=0\) for all \(x\), but \(G_\gamma(x)=x/\gamma\); reverse conversion and zero-set equivalence fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Forward-Step Factor Destroys Reverse Conversion

children.title: Merit-Function Geometry
children.top_down_role: Descent, stationarity, or level-set structure of envelope-based merit functions.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
review_flags: exact envelope bounds require locator verification

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), comparison with the trial point \(z=x\) and the smoothness bound for \(f\) yield
\[
F(T_\gamma(x))+\frac{\gamma}{2}(1-\gamma L)\|G_\gamma(x)\|^2\leq\varphi_\gamma(x)\leq F(x).
\]
Hence the envelope is finite and continuous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), lies below the composite objective on its domain, and dominates the objective at the forward-backward point by a positive quadratic residual term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope lies below the current composite objective and above the objective at the proximal-gradient point plus a positive residual term.
knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Function Geometry

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the strict subcritical stepsize condition,
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\varphi_\gamma(x)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}F(x),
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}\varphi_\gamma=
\operatorname*{argmin}F.
\]
Thus the forward-backward envelope changes the merit geometry without changing the global optimal value or global solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the reciprocal-Lipschitz threshold, the forward-backward envelope has the same infimum and global minimizers as the composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global-Minimum Preservation by the Forward-Backward Envelope

children.title: Exact-Penalty Geometry
children.top_down_role: Penalty parameter regimes preserving relevant constrained stationary structure.

assumptions_latex: \(M:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally \(K\)-Lipschitz near a closed set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_\rho(x)>M(s)\quad\text{for every nearby }x\notin S\text{ and nearest }s\in S.\]

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance to the feasible or stationary set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local Lipschitz bound combined with a residual error bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exact penalization of a residual-defined stationary set under an error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(P_\rho(x)=M(x)+\rho\|R(x)\|\). For every sufficiently nearby \(x\), choose a nearest \(s\in S\). Then
\[
P_\rho(x)\geq M(s)+\left(\frac{\rho}{\kappa}-K\right)\operatorname{dist}(x,S).
\]
Because \(\rho>\kappa K\), every nearby point outside \(S\) has strictly larger penalized value than its nearest residual-zero point. Consequently, local minimization of \(P_\rho\) reduces exactly to local minimization of \(M\) over \(S\); no nonzero-residual point can be a local minimizer in a neighborhood where the assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual norm becomes a locally exact penalty when its weight exceeds the product of the merit Lipschitz constant and error-bound modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed comparison follows from the Lipschitz and error-bound assumptions, but no inspectable source is supplied. Moreover, comparison with a nearest point in S alone does not establish that every nonzero-residual point cannot be a local minimizer or the asserted full equivalence of local minimization; a formulation around a specified constrained local minimizer requires precise neighborhood hypotheses.

children.title: Merit-to-Penalty Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between envelope merit behavior plus exact-penalty interpretations.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(0<\gamma<1/L\).
\(F=f+g\), with \(T_\gamma\), \(G_\gamma\), and \(\varphi_\gamma\) defined by the forward-backward construction.

notation.meaning: Smooth Taylor remainder based at the second argument.

review_flags: exact merit-penalty decomposition requires locator verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of envelope merit into objective, quadratic residual penalty, and smooth Taylor correction.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), evaluation of the envelope model at its minimizer gives
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x)=F(T_\gamma(x))+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|G_\gamma(x)\|^2-D_f(T_\gamma(x),x).
\]
Since \(|D_f(T_\gamma(x),x)|\leq \frac{L\gamma^2}{2}\|G_\gamma(x)\|^2\), the envelope is a quadratic residual penalty on the objective value at \(T_\gamma(x)\), perturbed by a controlled Taylor remainder. In particular, its penalty coefficient remains positive in the lower bound when \(\gamma L<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope equals the objective at the proximal-gradient point plus a quadratic residual penalty, minus a controlled Taylor remainder.
knowledge_statements.title: Merit-to-Penalty Correspondence

Search direction and accepted step length.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\), repeat while \(\|G_\gamma(x_k)\|\) exceeds a prescribed tolerance. Choose \(d_k\) satisfying the stated descent condition. Select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that, with \(\alpha_k=\alpha_0\beta^{j_k}\),
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq\varphi_\gamma(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\langle\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k),d_k\rangle.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Output the first iterate meeting the residual tolerance, or report the last iterate when a prescribed iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along an envelope descent direction until the Armijo inequality holds, then stop when the proximal-gradient residual reaches tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Line-Search Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity and Worst-Iterate Complexity of Envelope Armijo Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence and first-order complexity for uniformly gradient-related directions on a smooth envelope level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma\) is \(L_\varphi\)-Lipschitz on the generated level set and
\[
\langle\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k),d_k\rangle\le-c\|\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\|^2,\qquad \|d_k\|\le M\|\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\|.
\]
For geometric Armijo backtracking with \(\alpha_0>0\) and \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\), every accepted step satisfies
\[
\alpha_k\ge \underline\alpha:=\min\!\left\{\alpha_0,\frac{2\beta(1-\sigma)c}{L_\varphi M^2}\right\}>0.
\]
If \(\varphi_\gamma\) is bounded below by \(\varphi_{\inf}\), then
\[
\sum_{k=0}^\infty\|\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\|^2<\infty,
\quad \nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\to0,
\]
and
\[
\min_{0\le k\le N}\|\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\|^2
\le
\frac{\varphi_\gamma(x_0)-\varphi_{\inf}}{\sigma c\underline\alpha(N+1)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly gradient-related directions give nonvanishing Armijo steps, convergence of the envelope gradient to zero, and an order epsilon-to-the-minus-two iteration bound for an epsilon gradient certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma\) is Lipschitz on the generated level set.
The displayed descent and direction-size bounds hold uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\to0\) and an iterate with \(\|\nabla\varphi_\gamma\|\le\varepsilon\) occurs within \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) iterations.

notation.meaning: Level-set Lipschitz constant of the envelope gradient.
Uniform lower bound on accepted step lengths.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity and Worst-Iterate Complexity of Envelope Armijo Search

children.top_down_role: Second-order interfaces based on local envelope structure.

assumptions_latex: \(\varphi_\gamma\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the iterates.
\(H_k=\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\) is nonsingular and the computed direction is an envelope descent direction.
An Armijo line search is available.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), form \(H_k=\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\) and solve
\[
H_kd_k=-\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k).
\]
If the solution fails a prescribed descent test, replace or regularize \(H_k\) so that the resulting \(d_k\) is a descent direction. Choose \(\alpha_k\) by the envelope Armijo line search and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop and return \(x_k\) when \(\|G_\gamma(x_k)\|\) is below tolerance; otherwise continue until the iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the envelope Newton system, regularize if necessary for descent, and globalize the step by envelope Armijo backtracking.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Quadratic Convergence of Envelope Newton Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical local Newton behavior for a twice-smooth forward-backward envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_\star)=0\). If \(\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma\) is locally Lipschitz and \(H_\star=\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma(x_\star)\succ0\), then for every sufficiently close initial point the unregularized Newton system is well posed. With Armijo parameter \(\sigma\in(0,1/2)\), unit steps are eventually accepted and
\[
\|x_{k+1}-x_\star\|\le C\|x_k-x_\star\|^2
\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz envelope Hessian that is positive definite at the stationary point yields eventual full Newton steps and Q-quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma\) exists and is locally Lipschitz near \(x_\star\).

notation.meaning: Envelope Hessian at the stationary point.

children.title: Envelope Quasi-Newton Interface
children.top_down_role: Approximate-curvature interfaces using envelope-based secant information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local superlinear criterion for envelope quasi-Newton directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_k\to x_\star\), where \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_\star)=0\), and let \(H_\star=\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma(x_\star)\) be nonsingular. Suppose \(\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma\) is continuous near \(x_\star\), \(B_kd_k=-\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\), and
\[
\frac{\|(B_k-H_\star)d_k\|}{\|d_k\|}\to0.
\]
If unit steps are eventually accepted, then
\[
\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_\star\|}{\|x_k-x_\star\|}\to0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dennis–Moré approximation condition together with eventual unit steps yields Q-superlinear convergence of envelope quasi-Newton iterates.
assumptions_latex: The iterates converge to an envelope stationary point.
The envelope Hessian is continuous and nonsingular there.

notation.meaning: Exact envelope Hessian at the limiting point.

knowledge_statements.title: Dennis–Moré Superlinear Envelope Convergence

\(B_k\) is symmetric positive definite, and \(s_k^Ty_k>0\) whenever a BFGS update is accepted.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: BFGS-type quasi-Newton interface using envelope gradients and line-search globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\) and a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(B_kd_k=-\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\), select \(\alpha_k\) by an envelope line search, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Form \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_{k+1})-\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x_k)\). If \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), apply
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{s_k^Ty_k};
\]
otherwise retain or damp \(B_k\). Stop when \(\|G_\gamma(x_k)\|\) meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS can use envelope-gradient differences, positive-definite curvature models, and envelope line search while retaining the proximal-gradient residual as stopping test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Envelope with a Singular Stationary Hessian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy boundary showing that classical smoothness alone does not regularize the Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=0\) and \(f(x)=x^4\). Then
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x)=f(x)-\frac{\gamma}{2}|f'(x)|^2=x^4-8\gamma x^6.
\]
Although \(\varphi_\gamma\in C^\infty\) and \(\nabla\varphi_\gamma(0)=0\),
\[
\nabla^2\varphi_\gamma(0)=0.
\]
Thus the classical Newton equation is singular at the stationary point and the nonsingular-Hessian quadratic-rate theorem is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinitely differentiable forward-backward envelope can have a singular stationary Hessian, so smoothness alone does not ensure a regular Newton interface.

notation.meaning: Forward-backward envelope of the displayed smooth problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Envelope with a Singular Stationary Hessian

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indefinite Envelope Curvature Can Produce a Non-Descent Newton Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-sign boundary for Armijo-globalized envelope Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=0\) and \(f(x)=-x^2/2\). Then
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x)=-\frac{1+\gamma}{2}x^2,
\quad \nabla\varphi_\gamma(x)=-(1+\gamma)x,
\quad \nabla^2\varphi_\gamma(x)=-(1+\gamma).
\]
For \(x\ne0\), the Newton equation gives \(d=-x\), but
\[
\langle\nabla\varphi_\gamma(x),d\rangle=(1+\gamma)x^2>0.
\]
Hence the unmodified Newton direction is not a descent direction, and sufficiently small positive steps cannot satisfy a descent Armijo condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth nonsingular but negative envelope Hessian can make the Newton direction ascend the envelope, requiring curvature modification or another fallback.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Envelope Curvature Can Produce a Non-Descent Newton Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete convex example showing that first-order envelope smoothness does not imply classical second-order smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f=0\) and \(g(x)=|x|\), the forward-backward envelope is
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x)=g^\gamma(x)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{x^2}{2\gamma},& |x|\leq\gamma,\\
|x|-\dfrac{\gamma}{2},& |x|\geq\gamma.
\end{cases}
\]
This function is continuously differentiable, but its second derivative jumps from \(1/\gamma\) to \(0\) at \(x=\pm\gamma\). Thus a classical envelope Hessian need not exist even for a proper closed convex proximal term; Newton interfaces require additional regularity or generalized derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute-value proximal term produces a Huber envelope that is continuously differentiable but not twice differentiable at its transition points.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the scalar quadratic example,
\[
T_\gamma(x)=(1-\gamma L)x,
\qquad
\varphi_\gamma(x)=\frac{L}{2}(1-\gamma L)x^2.
\]
At \(\gamma=L^{-1}\), the envelope is constant and its gradient no longer detects nonzero residuals. For \(\gamma>L^{-1}\), the envelope is unbounded below although \(f\) is bounded below. Moreover, the iteration is contractive exactly when \(0<\gamma<2L^{-1}\); it oscillates without contraction at \(\gamma=2L^{-1}\) and diverges for \(\gamma>2L^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar quadratic shows that steps at least reciprocal-Lipschitz destroy envelope merit geometry, while steps at least twice that size prevent convergence.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5.2 The proximal gradient method for convex programs p. 93

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative boundary separating certifiable inexact proximal steps from uncontrolled displacement selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\). Suppose an inexact proximal point \(z\) is accompanied by \(e\) satisfying
\[
e\in\partial g(z)+\nabla f(x)+\gamma^{-1}(z-x),\qquad \|e\|\le\eta.
\]
With \(\widetilde G_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}(x-z)\), there exists
\[
v=e+\widetilde G_\gamma(x)+\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(x)\in\partial F(z).
\]
If \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz between \(x\) and \(z\), then
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(z))\le(1+\gamma L)\|\widetilde G_\gamma(x)\|+\eta.
\]
Without error control, displacement alone is not a certificate: for \(f=0\), \(g(y)=\langle a,y\rangle\), and the selection \(z=x\), the inclusion holds with \(e=a\), while \(\widetilde G_\gamma(x)=0\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(z))=\|a\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal displacement certifies stationarity only when the proximal optimality error is bounded; an uncontrolled error can coexist with zero displacement and arbitrarily poor stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and its gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the segment joining \(x\) and \(z\).
\(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial(f+g)(z))\le(1+\gamma L)\|\widetilde G_\gamma(x)\|+\eta\), whereas no displacement-only bound holds without controlling \(\eta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete nonconvex example exposing ambiguity of set-valued and uncontrolled inexact proximal selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x=0\), both points minimize the proximal subproblem, so
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(0)=\{-1,1\},
\qquad
G_\gamma(0)\in\{-\gamma^{-1},\gamma^{-1}\}.
\]
The envelope \(g^\gamma(x)=\frac{1}{2\gamma}\min\{(x-1)^2,(x+1)^2\}\) is not differentiable at \(0\). Hence neither a single-valued gradient-mapping representation nor a classical envelope gradient is available without a selection or regularity condition. Likewise, an inexact proximal point with no quantitative subproblem-error bound need not define a consistent residual or preserve envelope descent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible-step counterexample showing that envelope ordering need not match objective ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Here \(L=2\), the step is admissible, and direct calculation gives
\[
\varphi_\gamma(x_1,x_2)=\frac{3}{10}x_1^2+\frac{1}{5}x_2^2.
\]
For \(u=(1,0)\) and \(v=(0,1)\),
\[
\varphi_\gamma(v)=\frac15<\frac3{10}=\varphi_\gamma(u),
\qquad
F(v)=1>\frac12=F(u).
\]
Thus decrease or ordering in the envelope merit function does not by itself imply decrease or the same ordering in the original objective. A globalization method requiring objective monotonicity must impose that requirement separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with an admissible step, two points can be oppositely ordered by the forward-backward envelope and the original objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Merit Mismatch

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Dependent Residual Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling failure for proximal-gradient residuals when the stepsize changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(g=\delta_{\{0\}}\), and define the proximal-gradient residual by \(R_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\bigr)\) for \(\gamma>0\). Since \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x)=0\), one has \(R_\gamma(x)=x/\gamma\). Consequently, for any \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2>0\) and \(x\ne0\), \(\|R_{\gamma_1}(x)\|/\|R_{\gamma_2}(x)\|=\gamma_2/\gamma_1\), although the zero set remains \(\{0\}\). Thus residual magnitudes and fixed stopping thresholds are not invariant under parameter changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual zero set is stepsize-independent in this example, but its norm scales inversely with the stepsize, so numerical thresholds are not portable.

notation.meaning: indicator function of the singleton containing zero

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the smooth-inner, convex-nonsmooth-outer problem class and records residual-fitting and conditional exact-penalty instances; it does not state a trust-region algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable and let \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and nonsmooth. Then \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}h(f(x))\) is a composite nonsmooth optimization problem. The residual-fitting problem \(\min_x\|Ax-b\|\) is obtained with \(f(x)=Ax-b\) and \(h(y)=\|y\|\); for \(\|\cdot\|_2\), its minimizers are the classical least-squares minimizers. Whenever a smooth constrained problem admits an exact \(\ell_1\)-penalty formulation, that penalized problem is also of this composite form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex nonsmooth outer function composed with a continuously differentiable inner mapping defines a composite nonsmooth problem. Norm residual fitting is an instance, and the Euclidean-norm version has the classical least-squares minimizers. A smooth constrained problem is represented this way when its chosen L1 penalty is exact.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^m\text{ for the residual-fitting instance}
\text{The constrained-problem representation requires an exact }\ell_1\text{-penalty formulation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_x h(f(x))\text{ is a composite nonsmooth problem; norm-residual models and exact }\ell_1\text{-penalty formulations are instances.}

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Outer Smooth-Inner Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite objectives with a convex extended-valued outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-outer smooth-inner composite is an extended-real-valued function \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) of the form \(F(x)=h(c(x))\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable and \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Its effective domain is \(\operatorname{dom}F=\{x:c(x)\in\operatorname{dom}h\}\). The composite may be nonconvex because the inner map need not be affine, even though the outer function is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective composes a proper closed convex outer function with a continuously differentiable inner map; nonlinearity of the inner map may make it nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite objectives augmented by an extended-valued regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and a regularizer \(r:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a regularized composite problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\Phi(x)\), where \(\Phi(x)=h(c(x))+r(x)\). In the standard convex-outer model, \(c\) is continuously differentiable while \(h\) and \(r\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Extended values of \(r\) may encode structure, but no separate constraint set is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized composite adds a proper lower-semicontinuous penalty to a smooth-inner, convex-outer objective.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(r\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity and the boundary for exact subdifferential calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi=h\circ c+r=H\circ C\) and suppose \(\Phi(\bar x)<+\infty\). The limiting-subdifferential chain inclusion is \(\partial\Phi(\bar x)\subseteq\nabla c(\bar x)^\top\partial h(c(\bar x))+\partial r(\bar x)\). Equality holds under a valid convex-composite qualification, for example continuity of \(H\) at \(C(\bar x)\). Consequently every local minimizer satisfies \(0\in\nabla c(\bar x)^\top\partial h(c(\bar x))+\partial r(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a finite local minimizer, a pulled-back outer subgradient balances a regularizer subgradient; exact calculus requires a qualification.
assumptions_latex: For equality, a valid convex-composite qualification holds at \(\bar x\), such as continuity of \(H\) at \(C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\in\nabla c(\bar x)^\top\partial h(c(\bar x))+\partial r(\bar x).\]

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential, agreeing with the convex subdifferential on convex functions

knowledge_statements.title: Qualified Composite Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent realization as one convex-outer smooth-inner composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C(x)=(c(x),x)\) and \(H(u,v)=h(u)+r(v)\). Then \(H\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, \(C\in C^1\), and \(h(c(x))+r(x)=H(C(x))\), with \(\operatorname{dom}(H\circ C)=\{x:c(x)\in\operatorname{dom}h,\ x\in\operatorname{dom}r\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifting the inner map by the identity turns a regularized composite into one ordinary convex-outer smooth-inner composite.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(r\) are proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint geometry represented by an indicator within a composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(F(x)=h(c(x))\). The constrained composite problem \(\min_{x\in C}F(x)\) has the equivalent extended-valued representation \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}F(x)+\delta_C(x)\), where \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. The two formulations have identical feasible finite-valued points, optimal values, and global minimizers whenever the infimum is well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed-set constraint is equivalently represented by adding the set's indicator function to the composite objective.

notation.meaning: extended-valued indicator of the constraint set

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Constrained Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified extended-valued form for simultaneous regularization and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(h\) and \(r\) be proper lower-semicontinuous functions. The regularized constrained problem \(\min_{x\in C}h(c(x))+r(x)\) is represented on the ambient space by \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}h(c(x))+r(x)+\delta_C(x)\). These formulations have the same finite objective values on \(C\), the same optimal value, and the same minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization and feasibility combine into one extended-valued objective by adding both the regularizer and the constraint indicator.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(r\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for simultaneous regularization and explicit feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=h\circ c+r\) and \(\Phi=G+\delta_C\). At every finite local minimizer \(\bar x\), \(0\in\partial\Phi(\bar x)\). If the applicable chain and sum rules are exact, then \(0\in\nabla c(\bar x)^\top\partial h(c(\bar x))+\partial r(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\). If \(\Phi\) is convex, this inclusion is also sufficient for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity balances outer and regularizer subgradients with a constraint normal; for a convex total objective it characterizes global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: Exact separation requires valid chain and sum-rule qualifications.
Sufficiency requires convexity of the entire function \(h\circ c+r+\delta_C\).

children.title: Residual Composites
children.top_down_role: Composite objectives organized around nonlinear residual maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objectives formed by applying an aggregate loss to a smooth residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable and let \(\ell:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous loss. A residual composite problem minimizes \(F(x)=\ell(r(x))\). For the least-squares outer loss \(\ell(z)=\tfrac12\|z\|_2^2\), this becomes \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\). The vector \(r(x)\) records model discrepancies, while the outer loss determines how those discrepancies are aggregated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual composite applies an outer loss to a smooth vector of model discrepancies; nonlinear least squares is the quadratic special case.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact representation of residual zeros by a positive-definite loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell:\mathbb R^m\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfies \(\ell(z)=0\iff z=0\), then \(F(x)=0\iff r(x)=0\). If \(r^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname*{argmin}F=r^{-1}(0)\). If the residual equation is unsolvable, the infimum may be zero without being attained, so strict positivity of an attained minimum requires an attainment assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative loss vanishing only at zero makes residual zeros exactly the zero-valued global minimizers; unsolved problems need not have a positive attained minimum.

notation.meaning: zero set of the residual map

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Zero-Residual Merit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order calculus for an outer loss composed with a smooth residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\ell\circ r\), differentiability of \(\ell\) at \(r(x)\) gives \(\nabla F(x)=J_r(x)^\top\nabla\ell(r(x))\). If \(\ell\) is proper closed convex, then \(\partial F(x)\subseteq J_r(x)^\top\partial\ell(r(x))\), with equality under a valid convex-composite qualification, such as continuity of \(\ell\) at \(r(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer gradients or subgradients are pulled back through the residual Jacobian, with exact nonsmooth equality requiring a qualification.
assumptions_latex: For the gradient formula, \(\ell\) is differentiable at \(r(x)\).
For subdifferential equality, \(\ell\) is proper closed convex and a valid qualification holds.

children.title: Robust-Loss Composites
children.top_down_role: Composite objectives using robust outer losses for outlier-sensitive residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessary condition for separable locally Lipschitz residual losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every local minimizer \(\bar x\), Clarke's Fermat rule and chain rule give \(0\in\partial^C F(\bar x)\subseteq J_r(\bar x)^\top\prod_i\partial^C\rho_i(r_i(\bar x))\). Hence there are \(v_i\in\partial^C\rho_i(r_i(\bar x))\) satisfying \(\sum_i v_i\nabla r_i(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer, scalar Clarke subgradients can be selected so their Jacobian-weighted sum vanishes.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_i\) is locally Lipschitz near \(r_i(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Stationarity of Robust-Loss Composites

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational bounded-influence subclass of separable residual composites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\in C^1\). A bounded-influence robust-loss composite is \(F(x)=\sum_i\rho_i(r_i(x))\), where each \(\rho_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz and its Clarke subgradients are uniformly bounded: \(\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\sup_{v\in\partial^C\rho_i(t)}|v|<+\infty\). This definition controls marginal influence; it is one operational notion of robustness, not an equivalence with contamination robustness or every use of the term robust loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-influence robust-loss composite uses scalar losses with uniformly bounded Clarke subgradients.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz.
The term robust is restricted here to the stated bounded-influence subclass.

notation.meaning: Clarke subdifferential of the scalar loss

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Influence Robust-Loss Composites

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Influence Is Not Global Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of the bounded-influence subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Uniformly bounded scalar subgradients control marginal influence only. They imply neither convexity, coercivity, uniqueness of minimizers, nor that stationary points have small residuals. Convex bounded-slope losses and bounded redescending losses exhibit different global behavior despite both having bounded influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded influence alone does not imply convexity, coercivity, uniqueness, or residual accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The scalar losses have uniformly bounded Clarke subgradients.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Influence Is Not Global Regularity
Robust-Loss Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable residual composites using losses with bounded marginal influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_m):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable. A robust-loss composite has the form \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x))\), where every \(\rho_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz and has uniformly bounded limiting subgradients: \(\sup\{|v|:t\in\mathbb R,\ v\in\partial\rho_i(t)\}<+\infty\). This bounded-influence condition prevents the marginal contribution of a single arbitrarily large residual from growing without bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust-loss composite sums scalar residual losses whose subgradients are uniformly bounded, limiting the marginal influence of extreme residuals.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied for the selected bounded-limiting-subgradient definition of robust loss or for its bounded-influence interpretation. Because competing notions of robustness exist, an authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Robust Residual Geometry
children.top_down_role: Curvature, weighting, or saturation effects created by robust losses on residual maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Residual Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobian-weighted geometry induced by differentiable robust residual losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x))\), the residual map \(r\) is continuously differentiable, and every \(\rho_i\) is differentiable. With \(w(x)=(\rho_1'(r_1(x)),\ldots,\rho_m'(r_m(x)))\), the chain rule gives \(\nabla F(x)=J_r(x)^\top w(x)\). If \(|\rho_i'(t)|\le M_i\) for all \(t\), then the norm of the contribution from residual \(i\) is at most \(M_i\|\nabla r_i(x)\|\), independently of \(|r_i(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient is a Jacobian-transposed weighted residual vector; bounded loss derivatives cap each residual's gradient contribution regardless of residual magnitude.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual accuracy and coercivity under saturated influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho'(t)\to0\) as \(|t|\to\infty\), arbitrarily large residuals can contribute arbitrarily little to \(\nabla F\), so stationarity need not imply small residuals. If \(\rho\) is bounded above, unbounded residual sequences can have bounded objective values, so coercivity requires separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redescending influence can hide large residuals, and bounded losses need not yield coercive objectives.
assumptions_latex: For the coercivity boundary, \(\rho\) is bounded above.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{bounded or redescending influence}\not\Rightarrow\text{small residuals or coercivity}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Redescending-Influence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact curvature decomposition for twice-differentiable separable robust losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\sum_i\rho_i(r_i(x))\), \[\nabla^2F(x)=J_r(x)^\top D(x)J_r(x)+\sum_i\rho_i'(r_i(x))\nabla^2r_i(x),\qquad D(x)=\operatorname{Diag}(\rho_i''(r_i(x))).\] The first term is positive semidefinite when \(D(x)\succeq0\); the correction vanishes for affine residuals but may otherwise make the exact Hessian indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust curvature splits into a loss-curvature-weighted Gauss-Newton term and a residual-map curvature correction.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_i\) and \(\rho_i\) is twice continuously differentiable near the point.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Residual Hessian Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted normal-equation representation underlying IRLS-type models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r_i(x)\neq0\), set \(a_i(x)=\rho_i'(r_i(x))/r_i(x)\), with a finite limiting value at zero when available. Then \(\nabla F(x)=J_r(x)^\top A(x)r(x)\), where \(A(x)=\operatorname{Diag}(a_i(x))\). Freezing nonnegative weights and linearizing \(r\) yields a weighted least-squares surrogate; negative weights destroy its convex least-squares interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust stationarity is a weighted normal equation, and frozen nonnegative weights yield an IRLS-type local model.
assumptions_latex: The ratios \(\rho_i'(t)/t\) used at nonzero residuals are finite.
A weighted least-squares interpretation additionally requires nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Frozen-Weight Least-Squares Model
Exact-Penalty Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness from a Lipschitz objective and a constraint-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(v:\mathbb R^n\to[0,+\infty)\), and let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:v(x)=0\}\) be closed. Suppose \(\bar x\in S\) is a local minimizer of \(F\) over \(S\), \(F\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) with constant \(L\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa v(x)\) for all \(x\) in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), where \(\kappa\ge0\). Then, for every \(\rho>L\kappa\), the point \(\bar x\) is a local unconstrained minimizer of \(Q_\rho:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), defined by \(Q_\rho(x)=F(x)+\rho v(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a locally Lipschitz objective has a local constrained minimizer and the constraint violation controls distance to the feasible set, then every penalty weight exceeding the Lipschitz constant times the error-bound modulus makes that point a local unconstrained minimizer of the penalized objective.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(v:\mathbb R^n\to[0,+\infty)\), \(S=v^{-1}(0)\) is closed, and \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(F\) over \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\rho>L\kappa\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \bar x\text{ is a local minimizer of }Q_\rho=F+\rho v\text{ on }\mathbb R^n.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Map Linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order affine replacement of the smooth inner map at a base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a continuously differentiable inner map \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and base point \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), its first-order affine model at displacement \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is \(c_x(d)=c(x)+J_c(x)d\). Differentiability gives \(c(x+d)=c_x(d)+o(\|d\|)\) as \(d\to0\). Thus a composite objective \(h(c(x+d))\) is modeled by \(h(c_x(d))\), with only the smooth inner map linearized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a base point, replace the smooth inner map by its affine first-order expansion while retaining the displacement-dependent approximation error.

notation.meaning: affine inner-map model at the base point

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order remainder bound for an inner map with Lipschitz Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(J_c\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the line segment \([x,x+d]\), in the operator norm induced by the chosen vector norms. Then
\[
\|c(x+d)-c(x)-J_c(x)d\|\leq\frac{L}{2}\|d\|^2.
\]
If \(c\) is affine, the remainder is identically zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz inner Jacobian gives a quadratic affine-linearization error, while affine inner maps are modeled exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \([x,x+d]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Inner-Linearization Remainder
Outer-Function Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized composite models retain the original convex outer function exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=h\circ c\), with \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) continuously differentiable and \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. At a base point \(x\), the outer-preserving linearized model is \(m_x(d)=h(c(x)+J_c(x)d)\). The function \(h\) is neither differentiated nor replaced by a quadratic approximation; consequently, its extended-valued domain restrictions and nonsmooth convex geometry remain present in the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite linearization changes only the smooth inner map; the original convex outer function, including its nonsmoothness and domain restrictions, remains intact.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: trial displacement from the base point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural Properties of the Preserved-Outer Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity, closedness, epigraph structure, and properness of the affine precomposition of the preserved outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_x(d)=h(c(x)+J_c(x)d)\), where \(h\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Then \(m_x\) is convex and lower semicontinuous, \[\operatorname{epi}m_x=\{(d,t):(c(x)+J_c(x)d,t)\in\operatorname{epi}h\}.\] Moreover, \(m_x\) is proper if and only if \((c(x)+\operatorname{range}J_c(x))\cap\operatorname{dom}h\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine precomposition preserves convexity and lower semicontinuity, and the model is proper exactly when the affine linearized image intersects the outer domain.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x\text{ is convex and lower semicontinuous},\qquad m_x\text{ is proper}\iff(c(x)+\operatorname{range}J_c(x))\cap\operatorname{dom}h\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Properties of the Preserved-Outer Model
Proximal Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic stabilization of an outer-preserving linearized composite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the linearized composite model \(m_x(d)=h(c(x)+J_c(x)d)\) and a parameter \(\mu>0\), its proximal stabilization is \(M_{x,\mu}(d)=m_x(d)+\tfrac{1}{2\mu}\|d\|_2^2\). A stabilized model step is any \(d_\mu(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}M_{x,\mu}(d)\), when this set is nonempty. The quadratic term penalizes large displacements and makes \(M_{x,\mu}\) strongly convex whenever \(m_x\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic displacement penalty to the linearized composite model and choose a minimizer as the stabilized step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Stabilized Step and Proximal Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, proximal representation, and exact optimality certificate for Euclidean stabilization of a closed convex model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex and \(\mu>0\), then \(M_{x,\mu}(d)=m_x(d)+\|d\|^2/(2\mu)\) has a unique minimizer \(d_\mu(x)\). It satisfies \[d_\mu(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\mu m_x}(0)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial m_x(d_\mu(x))+\mu^{-1}d_\mu(x).\] Consequently, \(-d_\mu(x)/\mu\in\partial m_x(d_\mu(x))\), and \(d_\mu(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\partial m_x(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex model has a unique stabilized step, equal to the proximal point of zero, and its scaled displacement is an exact model-subgradient certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(m_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: proximal mapping of the convex model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extended-Valued Outer Functions Can Destroy Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of objective-level accuracy without outer Lipschitz continuity or domain compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h=\delta_{\{0\}}\), \(c(x)=x^2\), and use the base point \(x=0\). Since \(c(0)=c'(0)=0\),
\[
m_0(s)=h(0)=0
\]
for every \(s\), whereas
\[
F(s)=h(s^2)=+\infty
\]
for every \(s\neq0\). Thus a quadratic inner-linearization error need not yield finite objective-model error when exact and linearized images interact differently with the outer domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton-indicator outer function shows that excellent inner-map accuracy need not produce objective-model accuracy without outer-domain regularity.

notation.meaning: indicator function of the singleton zero

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Valued Outer Functions Can Destroy Model Accuracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Propagation of Inner-Map Error Through a Lipschitz Outer Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-model agreement under local Lipschitz continuity of the outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=h\circ c\) and \(m_x(s)=h(c(x)+J_c(x)s)\). If \(c\) is differentiable at \(x\) and \(h\) is \(L_h\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood containing both relevant exact and modeled image values, then
\[
|F(x+s)-m_x(s)|\leq L_h\|c(x+s)-c(x)-J_c(x)s\|=o(\|s\|).
\]
If \(J_c\) is additionally locally \(L_c\)-Lipschitz, then
\[
|F(x+s)-m_x(s)|\leq\frac{L_hL_c}{2}\|s\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz outer function transfers the inner linearization error to the composite model, giving little-o accuracy and a quadratic bound under a Lipschitz inner Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is Lipschitz on all relevant exact and modeled image values.

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz constant of the outer function
local Lipschitz constant of the inner Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation of Inner-Map Error Through a Lipschitz Outer Function
Model-Accuracy Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error-order classification for linearized composite models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=h\circ c\), where \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is differentiable, and define \(m_x(s)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)s)\). For \(p>0\), the models form an order-\(p\) accuracy family on \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) if there exist \(\kappa,\delta>0\) such that
\[
|F(x+s)-m_x(s)|\leq \kappa\|s\|^{p+1}
\]
whenever \(x,x+s\in D\) and \(\|s\|\leq\delta\). If \(h\) is Lipschitz on the relevant image and \(\nabla c\) is Lipschitz, then this condition holds with \(p=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-accuracy family is classified by the order of the uniform error between the composite objective and its inner-map linearization.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(D\).
\(h\) is finite on the model and objective values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for the unstabilized convex-composite Gauss–Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a=c(x)\), \(J=\nabla c(x)\), and \(m_x(s)=h(a+Js)\). If \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex and \((a+\operatorname{range}J)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\neq\varnothing\), then
\[
0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_s m_x(s)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in J^{\mathsf T}\partial h(a).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the affine-composition qualification, zero minimizes the Gauss–Newton model exactly when an outer subgradient at the current inner value pulls back to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Step Model-Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Dual of the Positive-Definite Stabilized Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation and primal-dual optimality system for the stabilized convex-composite subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a=c(x)\), \(J=\nabla c(x)\), and \(B\succ0\). If \((a+\operatorname{range}J)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\neq\varnothing\), then
\[
\inf_s\left\{h(a+Js)+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\right\}
=
\sup_y\left\{\langle a,y\rangle-h^*(y)-\tfrac12(J^{\mathsf T}y)^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}(J^{\mathsf T}y)\right\}.
\]
Primal-dual solutions satisfy \(y\in\partial h(a+Js)\) and \(Bs+J^{\mathsf T}y=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite stabilized Gauss–Newton model has a Fenchel dual in the outer covector and an exact subgradient balance optimality system.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the outer function

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Dual of the Positive-Definite Stabilized Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitations of the convex generalized Gauss–Newton formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Convexity of
\[
s\mapsto h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)s)+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_xs
\]
follows from convexity of \(h\) and \(B_x\succeq0\), but can fail if either condition is removed. In one dimension, \(h\equiv0\) and \(B_x=-1\) give the unbounded model \(-s^2/2\); with \(B_x=0\) and \(h(t)=\min\{t^2,1\}\), the affine-composite model need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity of the outer function and positive-semidefinite stabilization are genuine requirements for convex-subproblem guarantees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h\text{ nonconvex or }B_x\not\succeq0\;\centernot\implies\;M_x\text{ convex or bounded below}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Stabilization Boundary
Generalized Gauss-Newton Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-composite generalized Gauss–Newton model with quadratic stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=h(c(x))\), with \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) differentiable and \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) proper, closed, and convex, a generalized Gauss–Newton model at \(x\) is
\[
M_x(s)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)s)+\tfrac12\langle s,B_xs\rangle,
\]
where \(B_x\succeq0\). A model step is any minimizer of \(M_x\), possibly subject to a trust region. The construction preserves the outer function while replacing only the inner map by its first-order approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized Gauss–Newton preserves the convex outer function, linearizes the smooth inner map, and may add positive-semidefinite quadratic stabilization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_x(s)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)s)+\frac12\langle s,B_xs\rangle\) is a convex model in \(s\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the convex-composite Gauss–Newton formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits generalized convex-composite Gauss-Newton models, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the stabilized formulation or the trust-region variant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent certificate for any exact solution of the Gauss–Newton normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=J^{\mathsf T}r=\nabla F(x)\), and suppose \(s\) satisfies \(J^{\mathsf T}Js=-g\). Then
\[
g^{\mathsf T}s=-s^{\mathsf T}J^{\mathsf T}Js=-\|Js\|^2\leq0.
\]
If \(g\neq0\), then \(Js\neq0\), so \(g^{\mathsf T}s<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact Gauss–Newton step is a descent direction for nonlinear least squares unless the current gradient vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Gauss–Newton Descent Identity
Nonlinear Least-Squares Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Gauss–Newton specialization for a squared Euclidean residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable and \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|^2\). With \(J(x)=\nabla r(x)\), the Gauss–Newton model is
\[
M_x(s)=\tfrac12\|r(x)+J(x)s\|^2.
\]
Every unconstrained minimizer satisfies
\[
J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)s=-J(x)^{\mathsf T}r(x).
\]
If \(J(x)\) has full column rank, the model has the unique minimizer determined by these normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonlinear least squares, linearizing the residual yields a quadratic model whose minimizer solves the Gauss–Newton normal equations.
review_flags: Standard formulation, but no directly relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The least-squares model, normal equations, and full-column-rank uniqueness statement are standard and match the container, but no source reference or specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudoinverse Description of All Gauss–Newton Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed complete solution-set representation for the linearized least-squares subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M_x(s)=\tfrac12\|r+Js\|^2\),
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_s M_x(s)=-J^\dagger r+\ker J.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All least-squares steps are the pseudoinverse step plus Jacobian-nullspace motion.
review_flags: Deferred as local duplication: pseudoinverse parameterization, minimum-norm selection, and nullspace behavior are already canonically housed in A06.C08.NEC20281262DC.AND88F8313713 and A06.C08.NEC20281262DC.AND6C1519B2A0.
