knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality condition for the stabilized separable convex robust-loss model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_i=r_i(x)\), \(J_i=\nabla r_i(x)^{\mathsf T}\), and
\[
M_x(s)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(a_i+J_is)+\frac1{2t}\|s\|^2.
\]
Suppose each \(\rho_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(t>0\), and there exists \(s\) with \(a_i+J_is\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}\rho_i)\) for every \(i\). Then \(s_\star\) is the unique minimizer exactly when there are \(u_i\in\partial\rho_i(a_i+J_is_\star)\) satisfying
\[
0=\sum_{i=1}^mJ_i^{\mathsf T}u_i+t^{-1}s_\star.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the affine-domain qualification, pulled-back robust-loss subgradients balance the proximal term exactly at the unique stabilized model minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
There exists \(s\) such that \(a_i+J_is\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}\rho_i)\) for all \(i\).

notation.meaning: subgradient of the ith robust loss at its modeled residual

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Model Optimality System

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convex-subproblem guarantees for nonconvex robust losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Preserving a nonconvex robust loss after affine residual linearization need not produce a convex subproblem. With affine modeled residual \(s\) and \(\rho(t)=\min\{t^2,1\}\), the model \(s\mapsto\min\{s^2,1\}\) is nonconvex. Consequently, convex uniqueness and global subgradient-optimality guarantees do not extend without additional restrictions or a convex majorizing surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex redescending-style losses can make the outer-preserving Gauss–Newton model nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Robust-Loss Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth robust-loss Gauss–Newton variant based on nonnegative influence weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\sum_i\rho_i(r_i(x))\), write \(\psi_i=\rho_i'\), and define
\[
w_i(t)=\psi_i(t)/t\quad(t\neq0),
\]
with any finite nonnegative continuous extension at \(t=0\) when available. Assume \(\psi_i(0)=0\) whenever \(r_i(x)=0\), and \(w_i(r_i(x))\geq0\). Then
\[
Q_x(s)=\frac12\sum_iw_i(r_i(x))\bigl(r_i(x)+\nabla r_i(x)^{\mathsf T}s\bigr)^2
\]
satisfies \(\nabla Q_x(0)=\nabla F(x)\) and has model matrix \(J(x)^{\mathsf T}W(x)J(x)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiable robust losses with finite nonnegative influence weights yield an IRLS Gauss–Newton model matching the objective gradient at the base point.
assumptions_latex: The weights \(w_i(r_i(x))\) are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteratively Reweighted Gauss–Newton Curvature
Robust-Loss Gauss-Newton Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable robust-loss model obtained by linearizing each smooth residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x))\), where each residual \(r_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and each loss \(\rho_i:\mathbb{R}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. The robust Gauss–Newton model at \(x\) is
\[
M_x(s)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x)+\nabla r_i(x)^{\mathsf T}s)+\tfrac{1}{2t}\|s\|^2,
\]
where \(t>0\). Thus nonsmooth kinks or robust tails in the losses are retained exactly, while only the residual maps are linearized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust Gauss–Newton model preserves each convex robust loss and applies it to the affine approximation of its residual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_x\) is a strongly convex stabilized robust-loss model.

notation.meaning: convex robust loss for residual i

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports this robust-loss model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is coherent for convex robust losses and fits the container, but no inspectable source supports this particular convex-loss and proximal-stabilization formulation. The convex restriction also needs source confirmation because robust-loss families may include nonconvex losses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Local Convergence at a Regular Zero-Residual Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical local rate for exact Gauss–Newton iteration in the regular zero-residual regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have a locally Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x_\star\), satisfy \(r(x_\star)=0\), and suppose \(J(x_\star)\) has full column rank. For \(x_0\) sufficiently close to \(x_\star\),
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\bigl(J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k\bigr)^{-1}J_k^{\mathsf T}r(x_k)
\]
is well defined and obeys
\[
\|x_{k+1}-x_\star\|\leq C\|x_k-x_\star\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz residual Jacobian and full column rank at a zero-residual solution give local quadratic convergence of exact Gauss–Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Local Convergence at a Regular Zero-Residual Solution
Zero-Residual Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order agreement of least-squares and Gauss–Newton curvature at zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|^2\), suppose \(r\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x_\star\) and \(r(x_\star)=0\). Then
\[
\nabla^2F(x_\star)=J(x_\star)^{\mathsf T}J(x_\star),
\]
because the residual-weighted curvature term vanishes. Hence the Hessian of the Gauss–Newton quadratic model equals the exact Hessian of \(F\) at \(x_\star\). If \(J(x_\star)\) has full column rank, this common Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-residual solution, the omitted residual-weighted second derivatives vanish, so Gauss–Newton has exact objective curvature.
review_flags: Standard identity, but a directly supporting source is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-residual Hessian identity and the full-column-rank consequence are standard and correctly scoped, but the record has no citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=x^2\), Gauss–Newton gives \(x_{k+1}=x_k/2\), so convergence to the zero-residual solution is only Q-linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular zero-residual example converges only linearly.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonzero-Residual Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature discrepancy for least squares at a nonzero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|^2\), with twice continuously differentiable components \(r_i\),
\[
\nabla^2F(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)\nabla^2r_i(x).
\]
When \(r(x_\star)\neq0\), the Gauss–Newton matrix \(J(x_\star)^{\mathsf T}J(x_\star)\) generally omits a nonvanishing curvature term. Consequently, exact second-order agreement cannot be inferred from smoothness alone; it requires additional structure or cancellation of the displayed sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonzero residual, Gauss–Newton generally differs from the exact Hessian by residual-weighted second derivatives of the residual components.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_i\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x_\star\).
review_flags: Standard identity, but a directly supporting source is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hessian decomposition and the qualified nonzero-residual conclusion match the container, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Regime Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative decay of Gauss–Newton curvature error as residuals approach zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|^2\), and suppose \(\|\nabla^2r_i(x)\|\leq L_i\) on a neighborhood \(U\). Then for every \(x\in U\),
\[
\|\nabla^2F(x)-J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)\|\leq\sum_{i=1}^m L_i|r_i(x)|\leq\|L\|\,\|r(x)\|,
\]
where \(L=(L_1,\ldots,L_m)\). Thus the curvature discrepancy decreases continuously to zero along any sequence in \(U\) whose residual norms converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Gauss–Newton curvature error is bounded linearly by residual size when residual-component Hessians are uniformly bounded.
review_flags: Derived standard bound lacks a directly supporting source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-dependent curvature bound is plausible, but it has no supporting locator and does not explicitly identify the matrix, vector, and dual norm conventions needed for the second inequality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Merit Representation of Residual Zeros
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite scalar merit representation of a residual equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfies \(\psi(z)=0\iff z=0\), then \(F(x)=0\iff r(x)=0\). If \(r^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname*{argmin}F=r^{-1}(0)\). The equivalence fails if \(\psi\) vanishes away from zero or takes a value below \(\psi(0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite outer merit represents residual zeros exactly as its zero-valued global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Merit Representation of Residual Zeros

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation-neutral composition of an outer merit with a residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a residual-map composition is \(F=\psi\circ r\). Its effective domain is exactly \(\operatorname{dom}F=r^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)=\{x:r(x)\in\operatorname{dom}\psi\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual-map composition applies an outer merit to a vector residual, and its domain is the residual preimage of the outer domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Map Composition and Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified first-order calculus for a convex outer merit and smooth residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(r\in C^1\) and \(\psi\) is proper closed convex, then \(\partial(\psi\circ r)(\bar x)\subseteq J_r(\bar x)^\top\partial\psi(r(\bar x))\). Equality holds under a valid convex-composite qualification, for example continuity of \(\psi\) at \(r(\bar x)\). Every finite local minimizer consequently satisfies \(0\in J_r(\bar x)^\top\partial\psi(r(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified convex-outer subgradients pull back through the residual Jacobian, yielding a necessary stationarity condition.
assumptions_latex: For equality, a valid qualification holds at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\in J_r(\bar x)^\top\partial\psi(r(\bar x))\quad\text{at every finite local minimizer}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Map Composite Chain Rule
Residual-Map Compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite objectives formed by applying an outer merit function to a residual map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be a residual map and \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) an outer merit function. A residual-map composition is the extended-real objective
\[
F(x)=\psi(r(x)).
\]
Its domain is \(\operatorname{dom}F=\{x:r(x)\in\operatorname{dom}\psi\}\). When \(r\) is differentiable at \(x\), the associated first-order composite residual model is \(s\mapsto\psi(r(x)+\nabla r(x)s)\), optionally augmented by a convex stabilization term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual-map composition applies an outer merit function to a vector residual; its local model preserves the merit function and linearizes the residual.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats composite residual models.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and domain identity fit residual-map compositions, but the associated linearized-model statement is unsupported because no source reference or locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of residual-model accuracy through a locally Lipschitz outer merit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the hypotheses of the quadratic residual bound hold and \(\psi\) is \(L_\psi\)-Lipschitz on a set containing both \(r(x+s)\) and \(\widehat r_x(s)\), then \[|\psi(r(x+s))-\psi(\widehat r_x(s))|\le\frac{L_\psi L_J}{2}\|s\|^2.\] Without local Lipschitz continuity at the relevant residual values, quadratic residual accuracy need not transfer to merit accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz outer merit converts quadratic residual-model error into quadratic merit-model error.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi\) is \(L_\psi\)-Lipschitz on a set containing the exact and modeled residual values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order affine model generated by a residual value and classical Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a residual map \(r\) Fréchet differentiable at \(x\), define \(\widehat r_x(s)=r(x)+J_r(x)s\). Then \(r(x+s)=\widehat r_x(s)+o(\|s\|)\). If \(J_r\) is \(L_J\)-Lipschitz on the segment \([x,x+s]\), then \(\|r(x+s)-\widehat r_x(s)\|\le L_J\|s\|^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual-Jacobian model is the affine first-order residual approximation, with quadratic error under a segmentwise Lipschitz Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: For the quadratic estimate, \(J_r\) is \(L_J\)-Lipschitz on every point of \([x,x+s]\).

notation.meaning: affine residual model at the base point

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Residual-Jacobian Model
Residual-Jacobian Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine residual model generated by a residual value and Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable at \(x\), with Jacobian \(J(x)=\nabla r(x)\). The residual-Jacobian model is
\[
\widehat r_x(s)=r(x)+J(x)s.
\]
If \(r\) is Fréchet differentiable, then \(r(x+s)=\widehat r_x(s)+o(\|s\|)\) as \(s\to0\). If \(J\) is locally Lipschitz with constant \(L_J\), then for sufficiently small feasible steps,
\[
\|r(x+s)-\widehat r_x(s)\|\leq\tfrac{L_J}{2}\|s\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual-Jacobian model is the affine first-order approximation of a residual map, with quadratic error under a Lipschitz Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: For the quadratic bound, \(\nabla r\) is locally \(L_J\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat r_x(s)=r(x)+J(x)s\), with local error \(o(\|s\|)\) or at most \(L_J\|s\|^2/2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for the stabilized model step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unique minimizer of the proper stabilized model is characterized by \(0\in A^\top\partial\psi(b+As_{x,t})+t^{-1}s_{x,t}\). Equivalently, there exists \(y\in\partial\psi(b+As_{x,t})\) with \(s_{x,t}=-tA^\top y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model step balances a pulled-back outer subgradient against quadratic stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Merit Model Optimality System

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth convex outer merit preserved over an affine residual model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b=r(x)\), \(A=J_r(x)\), and \(t>0\). If \((b+\operatorname{range}A)\cap\operatorname{dom}\psi\neq\varnothing\), then \(M_{x,t}(s)=\psi(b+As)+\|s\|^2/(2t)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and strongly convex. It therefore has a unique minimizer \(s_{x,t}\). If the affine image misses \(\operatorname{dom}\psi\), the model is identically \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving a proper closed convex outer merit and adding quadratic stabilization gives a unique model step exactly when the affine residual reaches the outer domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Proper Stabilized Outer-Merit Model
Nonsmooth Outer Merit Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual model retaining a proper closed convex nonsmooth merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\psi(r(x))\), where \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is differentiable and \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, possibly nonsmooth. For \(t>0\), the stabilized outer-merit model is
\[
M_{x,t}(s)=\psi(r(x)+\nabla r(x)s)+\tfrac{1}{2t}\|s\|^2.
\]
It is strongly convex in \(s\), so whenever it attains its infimum it has a unique minimizer. Nonsmoothness of \(\psi\) is retained rather than differentiated away.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsmooth outer-merit model applies the original convex merit function to the affine residual and adds proximal stabilization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{x,t}\) is strongly convex and has at most one minimizer.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports this prox-linear merit model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The model form fits the container, but no inspectable source supports it. Moreover, properness of the affine composition is not guaranteed merely by properness of the outer function; a source-backed qualification ensuring a nonempty effective domain is needed before asserting a proper strongly convex subproblem.

children.title: Exact Prox-Linear Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Prox-linear variants based on exact resolution of each convex model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Exact Step and Composite Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact zero-displacement certificate under the convex-composite chain-rule qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the affine-composition qualification, let \(x^+\) be the exact minimizer of \(Q_t(\cdot;x)\). Then \[x^+=x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla c(x)^\top\partial h(c(x)).\] Under the corresponding exact chain rule for \(h\circ c\) at \(x\), these conditions are also equivalent to \(0\in\partial(h\circ c)(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standard chain-rule qualification, the exact prox-linear displacement is zero exactly at a composite stationary point.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex and \(c\) is differentiable at \(x\).
The exact prox-linear subproblem is proper.
The stated affine and nonlinear composite chain rules are exact at the relevant points.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Exact Step and Composite Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Dual of the Exact Prox-Linear Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of the stabilized affine-composite subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(b=c(x)\), \(J=\nabla c(x)\), and \(d=z-x\). If \((b+\operatorname{range}J)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\neq\varnothing\), then \[\min_d\left\{h(b+Jd)+\frac1{2t}\|d\|^2\right\}=\max_u\left\{\langle u,b\rangle-h^*(u)-\frac t2\|J^\top u\|^2\right\}.\] Whenever \(u^\star\) is dual optimal, the unique primal step satisfies \(d^\star=-tJ^\top u^\star\) and \(u^\star\in\partial h(b+Jd^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, the exact prox-linear subproblem has a Fenchel dual whose optimal multiplier recovers the unique primal step.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex and \(t>0\).
The primal affine composite is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_d h(b+Jd)+\|d\|^2/(2t)=\max_u \langle u,b\rangle-h^*(u)-t\|J^\top u\|^2/2\), with \(d^\star=-tJ^\top u^\star\) when the dual optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Dual of the Exact Prox-Linear Subproblem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness and Exact Optimality of the Prox-Linear Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural characterization of an exactly solved stabilized convex-composite linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\) and \(t>0\), define \(A_x(z)=c(x)+\nabla c(x)(z-x)\), and suppose \(h\circ A_x\) is proper. Then \(Q_t(z;x)=h(A_x(z))+\frac{1}{2t}\|z-x\|^2\) is proper, closed, and \(1/t\)-strongly convex, and therefore has a unique minimizer \(x^+\). It satisfies \[0\in\partial(h\circ A_x)(x^+)+\frac1t(x^+-x).\] Under the affine-composition qualification, this is equivalently \[\exists u\in\partial h(A_x(x^+)):\quad \nabla c(x)^\top u+\frac1t(x^+-x)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper exact prox-linear subproblem has a unique solution characterized by a convex optimality inclusion and, under qualification, an outer-subgradient multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier form additionally assumes the standard affine-composition qualification.

notation.meaning: Affine linearization of c at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness and Exact Optimality of the Prox-Linear Subproblem
Exact Prox-Linear Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact step rule for the convex-composite prox-linear method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}(h\circ c)\) and \(t_k>0\), form
\[
Q_k(z)=h(c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)(z-x_k))+\tfrac{1}{2t_k}\|z-x_k\|^2.
\]
Compute an exact minimizer \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}Q_k(z)\). Equivalently, with \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), solve the stabilized linearized composite subproblem to global optimality. Stop when \(\|s_k\|/t_k\) meets the prescribed stationarity tolerance; otherwise repeat from \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each exact prox-linear iteration globally minimizes the stabilized composite linearization and stops when the scaled step is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed subproblem attains its minimum.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly documents the exact prox-linear iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic content kind and exact argmin rule fit the terminal container, but no source locator documents the iteration. The interpretation of the scaled step as a stationarity stopping measure also requires source-backed assumptions.

children.title: Inexact Prox-Linear Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Prox-linear variants permitting approximate model solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate effect of objective-gap subproblem error on prox-linear descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k(y)=g(y)+h(c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)(y-x_k))+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\). If \(h\) is \(L_h\)-Lipschitz, \(\nabla c\) is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz, and \(Q_k(z_k)\leq\inf Q_k+\varepsilon_k\), then \[F(z_k)\leq F(x_k)+\varepsilon_k-\frac{1-t_kL_h\beta}{2t_k}\|z_k-x_k\|^2.\] Thus, for \(t_kL_h\beta<1\), this estimate certifies strict descent only when \(\varepsilon_k<\frac{1-t_kL_h\beta}{2t_k}\|z_k-x_k\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-gap error directly reduces the descent certified by an inexact prox-linear step and can eliminate it when too large.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex; \(h\) is convex and \(L_h\)-Lipschitz.
\(t_k>0\) and the displayed objective-gap criterion holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent Degradation Under Objective-Gap Inexactness
Inexact Prox-Linear Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap and stationarity-residual criteria for inexact subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the prox-linear subproblem \(Q_k\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), an objective-gap inexact solution \(z_k\) satisfies
\[
Q_k(z_k)\leq\inf_z Q_k(z)+\varepsilon_k.
\]
Alternatively, a stationarity-residual inexact solution has a computable vector \(v_k\in\partial Q_k(z_k)\) satisfying \(\|v_k\|\leq\eta_k\), where \(\eta_k\geq0\). The next iterate is \(x_{k+1}=z_k\). Exact solution is recovered when the selected tolerance is zero; convergence analyses must additionally prescribe how the tolerances decay or are summed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact prox-linear step is certified by a bounded subproblem objective gap or a bounded subgradient residual.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k\) is proper, closed, and strongly convex.
review_flags: The intended inexactness convention and convergence tolerance regime need a directly supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits the terminal container, and the two displayed criteria are recognizable inexactness certificates. No source locator establishes that these are the intended alternatives or specifies the tolerance regimes required by convergence analysis.

children.title: Subproblem Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Absolute, relative, adaptive, or certificate-driven inexactness classifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic calibration of gap, subgradient-residual, and solution-distance accuracy for a strongly convex subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with minimizer \(z^*\). If \(Q(z)-Q(z^*)\leq\varepsilon\), then \(\|z-z^*\|\leq\sqrt{2\varepsilon/\mu}\). If some \(v\in\partial Q(z)\) satisfies \(\|v\|\leq\eta\), then \[\|z-z^*\|\leq\eta/\mu,\qquad Q(z)-Q(z^*)\leq\eta^2/(2\mu).\] A distance bound alone gives neither an objective-gap upper bound nor a subgradient-norm upper bound without additional regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts gap or subgradient accuracy into distance accuracy and converts a subgradient residual into a gap bound; reverse conversions require more regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Conversion Between Accuracy Measures

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^d\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper, closed, and convex; \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex; and \(c:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable.
The prox-linear model is \(Q_t(y;x)=g(y)+h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+\frac{1}{2t}\|y-x\|^2\), where \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_k=0\) gives exact solves, \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\) gives asymptotically exact solves, and relative bounds tie inner accuracy to the outer residual.

notation.meaning: Prox-linear model at the current outer iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies exact, absolute-error, relative-error, and summable-error inner-solve criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), \(t_k>0\), and \(Q_k=Q_{t_k}(\cdot;x_k)\), an inexact point \(y_k\) satisfies an absolute objective-gap regime when \(Q_k(y_k)-\inf_y Q_k(y)\leq\varepsilon_k\), and a model-stationarity regime when \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial Q_k(y_k))\leq\varepsilon_k\). A relative regime requires either \(Q_k(y_k)-\inf Q_k\leq\eta_k\|y_k-x_k\|^2/(2t_k)\) or \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial Q_k(y_k))\leq\eta_k\|y_k-x_k\|/t_k\), with \(0\leq\eta_k<1\). Exact, asymptotically exact, and summably inexact regimes correspond respectively to \(\varepsilon_k=0\), \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), and \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prox-linear subproblems may be solved exactly or under absolute, relative, vanishing, or summable error criteria measured by model gap or model stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Accuracy Regimes

children.title: Prox-Linear Backtracking Variants
children.top_down_role: Variants globalized through trial-parameter contraction plus acceptance tests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Backtracking under a Quadratic Model-Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for finite termination of the inner stepsize-contraction loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell_x(y)=g(y)+h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))\), suppose \(F(y)\leq\ell_x(y)+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) at every trial point, and let \(y_t\) globally minimize \(Q_t(y;x)=\ell_x(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\|y-x\|^2\). Then \[F(y_t)\leq F(x)-\frac{1-tL}{2t}\|y_t-x\|^2.\] Consequently, for \(0<\sigma<1\), the test \(F(y_t)\leq F(x)-\frac{\sigma}{2t}\|y_t-x\|^2\) holds whenever \(t\leq(1-\sigma)/L\). Repeated contraction \(t\leftarrow\gamma t\), with \(0<\gamma<1\), therefore terminates after finitely many trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic upper bound on linearization error guarantees finite backtracking once the trial stepsize reaches an explicit threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(y_t\) is an exact global minimizer of \(Q_t(\cdot;x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\leq(1-\sigma)/L\Longrightarrow F(y_t)\leq F(x)-\sigma\|y_t-x\|^2/(2t)\), so geometric backtracking terminates finitely.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Backtracking under a Quadratic Model-Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Complexity of Accepted Prox-Linear Backtracking Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-step bound under a uniform accepted-stepsize lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose accepted trials satisfy \[F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-\frac{\sigma}{2t_k}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\qquad t_k\ge t_{\min}>0,\] where \(0<\sigma<1\), and define \(G_{t_k}(x_k)=(x_k-x_{k+1})/t_k\). If \(F\ge F_{\inf}\), then for every \(K\ge1\), \[\min_{0\le k<K}\|G_{t_k}(x_k)\|^2\le\frac{2(F(x_0)-F_{\inf})}{\sigma t_{\min}K}.\] Consequently, at most \(\lceil2(F(x_0)-F_{\inf})/(\sigma t_{\min}\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) accepted steps suffice to obtain \(\|G_{t_k}(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive accepted stepsizes turn the backtracking decrease test into an inverse-square stationarity bound.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted step satisfies the stated quadratic decrease test.

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on accepted stepsizes

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Complexity of Accepted Prox-Linear Backtracking Steps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Accepted-Stepsize Bound under Fixed Reinitialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-stepsize lower bound and inner-trial count for bounded reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(L>0\) and that the decrease test is guaranteed whenever \(t\le t_{\mathrm{acc}}:=(1-\sigma)/L\). At every outer iteration initialize \(t_k^{\mathrm{init}}\in[\underline t,\overline t]\), where \(0<\underline t\le\overline t<\infty\), and replace \(t\leftarrow\gamma t\), \(0<\gamma<1\), until acceptance. Then every accepted stepsize satisfies \[t_k\ge\min\{\underline t,\gamma t_{\mathrm{acc}}\},\] and the number of rejected trials is at most \[\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(\overline t/t_{\mathrm{acc}})}{\log(1/\gamma)}\right\rceil\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded reinitialization supplies the accepted-stepsize lower bound and a uniform bound on rejected trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_k\ge\min\{\underline t,\gamma(1-\sigma)/L\}\), with the stated rejection bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Accepted-Stepsize Bound under Fixed Reinitialization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backtracking May Fail without Quadratic Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar failure of stepsize contraction when the model error is subquadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x=0\), let \(\ell_0(z)=-z\), \(F(0)=0\), and \(F(z)=-z+\sqrt{|z|}\). The exact minimizer of \(\ell_0(z)+z^2/(2t)\) is \(y_t=t\). For \(0<\sigma<1\), the test \[F(y_t)\le F(0)-\frac{\sigma}{2t}|y_t|^2\] is equivalent to \[\sqrt t\le(1-\sigma/2)t.\] It therefore fails for every sufficiently small \(t\). Geometric contraction from such an initialization never obtains acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a quadratic upper model-error bound, shortening the stepsize can perpetually fail the prox-linear decrease test.
assumptions_latex: Each trial model is minimized exactly.

notation.meaning: exact trial minimizer at stepsize t

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking May Fail without Quadratic Model Accuracy

assumptions_latex: Each trial prox-linear subproblem has an exact minimizer, and \(F\) is bounded below on the generated level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted nonstationary step satisfies \(F(x_{k+1})<F(x_k)\), while repeated contraction of \(t\) eventually enforces acceptance under the usual composite smoothness bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone Armijo-type backtracking for exact prox-linear trial steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(t=t_k^{\mathrm{init}}>0\), \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\). Compute \(y\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z Q_t(z;x_k)\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=y\) and \(t_k=t\) when \[F(y)\leq F(x_k)-\frac{\sigma}{2t}\|y-x_k\|^2.\] If the test fails, replace \(t\leftarrow\gamma t\), recompute the trial minimizer, and repeat. Stop when an accepted step satisfies \(\|y-x_k\|/t\leq\epsilon\); otherwise return the last accepted iterate after the prescribed outer-iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking repeatedly shortens the trial stepsize until the exact prox-linear step produces a prescribed quadratic decrease in the objective.

children.title: Adaptive-Regularization Variants
children.top_down_role: Variants globalized through dynamic model-regularization parameters.

assumptions_latex: The trial model \(M_\mu(y;x)=g(y)+h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularization parameter is increased after unreliable models and may be decreased after highly reliable models; accepted trials satisfy a positive actual-to-predicted reduction test.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio-based adaptive regularization of exact prox-linear models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\) and \(\mu_k>0\), compute \(y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y M_{\mu_k}(y;x_k)\), set \(\operatorname{pred}_k=F(x_k)-M_{\mu_k}(y_k;x_k)\), and, when \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), define \(\rho_k=(F(x_k)-F(y_k))/\operatorname{pred}_k\). For thresholds \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\) and factors \(\gamma_+>1\), \(\gamma_-\in(0,1)\), accept \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) iff \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Increase \(\mu_k\) by \(\gamma_+\) after rejection, decrease it by \(\gamma_-\) when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\), and otherwise retain it. Stop when \(\mu_k\|y_k-x_k\|\leq\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive regularization accepts trials according to actual versus predicted reduction, increasing curvature after poor agreement and decreasing it after strong agreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Regularization Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the adaptive-regularization leaf, and the ratio construction is mathematically plausible. No source identifies this exact predicted-reduction denominator, acceptance policy, curvature update, or stopping residual, so the variant cannot be reviewed reliably without a specific algorithm or section citation.

children.title: Globalization Mechanism Comparison
children.top_down_role: Structural differences in acceptance, rejection, plus parameter adaptation.

assumptions_latex: Both mechanisms use the same exact composite linearization model and a positive quadratic coefficient.
An accepted trial is required to satisfy a fixed positive decrease or agreement threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(\mu=1/t\), both mechanisms globalize the same local step; they differ in whether model reliability is tested by sufficient decrease or by an actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares monotone backtracking with ratio-based adaptive regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The backtracking model \(Q_t(y;x)\) and regularized model \(M_\mu(y;x)\) coincide when \(\mu=1/t\). Backtracking changes \(t\) until the accepted minimizer obeys \(F(y)\leq F(x)-\sigma\|y-x\|^2/(2t)\). Ratio-based regularization instead changes \(\mu\) using \(\rho=(F(x)-F(y))/(F(x)-M_\mu(y;x))\) and accepts when \(\rho\geq\eta_1>0\). Thus both reject inaccurate local models by increasing quadratic curvature, but only the ratio mechanism distinguishes moderately successful from highly successful trials and permits a two-sided curvature update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking and adaptive regularization use the same quadratic model under reciprocal parameters, but test reliability using sufficient decrease and reduction ratios, respectively.
knowledge_statements.title: Globalization Mechanism Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role is appropriate for a comparison leaf, and the reciprocal identity between the two displayed models is correct. children.title: Accelerated Prox-Linear Variants
children.top_down_role: Prox-linear variants targeting improved complexity through extrapolation or estimate structures.

assumptions_latex: \(F=g+h\circ c\) is convex, and every extrapolated prox-linear subproblem is well posed.
A stepsize \(t>0\) is chosen within the range required by the composite model-error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns \(x_N\), or stops earlier when \(\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|/t\leq\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A FISTA-style extrapolated prox-linear iteration without asserting a rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_{-1}=x_0\), \(\theta_0=1\), and choose \(t>0\). For \(k\geq0\), set \(\theta_{k+1}=(1+\sqrt{1+4\theta_k^2})/2\), \(\beta_k=(\theta_k-1)/\theta_{k+1}\), and \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\). Compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{g(x)+h(c(y_k)+\nabla c(y_k)(x-y_k))+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-y_k\|^2\right\}.\] Stop and return \(x_{k+1}\) when \(\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|/t\leq\epsilon\); otherwise continue to the iteration limit. Any accelerated rate requires additional structure beyond this update specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accelerated variant extrapolates with Nesterov parameters and takes a prox-linear step from the extrapolated point; rate claims require additional structural assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_{-1}=x_0\). At iteration \(k\), form \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and compute \(z_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z Q_{t_k}(z;y_k)\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=z_k\) if \[F(z_k)\leq F(x_k)-\frac{\sigma}{2t_k}\|z_k-y_k\|^2\] for a fixed \(\sigma\in(0,1)\). If the test fails, reset \(y_k=x_k\), recompute \(z_k\), and apply the underlying noninertial acceptance rule, including stepsize backtracking if necessary. Stop when the accepted model-step residual \(\|z_k-y_k\|/t_k\) is at most \(\epsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Quadratic Stability Region for Constant Inertia
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-stability boundary for the scalar quadratic specialization of an unsafeguarded extrapolated prox-linear step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\lambda x^2/2\), \(\lambda>0\), consider \(y_k=x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and \(x_{k+1}=(1-t\lambda)y_k\). With \(a=1-t\lambda\), the characteristic polynomial is \(p(r)=r^2-a(1+\beta)r+a\beta\). Both roots lie strictly inside the unit disk if and only if \[|a\beta|<1,\qquad 1-a>0,\qquad 1+a(1+2\beta)>0.\] Failure of any inequality means that the recurrence is not strictly Schur stable and has a characteristic root of modulus at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three explicit Jury inequalities exactly characterize stability of the constant-inertia scalar quadratic recurrence.
assumptions_latex: No restart or descent safeguard is used.

notation.meaning: Characteristic polynomial of the two-step recurrence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quadratic divergence boundary for unsafeguarded inertial prox-linear steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\lambda x^2/2\), the extrapolated gradient, hence prox-linear, update is \(y_k=x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\) and \(x_{k+1}=(1-t\lambda)y_k\). Its characteristic polynomial is \[r^2-(1-t\lambda)(1+\beta)r+(1-t\lambda)\beta=0.\] With \(\beta=1\) and \(t\lambda=3\), this becomes \(r^2+4r-2=0\), whose roots are \(-2\pm\sqrt{6}\); one has modulus greater than one. Except for initial data lying in the stable eigenspace, the iterates therefore diverge, showing that unrestricted momentum cannot inherit the noninertial descent guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a convex quadratic, an unsafeguarded inertial prox-linear update can diverge when momentum and stepsize violate the recurrence stability region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional mean and variance for uniform with-replacement snapshot corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(i_1,\ldots,i_b\) be conditionally independent and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), set \(\Delta_i=c_i(y)-c_i(\widetilde x)\), and let \(\bar\Delta=n^{-1}\sum_i\Delta_i\). For \(\widehat c=c(\widetilde x)+b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^b\Delta_{i_j}\), \[\mathbb E[\widehat c\mid y,\widetilde x]=c(y),\qquad \mathbb E[\|\widehat c-c(y)\|^2\mid y,\widetilde x]=\frac1{bn}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\Delta_i-\bar\Delta\|^2.\] The analogous identity holds for the Jacobian estimator with the Frobenius norm. Both variances vanish at \(y=\widetilde x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform snapshot corrections are conditionally unbiased, have variance proportional to the inverse batch size, and are exact at the snapshot.
assumptions_latex: Indices are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement conditional on \(y\) and \(\widetilde x\).
The component differences have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\widehat c\mid y,\widetilde x]=c(y),\qquad \mathbb E[\|\widehat c-c(y)\|^2\mid y,\widetilde x]=\frac1{bn}\sum_i\|\Delta_i-\bar\Delta\|^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Snapshot Control-Variate Variance Identity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Importance Weighting for Nonuniform Snapshot Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased snapshot correction under positive nonuniform component probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let indices be sampled independently with probabilities \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\). For \(c(y)=n^{-1}\sum_i c_i(y)\), \[\widehat c=c(\widetilde x)+\frac1b\sum_{j=1}^b\frac{c_{i_j}(y)-c_{i_j}(\widetilde x)}{np_{i_j}}\] satisfies \(\mathbb E[\widehat c\mid y,\widetilde x]=c(y)\). Without the factors \((np_i)^{-1}\), the estimator instead targets \(c(\widetilde x)+\sum_i p_i(c_i(y)-c_i(\widetilde x))\), generally not \(c(y)\). The same condition applies to the Jacobian correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonuniform component sampling requires inverse-probability weights; unweighted snapshot corrections are generally biased.
assumptions_latex: Samples are conditionally independent given \(y\) and \(\widetilde x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat c\mid y,\widetilde x]=c(y)\) when each correction is divided by \(np_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Importance Weighting for Nonuniform Snapshot Sampling

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(y)=0\), let \(\widehat c\in\{-1,1\}\) with equal probabilities, and take \(h(z)=z^2\). Then \[\mathbb E[\widehat c]=c(y)=0,\qquad \mathbb E[h(\widehat c)]=1>0=h(c(y)).\] Thus unbiased inner-map estimation does not make a model containing a nonlinear outer composition unbiased.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\) contain \(b_k\) indices sampled independently and uniformly with replacement, independently of the past, and define \[v_k=v_{k-1}+\frac1{b_k}\sum_{i\in B_k}(c_i(y_k)-c_i(y_{k-1})).\] With \(e_k=v_k-c(y_k)\), \(\delta_i=c_i(y_k)-c_i(y_{k-1})\), and \(\bar\delta=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_i\), \[\mathbb E[e_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]=e_{k-1},\] \[\mathbb E[\|e_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]=\|e_{k-1}\|^2+\frac1{b_kn}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\delta_i-\bar\delta\|^2.\] Hence an imperfect initialization is transported rather than removed. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nearby-Point Transfer Cannot Generally Be Replaced by Base-Point Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of reporting stationarity at a nearby point rather than at the current base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=|x|\), represented by \(g=0\), \(h(z)=|z|\), and \(c(x)=x\). For fixed \(t>0\), \(x_t^+(x)=\operatorname{sign}(x)\max\{|x|-t,0\}\). Thus, for \(0<x<t\), \[x_t^+(x)=0,\qquad \|G_t(x)\|=x/t\to0\quad(x\downarrow0),\] whereas \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))=1.\] The nearby point \(x_t^+(x)=0\) is stationary, although the base point has no comparably small subgradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small prox-linear residual need not imply a small subgradient at the base point; stationarity may only hold at a nearby point.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Point Transfer Cannot Generally Be Replaced by Base-Point Stationarity

assumptions_latex: \(F=g+h\circ c\), where \(g\) is proper closed convex, \(h\) is convex and \(L_h\)-Lipschitz, and \(c\) has \(L_c\)-Lipschitz Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), \(t>0\), and \(x^+=x_t^+(x)\). Then there exists \(\widehat x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) such that \[\|\widehat x-x^+\|\leq\|x^+-x\|,\qquad F(\widehat x)\leq F(x^+),\] and \[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial F(\widehat x)\bigr)\leq\bigl(2+3L_hL_ct\bigr)\|G_t(x)\|.\] Consequently, any sequence with bounded stepsizes and \(\|G_{t_k}(x_k)\|\to0\) admits associated nearby points \(\widehat x_k\) whose limiting-subdifferential stationarity residual converges to zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-composite prox-linear envelope defined by exact model minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), define \[x_t\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{y}\left\{g(y)+h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x)\bigr)+\frac{1}{2t}\|y-x\|^2\right\}\] and let \(\varphi_t(x)\) be the minimum value. The model objective is \(t^{-1}\)-strongly convex, so \(x_t\) is unique and \[\varphi(x)-\varphi_t(x)\ge \frac{1}{2t}\|x-x_t\|^2=\frac{t}{2}\|G_t(x)\|^2.\] Consequently, the envelope gap is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(x=x_t\), equivalently when the prox-linear residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The prox-linear envelope lies below the objective, and its gap controls the squared prox-linear residual; the gap vanishes exactly at model-stationary points.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Envelope Geometry

assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is the exact prox-linear point for parameter \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable stopping certificate for an exactly solved prox-linear model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The test \[\|G_t(x)\|\le\varepsilon\] is a verifiable prox-linear stopping certificate. It certifies both the step bound \[\|x-x_t\|=t\|G_t(x)\|\le t\varepsilon\] and, through strong convexity of the regularized model, the envelope-gap relation \[\frac{t}{2}\|G_t(x)\|^2\le\varphi(x)-\varphi_t(x).\] Thus a small residual certifies a small model displacement. This certificate concerns prox-linear model stationarity; conversion to a limiting-subdifferential residual for \(\varphi\) requires an additional stationarity-transfer result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stopping when the prox-linear residual is at most epsilon certifies a step of at most t epsilon and links the residual to the envelope gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Stopping Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Stationarity Certificate for Predicted Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicted-decrease lower bound from an approximate first-order certificate for a strongly convex regularized model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_{x,\sigma}(z)=M_x(z)+(\sigma/2)\|z-x\|^2\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, with \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\). If \(v\in\partial Q_{x,\sigma}(y)\) and \(\|v\|\le\varepsilon\), then the predicted decrease \(\Delta_{x,\sigma}(y):=\varphi(x)-Q_{x,\sigma}(y)\) satisfies \[\Delta_{x,\sigma}(y)\ge\frac{\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2-\varepsilon\|y-x\|.\] In particular, if \(\varepsilon\le\theta(\sigma/2)\|y-x\|\) for some \(\theta\in[0,1)\), then \[\Delta_{x,\sigma}(y)\ge(1-\theta)\frac{\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small regularized-model stationarity residual preserves a quantitative predicted-decrease bound, with an explicit loss proportional to the residual and step length.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_{x,\sigma}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\), the current point is a comparison point for the regularized subproblem. Strong convexity of \(Q_{x,\sigma}\) at its minimizer \(y\) gives \[Q_{x,\sigma}(x)-Q_{x,\sigma}(y)\ge\frac{\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] Hence the computable quantity \[\Delta_{x,\sigma}(y):=\varphi(x)-Q_{x,\sigma}(y)\] satisfies \[\Delta_{x,\sigma}(y)\ge\frac{\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] A positive value therefore certifies predicted descent, while \(\Delta_{x,\sigma}(y)=0\) forces \(y=x\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite acceptance threshold under quadratic model accuracy and exact convex regularized-model minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_x\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\), and suppose \(|\varphi(y)-M_x(y)|\le(\kappa/2)\|y-x\|^2\). If \(y\ne x\) minimizes \(Q_{x,\sigma}(z)=M_x(z)+(\sigma/2)\|z-x\|^2\), define \(\operatorname{pred}=\varphi(x)-M_x(y)\) and \(\operatorname{ared}=\varphi(x)-\varphi(y)\). Then \[\operatorname{pred}\ge\sigma\|y-x\|^2,\qquad\frac{\operatorname{ared}}{\operatorname{pred}}\ge1-\frac{\kappa}{2\sigma}.\] Consequently, any threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\) is attained whenever \(\sigma\ge\kappa/[2(1-\eta)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under quadratic model accuracy, sufficiently strong regularization forces actual-to-predicted agreement above any fixed threshold below one.
assumptions_latex: \(M_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Regularization Model-Agreement Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Large Regularization Can Fail without Quadratic Model Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar failure of large-regularization acceptance when model error is not quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x=0\), let \(M_0(z)=-z\), \(\varphi(0)=0\), and \(\varphi(z)=-z+\sqrt{|z|}\). For every \(\sigma>0\), the exact minimizer of \(M_0(z)+(\sigma/2)z^2\) is \(y_\sigma=1/\sigma\). Thus \[\operatorname{pred}=\frac1\sigma,\qquad \operatorname{ared}=\frac1\sigma-\frac1{\sqrt\sigma},\qquad \frac{\operatorname{ared}}{\operatorname{pred}}=1-\sqrt\sigma.\] Increasing \(\sigma\) therefore worsens agreement and eventually gives negative actual reduction. The error \(\varphi(y)-M_0(y)=\sqrt{|y|}\) has no local quadratic bound at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without quadratic model accuracy, arbitrarily large regularization need not produce an acceptable trial.
assumptions_latex: The regularized model is minimized exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Large Regularization Can Fail without Quadratic Model Accuracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Large-Regularization Agreement with Inexact Model Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite agreement threshold under relative first-order subproblem accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_{x,\sigma}(z)=M_x(z)+(\sigma/2)\|z-x\|^2\), where \(M_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex and \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\). Suppose \(|\varphi(y)-M_x(y)|\le(\kappa/2)\|y-x\|^2\), \(v\in\partial Q_{x,\sigma}(y)\), and \(\|v\|\le\tau\sigma\|y-x\|\) for \(0\le\tau<1\). For \(y\ne x\), define \(\operatorname{pred}=\varphi(x)-M_x(y)\) and \(\operatorname{ared}=\varphi(x)-\varphi(y)\). Then \[\operatorname{pred}\ge(1-\tau)\sigma\|y-x\|^2>0,\qquad \frac{\operatorname{ared}}{\operatorname{pred}}\ge1-\frac{\kappa}{2(1-\tau)\sigma}.\] Hence an agreement threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\) is guaranteed when \(\sigma\ge\kappa/[2(1-\tau)(1-\eta)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative model-stationarity error enlarges the sufficient regularization threshold by the factor one over one minus the relative error.
assumptions_latex: \(M_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Regularization Agreement with Inexact Model Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity transfer from an exact regularized-model solution to the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) minimize \(M_x(z)+(\sigma/2)\|z-x\|^2\), where \(M_x\) is proper, closed, and convex. Suppose \(\operatorname{dist}(u,\partial\varphi(y))\le \kappa\|y-x\|\) for every \(u\in\partial M_x(y)\). Then \(-\sigma(y-x)\in\partial M_x(y)\) and \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\varphi(y))\le(\sigma+\kappa)\|y-x\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small exact regularized-model displacement certifies approximate stationarity when model and objective subgradients agree to first order.
assumptions_latex: The regularized model is minimized exactly.
The stated model-to-objective subgradient-consistency bound holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized-Model Displacement Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-step complexity under bounded regularization and subgradient-consistent exact models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(N\) accepted exact regularized-model trials \(x_{k+1}\ne x_k\), with \(\sigma_k\in[\underline\sigma,\overline\sigma]\), agreement ratio at least \(\eta>0\), and \(\inf\varphi> -\infty\). If \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\varphi(x_{k+1}))\le(\sigma_k+\kappa)\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\), then \[\min_{0\le k<N}\operatorname{dist}^2(0,\partial\varphi(x_{k+1}))\le\frac{(\overline\sigma+\kappa)^2[\varphi(x_0)-\inf\varphi]}{\eta\underline\sigma N}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease and the displacement certificate give inverse-square accepted-step stationarity complexity.
assumptions_latex: Every counted trial is accepted with ratio at least \(\eta>0\).
The objective is bounded below and the stated stationarity certificate holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Accepted-Step Stationarity Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consecutive Rejection Bound under Geometric Regularization Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Episode-local trial bound once a finite acceptance threshold is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every trial with \(\sigma\ge\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}>0\) is accepted, and every rejected trial replaces \(\sigma\) by a value at least \(\gamma_{\uparrow}\sigma\), where \(\gamma_{\uparrow}>1\). Starting from \(\sigma_0>0\), the number of consecutive rejected trials before acceptance is at most \[\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}/\sigma_0)}{\log\gamma_{\uparrow}}\right\rceil\right\}.\] Under the prior quadratic model-accuracy and relative stationarity assumptions, one may take \(\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}=\kappa/[2(1-\tau)(1-\eta)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric parameter increases and a finite acceptance threshold give a logarithmic bound on consecutive rejected trials.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma_{\uparrow}>1\), and each rejection increases \(\sigma\) by at least this factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Consecutive Rejection Bound under Geometric Regularization Growth

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Rejection Bound with Controlled Post-Acceptance Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total rejected-trial bound for multiplicative regularization updates over finitely many accepted steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose rejected trials update \(\sigma\leftarrow\gamma_{\uparrow}\sigma\), where \(\gamma_{\uparrow}>1\), every \(\sigma\ge\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}\) is accepted, and after each acceptance the next parameter satisfies \(\sigma^+\ge\gamma_{\downarrow}\sigma\), where \(0<\gamma_{\downarrow}\le1\). If \(N\) trials are accepted and \(R_N\) are rejected before and between them, then \[R_N\le \left\lceil\frac{\log(\max\{\sigma_0,\gamma_{\uparrow}\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}\}/\sigma_0)+N\log(1/\gamma_{\downarrow})}{\log\gamma_{\uparrow}}\right\rceil.\] Consequently, \(R_N=O(N+\log_+(\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}/\sigma_0))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlled decreases after successful trials and geometric increases after rejection give a global linear bound on rejected trials.

notation.meaning: total rejected trials associated with the first N accepted trials

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio-based globalization of convex composite models under a finite large-regularization acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At accepted iterate \(x_k\), choose \(\sigma>0\) and compute \(y\) with \(v\in\partial Q_{x_k,\sigma}(y)\), \(Q_{x_k,\sigma}(z)=M_{x_k}(z)+(\sigma/2)\|z-x_k\|^2\), and \(\|v\|\le\tau\sigma\|y-x_k\|\), where \(0\le\tau<1\). If \(y=x_k\), invoke the associated displacement-stationarity test. Otherwise set \(\operatorname{pred}=\varphi(x_k)-M_{x_k}(y)>0\), \(\operatorname{ared}=\varphi(x_k)-\varphi(y)\), and \(\rho=\operatorname{ared}/\operatorname{pred}\). If \(\rho\ge\eta\), accept \(x_{k+1}=y\) and choose \(\sigma_{k+1}\in[\gamma_{\downarrow}\sigma,\sigma]\); if \(\rho<\eta\), keep \(x_k\), replace \(\sigma\) by \(\gamma_{\uparrow}\sigma\), and recompute the trial. Here \(0<\eta<1\), \(\gamma_{\uparrow}>1\), and \(0<\gamma_{\downarrow}\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve increasingly regularized models until actual and predicted reductions agree, accept successful trials, and permit controlled regularization decreases after acceptance.
assumptions_latex: \(M_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(M_x(x)=\varphi(x)\).
Each trial satisfies the stated relative model-stationarity condition.
A finite threshold \(\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}\) guarantees \(\rho\ge\eta\), for example under the accepted quadratic model-accuracy theorem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every rejection episode is finite, and accepted trials satisfy \(\varphi(x_k)-\varphi(x_{k+1})\ge\eta\operatorname{pred}_k>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\alpha=1\). While \[\varphi(x_k+\alpha d_k)>\varphi(x_k)-\eta\alpha\Delta_k,\] replace \(\alpha\) by \(\tau\alpha\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of model-decrease Armijo backtracking when a positive nominal prediction is incompatible with the objective derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi(t)=t^2\), \(x=0\), \(d=1\), and let \(\Delta>0\). For every \(\alpha>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \[\varphi(x+\alpha d)=\alpha^2> -\eta\alpha\Delta=\varphi(x)-\eta\alpha\Delta.\] Hence no positive step is accepted despite the nominally positive predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive nominal prediction alone does not ensure termination: a non-descent direction can fail the Armijo test at every positive step length.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite geometric Armijo backtracking under directional agreement between the objective and predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi\) be directionally differentiable at \(x\) in direction \(d\), let \(\Delta>0\), and suppose \(\varphi'(x;d)\le-\Delta\). For every \(\eta,\tau\in(0,1)\), there exists \(j<\infty\) such that \(\alpha=\tau^j\) satisfies \[\varphi(x+\alpha d)\le\varphi(x)-\eta\alpha\Delta.\] Thus geometric model-decrease Armijo backtracking terminates finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the directional derivative is no greater than minus the predicted decrease, sufficiently small geometric trial steps satisfy the Armijo test.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Model-Decrease Backtracking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A safeguarded combination of adaptive regularization and line-search acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((x_k,\sigma_k)\), compute a regularized-model direction \(d_k\). First test the full trial \(x_k+d_k\) by its actual-to-predicted ratio. If accepted, set \(\alpha_k=1\), accept the trial, and optionally reduce \(\sigma_k\). Otherwise backtrack over \(\alpha\in\{1,\tau,\tau^2,\ldots\}\) until \[\varphi(x_k+\alpha d_k)\le\varphi(x_k)-\eta\alpha\Delta_k.\] If backtracking reaches a prescribed safeguard without acceptance, increase \(\sigma_k\), recompute \(d_k\), and repeat. Output the accepted iterate or stop when the common residual tolerance holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid regime first seeks full-step agreement, then backtracks, and finally strengthens regularization and recomputes the direction if line search is unsuccessful.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the seed trust-region algorithm generates objective values that are nonincreasing in a level set on which \(\varphi\) is bounded below. Let \(\chi_k\ge0\) be a criticality measure, and let the predicted reduction \(p_k>0\) satisfy \[p_k\ge c\chi_k\min\{\Delta_k,\chi_k\},\qquad |\operatorname{ared}_k-p_k|\le\kappa\Delta_k^2\] for fixed \(c,\kappa>0\). Suppose rejected trials shrink the radius by a factor uniformly bounded below one, while accepted trials do not shrink it. Then \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi_k=0\). If \(\chi\) is continuous and \(\chi(x)=0\) is the selected stationarity condition, every accumulation point of a subsequence satisfying \(\chi_k\to0\) is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ratio-based trust-region method has subsequential first-order convergence when trial steps achieve Cauchy-type decrease, model disagreement is quadratic in the radius, and the objective is bounded below.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Obstruction to telescoping stationarity complexity when the objective has no finite lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine objective \(\varphi(x)=-x\), iterates \(x_k=k\), and residuals \(G(x_k)=-1\) satisfy \(\varphi(x_k)-\varphi(x_{k+1})=\|G(x_k)\|^2=1\) at every iteration, but the residual never decreases. Uniform squared-residual descent therefore does not imply finite stationarity complexity without a finite lower bound on \(\varphi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine objective can decrease by the squared residual at every step while the residual remains constant, so lower boundedness is essential.

assumptions_latex: Successful iterations satisfy \(\varphi(x_k)-\varphi(x_{k+1})\ge c\|G_t(x_k)\|^2\) for a constant \(c>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Summing the sufficient-decrease inequality over the first \(N\) successful iterations gives \[c\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|G_t(x_k)\|^2\le\varphi(x_0)-\varphi(x_N)\le\varphi(x_0)-\varphi_{\inf}.\] Therefore \[\min_{0\le k<N}\|G_t(x_k)\|\le\sqrt{\frac{\varphi(x_0)-\varphi_{\inf}}{cN}}.\] In the exact first-order oracle model, the number of successful model solves required to produce an iterate with \(\|G_t(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\) is consequently \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\). Rejected trials or inner solver work require separate accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform descent proportional to the squared prox-linear residual yields an order epsilon-to-the-minus-two bound on successful iterations for residual stationarity.
