children.title: Ergodic-to-Best-Iterate Comparability
children.top_down_role: Translation limits between averaged and best-observed certificates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform angular condition under which a small vector-average residual forces a small observed residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space. Suppose there exist a unit vector \(u\) and \(c>0\) such that \(\langle u,r_k\rangle\geq c\|r_k\|\) for all \(k\leq N\). Then \[\|\bar r_N\|\geq\langle u,\bar r_N\rangle\geq c\frac{\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k\|r_k\|}{\Lambda_N}\geq c\min_{k\leq N}\|r_k\|,\] so \(\min_{k\leq N}\|r_k\|\leq c^{-1}\|\bar r_N\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform alignment excludes cancellation and transfers an ergodic residual bound to a best-iterate bound.
assumptions_latex: There are \(\|u\|=1\) and \(c>0\) with \(\langle u,r_k\rangle\geq c\|r_k\|\) for all \(k\leq N\).
knowledge_statements.title: Noncancellation Condition for Ergodic-to-Best Conversion
Ergodic-to-Best-Iterate Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of vector-averaged and best-iterate residual measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar r_N=\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k r_k\), convexity gives \(\|\bar r_N\|\leq\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k\|r_k\|\). There is no universal ordering between \(\|\bar r_N\|\) and \(\min_{0\leq k\leq N}\|r_k\|\). With equal weights, \(r_0=v\) and \(r_1=-v\) give \(\|\bar r_1\|=0<\min_k\|r_k\|\) for \(v\ne0\), whereas \(r_0=0\) and \(r_1=v\) give \(\min_k\|r_k\|=0<\|\bar r_1\|\). Thus rate comparability requires additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging residual vectors permits cancellation, and either the ergodic residual or the smallest individual residual can be smaller; the measures are not universally rate-comparable.
assumptions_latex: \(r_0,\ldots,r_N\) are vectors in a normed space, \(\lambda_k>0\), and \(\Lambda_N=\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One always has \(\|\bar r_N\|\leq\Lambda_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k\|r_k\|\), but neither \(\|\bar r_N\|\) nor \(\min_{0\leq k\leq N}\|r_k\|\) universally bounds the other. Additional sign, monotonicity, or residual-geometry assumptions are required for rate comparability.

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Residual Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Last-iterate rate under residual-norm monotonicity and a weighted energy estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\|r_k\|\) is nonincreasing, then \(\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k\|r_k\|^2\geq\Lambda_N\|r_N\|^2\). Combining this inequality with \(\sum_{k=0}^N\lambda_k\|r_k\|^2\leq E\) gives \(\|r_N\|\leq\sqrt{E/\Lambda_N}\). Under \(\lambda_k\geq\underline\lambda>0\), the bound becomes \(\|r_N\|\leq\sqrt{E/((N+1)\underline\lambda)}\), so the last iterate reaches residual tolerance \(\varepsilon\) within \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-norm monotonicity upgrades a prefix energy bound to the same O(1/sqrt(N)) rate for the last residual.
assumptions_latex: Residuals \(r_k\) lie in a Hilbert space and satisfy \(\|r_{k+1}\|\leq\|r_k\|\) for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy summability without monotonicity does not control every last residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define a scalar residual sequence by \(r_{2^m}=1/m\) for \(m\geq1\) and \(r_k=0\) at all other indices. Then \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|r_k|^2=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}1/m^2<\infty\), so the usual finite-energy premise holds. Nevertheless, along \(N=2^m\), one has \(\sqrt{N}|r_N|=2^{m/2}/m\to\infty\). Therefore finite energy cannot imply a uniform \(O(N^{-1/2})\) last-iterate rate without monotonicity or comparable structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Distance Contraction Gives R-Linear Residual and Orbit Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of local distance contraction for a nonexpansive fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive with \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\), and let \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\). Suppose the orbit remains in a region where \(\operatorname{dist}(x_{k+1},F)\le q\operatorname{dist}(x_k,F)\) for some \(q\in[0,1)\). Then \[\|x_k-Tx_k\|\le2q^k\operatorname{dist}(x_0,F).\] Moreover, \((x_k)\) converges to some \(x_\star\in F\), and \[\|x_k-x_\star\|\le\frac{2}{1-q}q^k\operatorname{dist}(x_0,F).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonexpansive map, geometric contraction of distance to the fixed-point set yields geometric residual decay and R-linear convergence of the orbit to a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: The orbit satisfies a uniform local distance contraction with factor \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Distance Contraction Gives R-Linear Residual and Orbit Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space, \(T:H\to H\), and \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
For some \(c>0\), \(\|Tx-z\|^2\leq\|x-z\|^2-c\|x-Tx\|^2\) holds for every \(x\in H\) and \(z\in F\).
On a neighborhood \(U\) of \(F\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa\|x-Tx\|\) for some \(\kappa>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in U\), \(\operatorname{dist}(Tx,F)\leq q\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\), where \(q=\sqrt{\max\{0,1-c/\kappa^2\}}<1\) whenever \(c<\kappa^2\), while the case \(c\geq\kappa^2\) forces one-step arrival at \(F\). Thus any orbit remaining in \(U\) converges Q-linearly in distance to \(F\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\), \(\inf_x|x-T(x)|=0\), and the Picard iterates satisfy \(x_k\to+\infty\) and \(|x_k-T(x_k)|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A firmly nonexpansive fixed-point model with approximate fixed points but no actual fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(T:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) by
\[
T(x)=x+\frac{1}{1+e^x}.
\]
Then \(T(x)>x\) for every \(x\), so \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\). Moreover,
\[
T'(x)=1-\frac{e^x}{(1+e^x)^2}\in[3/4,1),
\]
so \(T\) is firmly nonexpansive on \(\mathbb R\). Its displacement residual is
\[
R(x)=x-T(x)=-\frac{1}{1+e^x},
\]
which never vanishes but tends to zero as \(x\to+\infty\). The Picard sequence \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) satisfies \(x_k\to+\infty\) and \(|R(x_k)|\to0\). Thus inconsistency need not imply a positive residual floor, even for a firmly nonexpansive map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A firmly nonexpansive map can have no fixed point while an escaping Picard sequence has residuals converging to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistency with Vanishing Infimal Residual

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A one-sided residual threshold is not invariant under reciprocal primal-dual rescaling.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reciprocal scaling algebra directly exhibits primal-dual residual imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reciprocal rescaling shows why only one residual component cannot certify a primal-dual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\tau>0\), form the rescaled pair \((\widehat r_p,\widehat r_d)=(\tau r_p,\tau^{-1}r_d)\). Then \(\lVert\widehat r_p\rVert=\tau\lVert r_p\rVert\) and \(\lVert\widehat r_d\rVert=\tau^{-1}\lVert r_d\rVert\), while \(\lVert\widehat r_p\rVert\lVert\widehat r_d\rVert=\lVert r_p\rVert\lVert r_d\rVert\). Consequently, either component can be made arbitrarily small while the other becomes arbitrarily large. A calibrated primal-dual certificate must therefore control both components in a fixed normalization, for example \(\max\{\lVert r_p\rVert/\sigma_p,\lVert r_d\rVert/\sigma_d\}\le\varepsilon\) with prescribed \(\sigma_p,\sigma_d>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal scaling can make either primal or dual residual arbitrarily small while enlarging the other, so both require fixed joint calibration.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Residual Imbalance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reciprocal-scaling calculation is internally correct and fits the failure-boundary container, but no citation is supplied for interpreting the abstract pair as primal and dual residuals or for the asserted joint calibration requirement.

assumptions_latex: \(H=\mathbb R^n\) has its Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metric weighting may change a residual magnitude by any factor between \(\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(M)}\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(M)}\).

notation.meaning: Norm induced by the positive-definite metric M.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the claim is the Rayleigh-quotient bound for a positive-definite metric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional spectral bounds quantify residual distortion caused solely by changing the metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Euclidean and metric-weighted residual magnitudes obey \[\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(M)}\,\lVert r\rVert_2\le \lVert r\rVert_M\le \sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(M)}\,\lVert r\rVert_2.\] Both constants are sharp, attained by eigenvectors associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(M)\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(M)\), respectively. Hence two Euclidean-equal residuals can differ in metric norm by a factor as large as \(\sqrt{\kappa(M)}\). Without uniform spectral bounds on a varying metric, metric-small residuals need not be uniformly comparable to Euclidean-small residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite weighting distorts residual sizes according to the metric's extreme eigenvalues; without uniform spectral bounds, residual tolerances are not comparable.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Dependent Residual Distortion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional Rayleigh-quotient bounds and sharpness claim are mathematically correct and the property fits the container, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Scaled Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates normalized by problem or iterate-dependent scales.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Scaling and Uniform Sequential Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterate-dependent positive scalar normalization and the exact two-sided boundedness needed for equivalence of vanishing residual sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s:X\to(0,+\infty)\) and \(r_s(x)=s(x)r(x)\). Then \(r_s^{-1}(0)=r^{-1}(0)\). If \(0<m\le s(x_k)\le M<+\infty\), then \(\lVert r_s(x_k)\rVert\to0\) if and only if \(\lVert r(x_k)\rVert\to0\). The lower bound is necessary for the implication from scaled to raw residuals: \(r(x_k)=u\ne0\) and \(s(x_k)\downarrow0\) give \(r_s(x_k)\to0\). The upper bound is necessary for the reverse implication: if \(r(x_k)=u/k\) and \(s(x_k)=k\), then \(r(x_k)\to0\) but \(r_s(x_k)=u\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive pointwise scaling preserves exact zeros, while equivalence of vanishing scaled and raw residuals requires scales bounded above and away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \(r:X\to H\) maps into a normed space.

notation.meaning: A fixed nonzero residual vector used in the boundary examples.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Scaling and Uniform Sequential Equivalence

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty set and \(H\) is a normed space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling preserves the zero set and converts tolerances by \(\lVert r_s(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon\iff\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon/s\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive scalar normalization is an elementary residual definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar normalization of a residual map with its induced tolerance conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual scaled by \(s\) is the map \(r_s:X\to H\) defined by \(r_s(x)=s\,r(x)\). Because \(s>0\), its zero set is unchanged: \(r_s^{-1}(0)=r^{-1}(0)\). For every \(x\in X\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the scaled stopping test satisfies \(\lVert r_s(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon\) if and only if \(\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon/s\). Thus a numerical tolerance attached to a scaled residual is meaningful only together with its declared scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled residual multiplies the original residual by a positive constant, preserving zeros while dividing the equivalent unscaled tolerance by that constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, zero-set preservation, and tolerance conversion are precise and correct, but no source with a specific locator is supplied for this normalization class.

children.title: Unscaled Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates retained in their native magnitude.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty set and \(H\) is a normed space.
\(r:X\to H\) is the residual specified by the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An unscaled certificate reports \(\lVert r(x)\rVert\) without an additional normalization factor or metric transformation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the unscaled class is defined relative to the model-native residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The model-native residual is retained without scalar or metric normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unscaled residual associated with \(r\) is \(r_{m raw}(x)=r(x)\), and its magnitude is \(\rho_{m raw}(x)=\lVert r(x)\rVert\). An unscaled \(\varepsilon\)-certificate at \(x\in X\) is the inequality \(\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is expressed in the native units of \(r\). This definition fixes the identity normalization and does not imply invariance under a change of variables, physical units, or ambient norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unscaled residual is the model's native residual measured directly in its ambient norm, with no additional scalar or metric normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Unscaled Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identity-normalization definition is internally consistent and appropriately classified as a definition, but it lacks an inspectable source citation.

children.title: Metric-Weighted Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates measured through a chosen metric weight.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Weights Can Destroy Zero-Set Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp injectivity boundary for preservation of the original residual equation under metric weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(M\succeq0\) is singular, \(M^{1/2}r(x)\) can vanish while \(r(x)\ne0\). For any \(0\ne u\in\ker M\), the constant residual \(r(x)=u\) satisfies \(M^{1/2}r(x)=0\) everywhere although \(r(x)\) never vanishes. Thus unconditional zero-set preservation requires positive definiteness; for a fixed residual range, the exact weaker requirement is \(\ker M\cap\operatorname{range}(r)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular weight may annihilate a nonzero residual; zero-set preservation requires injectivity on the residual range.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite and singular.

notation.meaning: Nonzero residual direction annihilated by the weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Weights Can Destroy Zero-Set Equivalence

assumptions_latex: \(H=\mathbb R^n\) has its Euclidean inner product.
\(r:X\to H\) and \(M\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The metric-weighted residual vanishes exactly where \(r\) vanishes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive-definite square-root weighting is the canonical metric residual normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite metric normalization of residual vectors and their magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The \(M\)-weighted residual is \(r_M:X\to H\) defined by \(r_M(x)=M^{1/2}r(x)\). Its Euclidean magnitude equals the metric norm of the raw residual: \[\lVert r_M(x)\rVert_2=\sqrt{\langle Mr(x),r(x)\rangle}=\lVert r(x)\rVert_M.\] Since \(M\) is positive definite, \(M^{1/2}\) is invertible and \(r_M(x)=0\) if and only if \(r(x)=0\). A weighted tolerance must specify \(M\), because changing \(M\) changes every nonzero residual magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric-weighted residual applies the positive-definite square root of a metric, preserving zeros but changing nonzero magnitudes according to that metric.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Weighted Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-definite square-root weighting, norm identity, and zero-set equivalence are correct in finite dimensions, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Cross-Normalization Comparability
children.top_down_role: Comparability boundaries across scaled, native, and metric-weighted residuals.

assumptions_latex: \(H=\mathbb R^n\), and \(M,N\) are symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two normalized residuals are uniformly comparable precisely through the extreme generalized eigenvalues of \((M,N)\) and the scale ratio \(s/t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generalized Rayleigh quotients give exact cross-normalization constants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional comparison constants for two scalar-and-metric residual normalizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=N^{-1/2}MN^{-1/2}\). For every nonzero residual \(r\), \[\frac{s}{t}\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(A)}\le \frac{s\lVert r\rVert_M}{t\lVert r\rVert_N}\le\frac{s}{t}\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(A)}.\] The constants are sharp. Consequently, a certificate \(s\lVert r\rVert_M\le\varepsilon\) implies \(t\lVert r\rVert_N\le (t/s)\lambda_{\min}(A)^{-1/2}\varepsilon\). Uniform comparability over a family of normalizations requires uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds on the relevant generalized eigenvalues and on the scalar ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two scaled metric residuals are comparable using sharp generalized-eigenvalue bounds; uniform certificate conversion requires those bounds and scale ratios to remain controlled.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Normalization Comparability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generalized-eigenvalue comparison and certificate conversion are mathematically consistent and correctly presented as a property, but the sharp bounds and uniform-comparability assertion have no cited source.

children.title: Base-Point Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates evaluated at the designated reference point.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The witness certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\le\varepsilon\) at the base point itself.

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of F at x.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a small subgradient is the standard pointwise stationarity certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-subdifferential stationarity certified at the reported base point.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A base-point \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity certificate for \(F\) at \(x\) is a vector \(v\in\partial F(x)\) satisfying \(\lVert v\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\). Equivalently, the certificate establishes \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\le\varepsilon\). Both membership and the norm bound concern the same reported point \(x\); a small subgradient known only at another point is not, without a transfer result, a base-point certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base-point certificate is a subgradient at the reported point whose norm is at most the prescribed stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Base-Point Certificates

children.title: Nearby-Point Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates evaluated at a related proximal or corrected point.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary point within distance \(\delta\) of the base point \(x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nearby-point stationarity pairs displacement and subgradient bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity is witnessed at a controlled nearby point rather than necessarily at the base point.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \((\delta,\varepsilon)\)-nearby-point stationarity certificate relative to the base point \(x\) is a pair \((y,v)\) such that \(y\in\operatorname{dom}F\), \(\lVert y-x\rVert_2\le\delta\), \(v\in\partial F(y)\), and \(\lVert v\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\). It certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(y))\le\varepsilon\) at a point lying in the closed \(\delta\)-ball about \(x\), but does not by itself bound \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearby-point certificate gives a close evaluation point and a small subgradient there, without automatically asserting stationarity at the base point.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Point Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.4 Subdifferential Calculus in Banach Spaces p. 112
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

children.title: Base-to-Nearby Certificate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer quality and location mismatch between the two certificate forms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Close Stationarity Does Not Transfer to the Base Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nearby-to-base stationarity transfer without regularity controlling subdifferential variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(t)=|t|\). For any \(a>0\), take \(x=a\) and \(y=0\). Then \(0\in\partial F(y)\) and \(|x-y|=a\), so \((y,0)\) is an \((a,0)\)-nearby-point certificate relative to \(x\). Nevertheless, \(\partial F(x)=\{1\}\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))=1\). Thus the nearby point may approach the base point while its exact stationarity still yields no vanishing base-point stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For absolute value, exactly stationary nearby points can approach positive base points whose stationarity residual remains one.

notation.meaning: Base point lacking a small stationarity residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Close Stationarity Does Not Transfer to the Base Point

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal residual at \(x\) produces a nearby-point certificate \((y,v)\) with equal displacement and stationarity controls.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal optimality transfers a base displacement residual to a nearby subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakly convex proximal transfer from a base-point residual to stationarity at its proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(v=(x-y)/\lambda\). Then \(v\in\partial F(y)\), \(\lVert v\rVert_2=\lVert x-y\rVert_2/\lambda\), and \(\lVert x-y\rVert_2=\lambda\lVert v\rVert_2\). Therefore, if the base-point proximal residual satisfies \(\lVert x-y\rVert_2/\lambda\le\varepsilon\), the pair \((y,v)\) is a \((\lambda\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\)-nearby-point stationarity certificate relative to \(x\). This conclusion locates the certified subgradient at \(y\), not generally at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small proximal residual at the base point yields a nearby point within lambda times the tolerance and a subgradient there of tolerance size.
knowledge_statements.title: Base-to-Nearby Certificate Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is correctly scoped to a proper lower-semicontinuous weakly convex function with the required proximal parameter, and its nearby-point conclusion is not overstated. However, the proximal optimality-to-limiting-subgradient transfer requires an authoritative theorem or section locator.

children.title: Pointwise Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates attached to individual iterates or evaluation points.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty set, \(H\) is a normed space, and \(R:X\to H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate concerns the single iterate \(x_k\) and uses neither averaging nor random selection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise aggregation evaluates one explicitly identified iterate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A certificate attached to one identified iterate, without ergodic or sampled aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pointwise \(\varepsilon\)-residual certificate for the sequence \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\) is an index \(k\ge0\) together with the evaluated residual \(R(x_k)\) such that \(\lVert R(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\). When \(R(x)=0\) characterizes the target solution condition, the certificate directly bounds violation at the reported iterate \(x_k\). It makes no claim about the residual of an average of iterates, an expectation, or an iterate selected without reporting its realized residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise certificate reports one specific iterate whose directly evaluated residual meets the tolerance, with no averaging or sampling interpretation.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise certificate is clearly distinguished from ergodic and sampled certificates and is correctly assigned the certificate content kind, but no inspectable source citation is supplied.

children.title: Ergodic Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates attached to averaged iterates or residual quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted aggregation of composite residual magnitudes over a finite iteration window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_k\in H\) be residual vectors in a Hilbert space \(H\), and let \(w_k\ge 0\) with \(W_N:=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k>0\). The weighted ergodic residual certificate is
\[C_N^{\mathrm{erg}}:=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\lVert r_k\rVert^2.\]
The finite trajectory is ergodically \(\varepsilon\)-stationary when \(C_N^{\mathrm{erg}}\le \varepsilon^2\). This inequality certifies that at least one index \(k<N\) with \(w_k>0\) satisfies \(\lVert r_k\rVert\le\varepsilon\); it does not by itself identify that index or certify the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted mean squared residual below ε² certifies that some positively weighted iterate has residual at most ε, without certifying the last iterate.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and minimum-residual implication are mathematically precise and fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Sampled Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates attached to randomly or selectively sampled iterates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: High-Probability Conversion of a Sampled Mean-Square Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail guarantee obtained from a nonnegative sampled squared-residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb E\|r_K\|^2\le\varepsilon^2\), then for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\|r_K\|>\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt\delta}\right)\le\delta.\] Equivalently, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), the sampled residual norm is at most \(\varepsilon/\sqrt\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expected squared-residual certificate yields a high-probability sampled-residual bound by Markov's inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a sampled index and \(\mathbb E\|r_K\|^2\le\varepsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Conversion of a Sampled Mean-Square Certificate
Sampled Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certification at an index randomly sampled from a prescribed iteration window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_0,\ldots,r_{N-1}\in H\), and choose weights \(w_k\ge0\) with \(W_N:=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k>0\). Draw an index \(K\) independently of any subsequent certificate evaluation according to \(\mathbb P(K=k)=w_k/W_N\). The sampled certificate reports \(C_N^{\mathrm{samp}}:=\lVert r_K\rVert^2\). It is an \(\varepsilon\)-certificate in expectation when
\[\mathbb E[C_N^{\mathrm{samp}}]=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\lVert r_k\rVert^2\le\varepsilon^2.\]
A single realization certifies only the sampled iterate; the expectation bound is over the sampling rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling an iterate proportionally to its weight makes its expected squared residual equal the corresponding weighted ergodic certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: expectation of a finite discrete random variable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sampling identity is correct for the stated finite residual sequence and fits a sampled-certificate container, but it lacks a citation.

children.title: Certificate Aggregation Comparability
children.top_down_role: Comparability boundaries among pointwise, averaged, and sampled reporting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cancellation Separates Averaged-Vector and Mean-Squared Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp non-equivalence between averaging residual vectors and averaging their squared norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\ne0\) in a Hilbert space, take \(r_0=u\), \(r_1=-u\), and \(w_0=w_1=1\). Then \[\left\|\frac{r_0+r_1}{2}\right\|^2=0,\qquad \frac{\|r_0\|^2+\|r_1\|^2}{2}=\|u\|^2>0.\] Thus a zero averaged residual vector need not imply that any pointwise residual or the mean squared residual is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite residuals cancel when averaged as vectors even though both pointwise residuals and their mean squared norm remain nonzero.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation Separates Averaged-Vector and Mean-Squared Certificates
Certificate Aggregation Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic comparison among pointwise, weighted-ergodic, and randomly sampled residual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For residuals \(r_k\in H\), nonnegative weights \(w_k\), and \(W_N:=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k>0\), let \(K\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(K=k)=w_k/W_N\). Then
\[\min_{k:w_k>0}\lVert r_k\rVert^2\le \mathbb E\lVert r_K\rVert^2=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\lVert r_k\rVert^2\le\max_{k:w_k>0}\lVert r_k\rVert^2.\]
Moreover, the norm of the averaged residual obeys
\[\left\lVert\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_kr_k\right\rVert^2\le\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\lVert r_k\rVert^2.\]
Thus these aggregation modes are comparable, but generally not interchangeable by equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sampled expectation equals the weighted mean squared residual, lies between pointwise extremes, and dominates the squared norm of the averaged residual.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convexity of the squared norm and elementary weighted-average bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-average bounds and convexity inequality are correct and appropriately classified as a comparability property, but no source is cited.

children.title: Absolute Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Stopping thresholds expressed on an absolute residual scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-independent admissibility condition for an observed composite residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x)\in H\) be the exact residual and \(\widetilde r(x)\in H\) its computed value. An absolute residual tolerance \(\delta\ge0\) is satisfied when
\[\lVert\widetilde r(x)-r(x)\rVert\le\delta.\]
Consequently, an observed stopping test \(\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obs}}\) certifies the exact bound
\[\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obs}}+\delta.\]
The tolerance is independent of the magnitude of \(r(x)\), so a fixed positive \(\delta\) imposes an absolute accuracy floor on residual certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If residual evaluation has absolute error δ, an observed tolerance ε certifies an exact residual no larger than ε+δ.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.2 Absolute Deterministic Noise p. 98

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.2 Absolute Deterministic Noise p. 98

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute Error Budget for a Target Exact Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp worst-case allocation of observed and evaluation-error budgets for a prescribed exact-residual target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(\lVert\widetilde r(x)-r(x)\rVert\le\delta\), a sufficient worst-case stopping rule for the target \(\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\rm tar}\) is \(\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\rm tar}-\delta\), which requires \(0\le\delta\le\varepsilon_{\rm tar}\). Equivalently, an observed budget \(\varepsilon_{\rm obs}\) is valid whenever \(\varepsilon_{\rm obs}+\delta\le\varepsilon_{\rm tar}\). This allocation is sharp under only the absolute-error assumption, since the residual and evaluation error may be collinear and oppositely directed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To guarantee an exact target under absolute evaluation error, the observed threshold plus the error budget must not exceed the target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\rm obs}\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon_{\rm obs}+\delta\le\varepsilon_{\rm tar}\implies\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\rm tar}\).

notation.meaning: Stopping threshold applied to the computed residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Error Budget for a Target Exact Tolerance

children.title: Relative Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Stopping thresholds normalized by a reference magnitude.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-dependent residual accuracy measured relative to the exact residual magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x),\widetilde r(x)\in H\), and fix \(0\le\eta<1\). A relative residual tolerance is satisfied when
\[\lVert\widetilde r(x)-r(x)\rVert\le\eta\lVert r(x)\rVert.\]
The exact and computed residual magnitudes then satisfy
\[(1-\eta)\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert\le(1+\eta)\lVert r(x)\rVert.\]
Hence an observed test \(\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obs}}\) certifies \(\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obs}}/(1-\eta)\). The restriction \(\eta<1\) is necessary for this upper calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative residual error η below one yields two-sided magnitude bounds and converts an observed tolerance ε into the exact tolerance ε/(1−η).

children.title: Blockwise Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Stopping thresholds assigned across residual components or blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Extraction of Block Bounds from a Product-Norm Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse conversion from one weighted product tolerance to individual block tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e=(e_i)_{i=1}^m\) and \(\|e\|_a^2=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\|e_i\|_{H_i}^2\), where \(a_i>0\). If \(\|e\|_a\le\Delta\), then \[\|e_i\|_{H_i}\le\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{a_i}}\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Each constant is sharp because equality is attained by an error supported only on block \(i\). Consequently, a single product tolerance guarantees prescribed block bounds \(\delta_i\) whenever \(\Delta\le\min_i\sqrt{a_i}\,\delta_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted product tolerance yields sharp individual block bounds, with the least permissive weighted block determining a threshold that guarantees every target.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Extraction of Block Bounds from a Product-Norm Tolerance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Observed Block Residual to Exact Global Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise observed thresholds combined with blockwise residual-evaluation error budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=(r_i)\), \(\widetilde r=(\widetilde r_i)\), and \(\|z\|_a^2=\sum_i a_i\|z_i\|^2\), where \(a_i>0\). If \[\|\widetilde r_i-r_i\|\le\delta_i,\qquad \|\widetilde r_i\|\le\varepsilon_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] then \[\|r_i\|\le\varepsilon_i+\delta_i,\qquad \|r\|_a\le\left(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i(\varepsilon_i+\delta_i)^2\right)^{1/2}.\] Therefore an exact global target \(\|r\|_a\le\tau\) is certified whenever \(\sum_i a_i(\varepsilon_i+\delta_i)^2\le\tau^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observed block thresholds and block evaluation-error budgets yield a computable exact product-residual certificate.
assumptions_latex: The residual space is a finite orthogonal product.

notation.meaning: observed residual threshold for block i
residual-evaluation error budget for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Observed Block Residual to Exact Global Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Weight Blocks Are Invisible to a Product Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of positive weights when a global product tolerance must control every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|e\|_a^2=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\|e_i\|_{H_i}^2\) with \(a_i\ge0\). If \(a_j=0\) for some nontrivial block \(H_j\), then for every \(M>0\) there is an error supported on block \(j\) with \(\|e_j\|_{H_j}=M\) but \(\|e\|_a=0\). Hence no finite bound on \(\|e\|_a\) can imply a bound on block \(j\) unless \(a_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero product-norm weight hides every error in that block, so positive weights are necessary for blockwise certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Weight Blocks Are Invisible to a Product Tolerance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Block Tolerances and Product Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward conversion of finite blockwise residual-error budgets into a weighted product tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\) be an orthogonal product, let \(e_i=\widetilde r_i-r_i\), and let \(a_i>0\). If \(\|e_i\|_{H_i}\le\delta_i\) for every \(i\), then, for \(\|e\|_a^2=\sum_i a_i\|e_i\|_{H_i}^2\), \[\|\widetilde r-r\|_a\le\left(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\delta_i^2\right)^{1/2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individual block error budgets combine quadratically into a weighted product-space tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Block Tolerances and Product Aggregation
Blockwise Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise residual calibration for a finite orthogonal block decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\) be an orthogonal product Hilbert space, with exact and computed residuals \(r=(r_i)_{i=1}^m\) and \(\widetilde r=(\widetilde r_i)_{i=1}^m\). Given tolerances \(\delta_i\ge0\), the blockwise absolute condition is
\[\lVert\widetilde r_i-r_i\rVert_{H_i}\le\delta_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
For positive calibration weights \(a_i\), define \(\lVert z\rVert_a^2:=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\lVert z_i\rVert_{H_i}^2\). Then
\[\lVert\widetilde r-r\rVert_a\le\left(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\delta_i^2\right)^{1/2}.\]
Thus block tolerances induce a single product-space tolerance without requiring identical block scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individual block error limits combine quadratically into a weighted product-space residual tolerance.

notation.meaning: exact and computed residuals in block i

children.title: Cross-Tolerance Calibration
children.top_down_role: Consistency and imbalance boundaries across tolerance conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Tolerance Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of mixed absolute-relative evaluation error into an exact residual threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x),\widetilde r(x)\in H\) satisfy the mixed error model
\[\lVert\widetilde r(x)-r(x)\rVert\le\delta+\eta\lVert r(x)\rVert,\qquad \delta\ge0,\quad 0\le\eta<1.\]
Then
\[\lVert r(x)\rVert\le\frac{\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert+\delta}{1-\eta}.\]
Therefore a desired exact tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is guaranteed by the computed stopping threshold
\[\lVert\widetilde r(x)\rVert\le(1-\eta)\varepsilon-\delta,\]
provided its right-hand side is nonnegative. Feasibility requires \(\delta\le(1-\eta)\varepsilon\), explicitly exposing the tradeoff between absolute and relative error budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed absolute-relative error converts an observed residual into an exact bound; the absolute budget must not exceed (1−η) times the target.

children.title: Proximal Evaluation Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Residual interfaces for approximate proximal evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II approximate proximal evaluation through an epsilon-subgradient inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(v\in H\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(z\in\operatorname{dom}g\). If \[(v-z)/\gamma\in\partial_\epsilon g(z),\] then, for \(Q_v(y)=g(y)+(2\gamma)^{-1}\|y-v\|^2\), \[Q_v(z)-\min_yQ_v(y)\le\epsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A type-II epsilon-subgradient proximal inclusion implies the same epsilon budget for the proximal objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Subgradient Inclusion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error representation of an approximate proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z\in\operatorname{dom}g\) and \(a\in\partial g(z)\), set \(e=z-v+\gamma a\). Then \[z=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(v+e).\] Consequently, \(\|z-v+\gamma a\|\le\delta\) certifies that \(z\) is the exact proximal point for an input within \(\delta\) of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal optimality residual is exactly an input backward error.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex
knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed-Input Proximal Evaluation
Proximal Evaluation Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap criterion for an approximate proximal oracle in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and take \(v\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\). Define
\[Q_v(y):=g(y)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert y-v\rVert^2,\qquad p:=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(v)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in H}Q_v(y).\]
A computed point \(\widetilde p\in\operatorname{dom}g\) is an \(\epsilon\)-inexact proximal evaluation when
\[Q_v(\widetilde p)\le Q_v(p)+\epsilon,\qquad \epsilon\ge0.\]
This criterion measures inexactness in proximal-subproblem objective value and reduces to exact proximal evaluation when \(\epsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate proximal point is ε-inexact when its regularized subproblem value is within ε of the exact proximal minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(g:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex

children.title: Model-Subproblem Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Residual interfaces for approximate solutions of local model subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Subproblem Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity-residual criterion for approximate minimization of a convex local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_x:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper, lower semicontinuous, convex model subproblem at a base point \(x\). A computed point \(y\in\operatorname{dom}m_x\) satisfies model-subproblem stationarity tolerance \(\tau\ge0\) when there exists \(s\in\partial m_x(y)\) such that
\[\lVert s\rVert\le\tau,\]
or equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial m_x(y))\le\tau\). If \(\tau=0\), then \(0\in\partial m_x(y)\), and convexity implies that \(y\) is a global minimizer of \(m_x\). For \(\tau>0\), the vector \(s\) is a directly checkable model-stationarity residual when supplied by the subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model subproblem is solved to tolerance τ when its computed point admits a subgradient of norm at most τ.
assumptions_latex: \(m_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex

notation.meaning: convex local model at base point x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap criterion and epsilon-subdifferential formulation for a convex local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_x:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(m_x^*:=\inf_Hm_x>-�\infty\). For \(y\in\operatorname{dom}m_x\) and \(\epsilon\ge0\), \[m_x(y)-m_x^*\le\epsilon\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial_\epsilon m_x(y),\] where \(u\in\partial_\epsilon m_x(y)\) means \(m_x(z)\ge m_x(y)+\langle u,z-y\rangle-\epsilon\) for every \(z\in H\). Attainment of \(m_x^*\) is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex model has objective error at most epsilon exactly when zero is an epsilon-subgradient at the computed point.
assumptions_latex: \(m_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex
knowledge_statements.title: Model Objective-Gap Inexactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Gap Does Not Control Model Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of objective accuracy to imply a small ordinary subgradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m(t)=|t|\) and \(y_\epsilon=\epsilon>0\), \[m(y_\epsilon)-\min m=\epsilon\to0,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial m(y_\epsilon))=1.\] Thus vanishing convex-model objective error need not imply a vanishing model-stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute-value model has arbitrarily small objective error while its ordinary subgradient residual remains one.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Gap Does Not Control Model Stationarity

children.title: Proximal-to-Model Error Calibration
children.top_down_role: Translation and mismatch between proximal and model-subproblem error measures.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Reverse Gap-to-Stationarity Calibration without Additional Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of proximal objective error to control an ordinary subgradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(g(t)=|t|\), \(v=0\), and \(\gamma>0\). For \(z_n\downarrow0\), \[Q_0(z_n)-Q_0(0)=z_n+\frac{z_n^2}{2\gamma}\to0,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial Q_0(z_n))=1+\frac{z_n}{\gamma}\to1.\] Thus objective-gap control does not imply ordinary stationarity-residual control without additional smoothness or an appropriate error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing proximal objective gap can coexist with a nonvanishing ordinary subgradient residual.
knowledge_statements.title: No Reverse Gap-to-Stationarity Calibration without Additional Regularity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a proximal-objective subgradient residual into point and objective errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_v(y)=g(y)+(2\gamma)^{-1}\|y-v\|^2\), where \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex and \(\gamma>0\), and let \(p=\arg\min Q_v\). For every \(s\in\partial Q_v(z)\), \[\|z-p\|\le\gamma\|s\|,\qquad Q_v(z)-Q_v(p)\le\frac{\gamma}{2}\|s\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-objective subgradient of norm tau gives point error at most gamma tau and objective error at most gamma tau squared over two.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-to-Proximal Error Calibration
Proximal-to-Model Error Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of proximal objective error into point and residual errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the proximal setup, \(Q_v(y)=g(y)+(2\gamma)^{-1}\lVert y-v\rVert^2\) is \(1/\gamma\)-strongly convex and has minimizer \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(v)\). If \(\widetilde p\) satisfies \(Q_v(\widetilde p)-Q_v(p)\le\epsilon\), then
\[\lVert\widetilde p-p\rVert\le\sqrt{2\gamma\epsilon}.\]
For the exact and computed proximal residuals \(R_\gamma(v):=\gamma^{-1}(v-p)\) and \(\widetilde R_\gamma(v):=\gamma^{-1}(v-\widetilde p)\), this yields
\[\lVert\widetilde R_\gamma(v)-R_\gamma(v)\rVert\le\sqrt{\frac{2\epsilon}{\gamma}}.\]
Thus a proximal objective-gap budget calibrates directly to a residual-evaluation error budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ε proximal objective gap gives point error at most √(2γε) and proximal-residual error at most √(2ε/γ).
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Splitting Error Can Shift the Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact fixed-point convergence under persistent additive error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(Tz=qz\) with \(0<q<1\), so \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\). For constant error \(e^k=c\ne0\), the inexact iteration \[z^{k+1}=qz^k+c\] converges to \(c/(1-q)\ne0\). Thus bounded persistent operator error need not preserve the fixed point of the exact splitting map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for a contraction, constant additive splitting error moves the limit away from the exact fixed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Splitting Error Can Shift the Limit

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Summably Perturbed Averaged Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic result for an additively perturbed averaged fixed-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\), and let \[z^{k+1}=Tz^k+e^k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e^k\|<\infty.\] Then \((z^k)\) is bounded, \(\|z^k-Tz^k\|\to0\), and \(z^k\rightharpoonup z^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). In finite-dimensional spaces the convergence is strong.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable additive errors preserve fixed-point convergence of an averaged splitting iteration and force its fixed-point residual to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is averaged and has a fixed point
knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of Summably Perturbed Averaged Splitting
Splitting-Operator Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive perturbation model and summability condition for an averaged splitting iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\) be an \(\alpha\)-averaged splitting operator with \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). An inexact splitting iteration has the form
\[z^{k+1}=Tz^k+e^k,\]
where \(e^k\in H\) is the aggregate error from inexact component-operator evaluations. The standard summable-error regime requires
\[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e^k\rVert<\infty.\]
Under this regime, the perturbations have finite total magnitude; this is the calibration condition used to preserve the asymptotic fixed-point behavior of the corresponding exact averaged iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact splitting step adds error to an averaged fixed-point update; summable error is the standard condition for preserving asymptotic behavior.

children.title: Deterministic Residual Noise
children.top_down_role: Residual perturbations represented by deterministic error controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Residual Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise residual-error model with prescribed nonrandom error budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_k\in H\) be the exact residual at iteration \(k\), and let \(\widetilde r_k=r_k+\xi_k\) be its observed value. The residual noise is deterministic with budget sequence \((\delta_k)_{k\ge0}\) when
\[\lVert\xi_k\rVert=\lVert\widetilde r_k-r_k\rVert\le\delta_k\quad\text{for every }k\ge0,\]
where each \(\delta_k\ge0\) is prescribed and no probability model is invoked. Uniformly bounded noise corresponds to \(\sup_k\delta_k<\infty\); vanishing noise corresponds to \(\delta_k\to0\); and summable noise corresponds to \(\sum_k\delta_k<\infty\). These regimes impose progressively stronger asymptotic control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic residual noise is a pathwise error bounded at every iteration by a prescribed nonrandom sequence, with bounded, vanishing, and summable subregimes.

source_refs.locator: 4.2.2 Absolute Deterministic Noise p. 98

review_flags: source_context_may_define deterministic oracle noise rather than residual noise

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.2 Absolute Deterministic Noise p. 98

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative pathwise noise regime and its two-sided residual comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde r_k=r_k+\xi_k\) in a normed space and suppose \(\|\xi_k\|\le\eta_k\|r_k\|\) with \(0\le\eta_k<1\). Then \[(1-\eta_k)\|r_k\|\le\|\widetilde r_k\|\le(1+\eta_k)\|r_k\|,\] and consequently \(\|r_k\|\le\|\widetilde r_k\|/(1-\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic relative error below one makes the exact and observed residual norms pathwise equivalent.

children.title: Stochastic Residual Noise
children.top_down_role: Residual perturbations represented through random error behavior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Averaging Complexity for Variance-Bounded Residual Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch-size calibration for an averaged unbiased scalar residual oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditionally on \(\mathcal F_k\), let \(Y_{k,1},\ldots,Y_{k,b}\) be independent with \(\mathbb E[Y_{k,i}\mid\mathcal F_k]=r_k\) and \(\mathbb E[(Y_{k,i}-r_k)^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_k^2\). For \(\widetilde r_k=b^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^bY_{k,i}\), \[\mathbb P(|\widetilde r_k-r_k|\ge t\mid\mathcal F_k)\le\frac{\sigma_k^2}{bt^2}.\] Hence confidence at least \(1-\alpha\) at accuracy \(t\) is ensured by \(b\ge\sigma_k^2/(\alpha t^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging independent unbiased samples reduces conditional variance by the batch size and gives a Chebyshev sample bound.
assumptions_latex: The samples are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_k\)
Each conditional variance is at most \(\sigma_k^2\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\ge\frac{\sigma_k^2}{\alpha t^2}\Longrightarrow\mathbb P(|\widetilde r_k-r_k|\le t\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge1-\alpha
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Complexity for Variance-Bounded Residual Noise

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-tail scalar stochastic residual-noise regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde r_k=r_k+\xi_k\), where \(r_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable. If \[\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\xi_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma_k^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,\] then \[\mathbb P(|\widetilde r_k-r_k|\ge t\mid\mathcal F_k)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma_k^2}\right)\] for every \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional sub-Gaussian noise yields an exponential residual-error tail stronger than variance-only Chebyshev control.

notation.meaning: information preceding the kth noise realization

knowledge_statements.title: Conditionally Sub-Gaussian Residual Noise
Stochastic Residual Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional second-moment model for noise entering a computed residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space with filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\). A computed residual \(\widetilde r_k\) has stochastic residual noise relative to the exact residual \(r_k\) if \(\widetilde r_k=r_k+\xi_k\), where \(r_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and \(\xi_k\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[|\xi_k|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq \sigma_k^2\) almost surely. Consequently, for every \(t>0\), \(\mathbb P(|\widetilde r_k-r_k|\geq t\mid\mathcal F_k)\leq \sigma_k^2/t^2\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic residual noise is conditionally unbiased and has bounded conditional variance, yielding a conditional probability bound for residual error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(|\widetilde r_k-r_k|\geq t\mid\mathcal F_k)\leq \sigma_k^2/t^2\) for every \(t>0\).

notation.meaning: exact nonnegative residual at iteration k

children.title: Noise-Regime Robustness Separation
children.top_down_role: Robustness distinctions between deterministic and stochastic perturbations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of one-step stochastic residual-certificate guarantees over multiple tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose events \(E_k\) encode correctness of stochastic residual certificates and \(\mathbb P(E_k^c\mid\mathcal F_k)\le\alpha_k\) almost surely. For every finite index set \(K\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{k\in K}E_k\right)\ge1-\sum_{k\in K}\alpha_k.\] If \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k<\infty\), then \(E_k^c\) occurs only finitely often almost surely. Thus per-test confidence is not a simultaneous pathwise guarantee; confidence must be allocated across tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon soundness costs the sum of failure probabilities, while summable failure budgets give eventual almost-sure correctness.

notation.meaning: event that the kth stochastic certificate is sound

knowledge_statements.title: Horizonwise and Almost-Sure Confidence Separation
Noise-Regime Robustness Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates pathwise deterministic guarantees from high-probability soundness of stochastic stopping rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|\widetilde r_k-r_k|\leq\|e_k\|\) almost surely. If \(\|e_k\|\leq\delta_k\) deterministically, then \(\widetilde r_k+\delta_k\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow r_k\leq\varepsilon\) pathwise. If instead \(\mathbb E[\|e_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma_k^2\), then for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), conditional Chebyshev gives \(\mathbb P(\|e_k\|\leq\sigma_k/\sqrt{\alpha}\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq1-\alpha\). Consequently, \(\mathbb P(\{\widetilde r_k+\sigma_k/\sqrt{\alpha}>\varepsilon\}\cup\{r_k\leq\varepsilon\}\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq1-\alpha\); equivalently, the stochastic stopping implication is sound with conditional probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic envelope makes the stopping implication valid on every path, whereas a conditional second-moment bound makes that implication valid only with a specified confidence level.
assumptions_latex: Under the stochastic regime, \(\mathbb E[\|e_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma_k^2\), with \(\sigma_k\) \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deterministic control yields a pathwise implication; conditional second-moment control makes the corresponding implication valid with conditional probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

children.title: Single-Residual Stopping
children.top_down_role: Stopping interfaces governed by one residual certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Residual Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping certificate based on one calibrated nonnegative residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(S\subseteq X\) be the stationary set of the target problem, and let \(R:X\to[0,\infty]\) satisfy \(R(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in S\). Given \(\varepsilon\geq0\), a single-residual stopping certificate at \(x_k\in X\) is the verified inequality \(R(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\). If an error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa R(x)\) holds at \(x_k\) for some \(\kappa\geq0\), then the certificate also guarantees \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\leq\kappa\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-residual certificate verifies that one calibrated residual is below tolerance; an applicable error bound additionally converts it into a distance-to-stationarity guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \(S\subseteq X\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\), and under the stated error bound, \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\leq\kappa\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Residual Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint stopping certificate requiring several normalized residual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_i:X\to[0,\infty]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) measure distinct necessary conditions, and let \(\varepsilon_i>0\). A composite-residual stopping certificate at \(x_k\) is \(R_i(x_k)\leq\varepsilon_i\) for every \(i\). Equivalently, with \(R_{\max}(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}R_i(x)/\varepsilon_i\), stopping occurs exactly when \(R_{\max}(x_k)\leq1\). If simultaneous vanishing of all components is equivalent to stationarity, then zero composite residual characterizes the stationary set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop only when every residual component meets its own tolerance, equivalently when the maximum normalized residual is at most one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\max}(x_k)\leq1\) if and only if \(R_i(x_k)\leq\varepsilon_i\) for all \(i\).

children.title: Residual Aggregation for Stopping
children.top_down_role: Aggregation choices and imbalance boundaries for composite stopping certificates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of signed scalar aggregation to certify componentwise stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For signed normalized residuals \(r_i\) and positive weights \(w_i\), \[\left|\sum_{i=1}^m w_i r_i\right|\leq1\] does not imply \(|r_i|\leq1\) for every \(i\). In particular, for \(m=2\), \(w_1=w_2=1\), and \(r=(M,-M)\) with \(M>1\), the aggregate is zero although both component bounds fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large signed residuals can cancel, so a signed sum alone cannot certify componentwise stopping.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i>0\), and signed residual components are permitted.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation Makes Signed Aggregation Unsound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent comparison of finite-dimensional normalized residual aggregates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(1\leq p<\infty\), \[\lVert r\rVert_\infty\leq\lVert r\rVert_p\leq m^{1/p}\lVert r\rVert_\infty.\] Both constants are sharp. Consequently, the threshold \(\lVert r\rVert_p\leq1\) is sufficient for componentwise stopping \(\lVert r\rVert_\infty\leq1\), whereas componentwise stopping guarantees only \(\lVert r\rVert_p\leq m^{1/p}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite p-norm aggregation is conservative relative to componentwise stopping, with a sharp dimension factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Comparison of Norm Aggregates
Residual Aggregation for Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar aggregation of finitely many normalized stopping residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative residuals \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\), positive tolerances \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_m\), and \(p\in[1,\infty]\), define \(A_p(x)=\|(R_i(x)/\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^m\|_p\). Then \(A_p(x)\leq1\) implies \(R_i(x)\leq\varepsilon_i\) for every \(i\). For \(p=\infty\), the converse also holds, so \(A_\infty(x)\leq1\) represents componentwise stopping exactly. For finite \(p\), the rule is generally stricter because it also restricts the combined normalized residual mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm aggregates normalized residuals into one statistic; the maximum norm exactly reproduces componentwise stopping, while finite norms are generally stricter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_p(x)\leq1\Rightarrow R_i(x)\leq\varepsilon_i\) for all \(i\), with equivalence when \(p=\infty\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual stopping based on primal feasibility, dual stationarity, and complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(h_i(x)\le0\), where \(f,h_i\) are proper closed convex functions. For \(z\ge0\), define \[r_{\rm p}=\bigl(\|Ax-b\|^2+\|[h(x)]_+\|^2\bigr)^{1/2},\quad r_{\rm d}=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)+A^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_i z_i\partial h_i(x)\right),\quad r_{\rm c}=\|z\odot h(x)\|.\] The test \(\max\{r_{\rm p},r_{\rm d},r_{\rm c}\}\le\varepsilon\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT stopping condition. At \(\varepsilon=0\), it is equivalent to the KKT system and certifies primal-dual optimality. Slater's condition is sufficient for every attained primal optimum to admit such multipliers. For \(\varepsilon>0\), the residual bounds alone imply no universal objective-gap bound without an additional stability estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete KKT stopping test checks primal feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity. Zero residual certifies convex optimality; positive residual requires stability information for objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and each \(h_i\) are proper closed convex functions.
KKT sufficiency holds; Slater's condition suffices for the stated multiplier-existence assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\rm p}=r_{\rm d}=r_{\rm c}=0\Rightarrow(x,y,z)\) is a primal-dual optimal KKT point.

notation.meaning: Componentwise positive part of inequality violations.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Residual Stopping Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-safe relative and mixed normalization of the feasible primal-dual gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For primal-feasible \(x\), dual-feasible \(y\), and \(G=P(x)-D(y)\ge0\), set \(s=\max\{1,|P(x)|,|D(y)|\}\). If \(G/s\le\varepsilon_{\rm rel}\), then \[P(x)-p^\star\le G\le\varepsilon_{\rm rel}s,\qquad d^\star-D(y)\le G\le\varepsilon_{\rm rel}s.\] More generally, \(G\le\varepsilon_{\rm abs}+\varepsilon_{\rm rel}s\) gives the corresponding mixed absolute-relative bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-safe objective scale converts a feasible primal-dual gap into relative or mixed stopping bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) and \(y\) are primal and dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Primal-Dual Gap Stopping
Primal-Dual Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality stopping certificate based on exact feasibility and a primal-dual gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal minimization problem with optimal value \(p^\star\) and a dual maximization problem with optimal value \(d^\star\), and assume weak duality. For a primal-feasible \(x_k\) and dual-feasible \(y_k\), define \(G_k=P(x_k)-D(y_k)\). If \(G_k\leq\varepsilon_g\), then \(0\leq P(x_k)-p^\star\leq G_k\leq\varepsilon_g\) and \(0\leq d^\star-D(y_k)\leq G_k\leq\varepsilon_g\). For approximately feasible points, feasibility residuals may be included in a stopping rule, but objective-error conclusions require additional problem-specific bounds relating those residuals to feasible objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exactly feasible primal and dual points, a small duality gap certifies both primal and dual objective accuracy. Approximate feasibility requires additional error bounds before the same conclusion is available.
assumptions_latex: Weak duality holds: \(D(y)\leq P(x)\) for every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\).
\(x_k\) is primal feasible and \(y_k\) is dual feasible.

children.title: Model-Accuracy Stopping
children.top_down_role: Stopping certificates tied to local model fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Accuracy Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping condition corrected by a certified model-to-true residual discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(x_k)\) be the true residual and let \(R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}(x_k)\) be a residual computed from a local model. Suppose \(|R(x_k)-R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}(x_k)|\leq\omega_k\), where \(\omega_k\geq0\). Model-accuracy stopping at tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) uses the condition \(R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}(x_k)+\omega_k\leq\varepsilon\). Whenever it holds, \(R(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\). Under the absolute-error bound alone, the weaker test \(R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\) does not in general imply \(R(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add the certified model discrepancy to the model residual before testing the target tolerance; the uncorrected test is not generally sound under an absolute-error bound alone.

children.title: Inexactness Stopping
children.top_down_role: Stopping certificates tied to controlled computational error.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexactness Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping condition corrected for certified computational or oracle inexactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k^{\mathrm{ex}}\) denote the residual obtained from an exact subproblem or oracle and let \(\widetilde R_k\) be its computed approximation. If \(|\widetilde R_k-R_k^{\mathrm{ex}}|\leq\delta_k\), then inexactness-aware stopping at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) requires \(\widetilde R_k+\delta_k\leq\varepsilon\). This condition certifies \(R_k^{\mathrm{ex}}\leq\varepsilon\). If only \(\widetilde R_k\leq\varepsilon\) is checked, an error cancellation of size up to \(\delta_k\) may produce premature stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed residual must be augmented by its certified numerical or oracle error before it can certify the exact residual tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Error Stopping Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Allocates the stopping tolerance among computed residual, model error, and oracle error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the true residual \(R_k\), model residual \(R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}\), and computed residual \(\widetilde R_k\) satisfy \(|R_k-R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}|\leq\omega_k\) and \(|R_k^{\mathrm{mod}}-\widetilde R_k|\leq\delta_k\). Then \(R_k\leq\widetilde R_k+\omega_k+\delta_k\). Hence any nonnegative budget allocation \(\varepsilon_r+\varepsilon_m+\varepsilon_o\leq\varepsilon\), together with \(\widetilde R_k\leq\varepsilon_r\), \(\omega_k\leq\varepsilon_m\), and \(\delta_k\leq\varepsilon_o\), certifies \(R_k\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the target tolerance among observed residual, model discrepancy, and oracle error; their certified sum bounds the true residual.
assumptions_latex: All residuals, errors, and budget components are nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.title: Small Residual without Solution Proximity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary family showing failure of uniform residual-to-solution error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a>0\), minimize \(f_a(x)=a x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\). The unique solution set is \(S_a=\{0\}\), and the gradient residual is \(R_a(x)=|f_a'(x)|=a|x|\). At \(x_a=1\), \(R_a(x_a)=a\to0\) as \(a\downarrow0\), while \(\operatorname{dist}(x_a,S_a)=1\). Therefore no constant \(\kappa\) independent of \(a\) can satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S_a)\leq\kappa R_a(x)\) throughout this family; small uncalibrated residual does not imply solution proximity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing curvature makes the gradient residual arbitrarily small at a point that remains distance one from the unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The residual is the absolute gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_a(1)\to0\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(1,S_a)=1\), so no family-uniform residual error bound exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Residual Along an Escaping Sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed smooth optimization problem whose gradient residual vanishes along points diverging from its unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\log(1+x^2)\) on \(\mathbb R\). Its unique global minimizer is \(0\), and \(R(x)=|f'(x)|=2|x|/(1+x^2)\). For \(x_k=k\), \[R(x_k)=\frac{2k}{1+k^2}\to0,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x_k,\{0\})=k\to\infty.\] Thus vanishing gradient residual need not imply solution proximity without localization or a residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed smooth coercive objective has points escaping to infinity whose gradients vanish despite a unique minimizer at zero.

False Convergence under Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cancellation by oracle error produces a zero reported residual away from stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), whose unique stationary point is \(0\). At every iteration set \(x_k=1\), and let an inexact gradient oracle return \(\widetilde g_k=f'(x_k)+e_k\) with \(e_k=-1\). Then the reported residual \(\widetilde R_k=|\widetilde g_k|\) equals \(0\), although the exact residual is \(R_k=|f'(x_k)|=1\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,\{0\})=1\). Thus unaccounted persistent inexactness can cause a stopping test to declare false convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent oracle error can exactly cancel the true gradient, reporting zero residual at iterates that stay away from the solution.
assumptions_latex: The stopping test uses only \(\widetilde R_k=|\widetilde g_k|\).
The oracle error is not included in the stopping tolerance.

children.title: Cross-Parameter Residual Incomparability
children.top_down_role: Residual ranking failures caused by changes in algorithmic parameters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter comparison for normalized proximal residuals of one maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be maximal monotone on a Hilbert space and set \(A_\gamma x=\gamma^{-1}(x-J_{\gamma A}x)\). For \(0<\gamma\le\mu\), \[\|A_\mu x\|\le\|A_\gamma x\|\le\frac{\mu}{\gamma}\|A_\mu x\|.\] Thus a parameter interval \([\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma]\subset(0,\infty)\) gives a uniform comparison factor at most \(\overline\gamma/\underline\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized proximal residuals are uniformly comparable on parameter ranges having a bounded ratio; the factor can diverge on unrestricted ranges.

notation.meaning: Yosida approximation and normalized proximal residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Yosida Residual Comparison Across Parameters
Cross-Parameter Residual Incomparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Raw proximal residual magnitudes are not uniformly comparable across parameter choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing \(g(x)=|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\), define the parameterized proximal residual \(R_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x)|\) for \(\gamma>0\). At \(x=1\), soft thresholding gives \(R_\gamma(1)=1\) when \(0<\gamma\leq1\) and \(R_\gamma(1)=1/\gamma\) when \(\gamma>1\). Hence \(R_1(1)/R_\gamma(1)=\gamma\to\infty\). No parameter-independent two-sided comparison constant exists over all positive parameters, so stopping thresholds cannot be transferred across \(\gamma\) without calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an absolute-value objective, changing the proximal parameter changes the same point's residual by an arbitrarily large factor, defeating uniform threshold transfer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is no finite \(C\) independent of \(\gamma\) such that \(C^{-1}R_1(1)\leq R_\gamma(1)\leq C R_1(1)\) for every \(\gamma>0\).

children.title: Cross-Metric Residual Incomparability
children.top_down_role: Residual ranking failures caused by changes in measurement geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Metric Residual Incomparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that unrestricted positive-definite metrics admit no uniform residual-equivalence constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\equiv 0\), let \(g=\delta_{\{0\}}\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), and fix the proximal parameter \(\lambda=1\). For every symmetric positive-definite matrix \(Q\), the metric proximal point is \(\operatorname{prox}^{Q}_{g}(x)=0\), so the associated residual is \(R_Q(x)=\|x\|_Q\). For \(t>1\), set \(Q_t=\operatorname{diag}(t^2,t^{-2})\). Then
\[
\frac{R_{Q_t}(e_1)}{R_I(e_1)}=t,
\qquad
\frac{R_{Q_t}(e_2)}{R_I(e_2)}=t^{-1}.
\]
Consequently, no constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), independent of \(Q\), satisfy \(cR_I(x)\le R_Q(x)\le CR_I(x)\) for every positive-definite \(Q\) and every \(x\in\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric proximal residuals are not uniformly comparable when metric eigenvalues are unrestricted; one coordinate ratio diverges while another vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) ranges over all symmetric positive-definite matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\,0<c\le C<\infty\) uniform in \(Q\) such that \(cR_I(x)\le R_Q(x)\le CR_I(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product calibration when parameter normalization and quadratic geometry vary jointly while the residual vector remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\lambda_0>0\), \(Q_0\succ0\), and \(F\), and define \(R_{\lambda,Q}(x)=\lambda^{-1}\|F(x)\|_Q\). If \(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda\le\overline\lambda<\infty\) and \(mQ_0\preceq Q\preceq MQ_0\), then \[\frac{\lambda_0\sqrt m}{\overline\lambda}R_{\lambda_0,Q_0}(x)\le R_{\lambda,Q}(x)\le\frac{\lambda_0\sqrt M}{\underline\lambda}R_{\lambda_0,Q_0}(x).\] If the residual vector also depends on \((\lambda,Q)\), these bounds require an additional comparison for that dependence.

Joint Parameter-Metric Calibration Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies failure of uniform calibration when both proximal parameter and metric scaling are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\equiv0\), let \(g=\delta_{\{0\}}\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), and define \(R_{\lambda,Q}(x)=\lambda^{-1}\|x-\operatorname{prox}^{Q}_{\lambda g}(x)\|_Q=\lambda^{-1}\|x\|_Q\). Use \(R_{1,I}\) as the reference residual. For \(t>1\), take \((\lambda_t,Q_t)=(t,t^4I)\) and \((\widetilde\lambda_t,\widetilde Q_t)=(t,t^{-2}I)\). Every nonzero \(x\) then satisfies
\[
\frac{R_{\lambda_t,Q_t}(x)}{R_{1,I}(x)}=t,
\qquad
\frac{R_{\widetilde\lambda_t,\widetilde Q_t}(x)}{R_{1,I}(x)}=t^{-2}.
\]
Thus unrestricted joint variation of parameter and metric destroys every uniform two-sided calibration against the reference residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly varying the proximal parameter and metric can make the calibrated residual arbitrarily larger or smaller than a fixed reference residual.
assumptions_latex: Neither \(\lambda\) nor the eigenvalues of \(Q\) have uniform bounds.
